proofs.doc: The fused zero −1 absorbs under the fused product (it is the wall).

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.shift_ring_hom
proofs.doc: The shift is a ring isomorphism (R, fadd, ⊞) ≅ (R, +, ·): it carries both operations.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.multAdd_not_distrib_add
proofs.doc: Plain addition and mult-add do not form a ring: ⊞ does not distribute over +.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.mpow_multAdd
proofs.doc: (a ⊞ b)^⊞n = a^⊞n ⊞ b^⊞n: each power map is an endomorphism of mult-add.
proofs.statement: mpow (multAdd a b) n = multAdd (mpow a n) (mpow b n)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.mpow_mul
proofs.doc: (a^⊞m)^⊞n = a^⊞(m·n): composing power maps multiplies the exponents.
proofs.statement: mpow (mpow a m) n = mpow a (m * n)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateRel_refl
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tate_glue
proofs.doc: The glued point: q − 1 sits with 0, i.e. multiplying the lift by q changes nothing. (Stated as 1 + 0 multiplied by q equals 1 + a whenever 1 + a = q.)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateRel_multAdd
proofs.doc: Mult-add respects the gluing on each side.
proofs.statement: tateRel q (multAdd a b) (multAdd a' b')

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_commMonoid
proofs.doc: The Tate quotient is a commutative monoid under mult-add.
proofs.statement: CommMonoidLaws (TateQ.op q) (TateQ.zero q) where comm x y

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_glued
proofs.doc: In the quotient the class of q − 1 is the identity.
proofs.statement: (Quotient.mk (tateSetoid q) a : TateQ q) = TateQ.zero q
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_inverse
proofs.doc: On a field, every class off the wall has an inverse in the Tate quotient.
proofs.statement: TateQ.op q (Quotient.mk (tateSetoid q) a) (Quotient.mk (tateSetoid q) (multAddInv a)) = TateQ.zero q

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.slope_walls_mod5
proofs.doc: Walls of slope addition (a + b)/(1 − ab) are the roots of 1 + a². Mod 5 and 13 there are two (two-walled country, a split torus with p − 1 points); mod 3, 7, 11 none (turning country, a non-split torus with p + 1 points). Split exactly at p ≡ 1 mod 4.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.multAdd_one_wall_mod7
proofs.doc: Mult-add mod p always has exactly one finite wall, −1 (the other wall is at infinity).

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.three_twists
proofs.doc: **The three twists sum to the standard spin-orbit coefficient** m₂(4m₁ + 3m₂)/(2M).
proofs.statement: m₂ * twistSum m₁ m₂ = m₂ * (4 * m₁ + 3 * m₂) / (2 * (m₁ + m₂))

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.three_twists_poly
proofs.doc: Polynomial form (no division): 2M · (½m₂ + m₂ + 2m₁) = 4m₁ + 3m₂ times M/M.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.test_limit
proofs.doc: **Test-gyroscope limit** m₁ = 0: the coefficient is (3/2)·m₂, the Gravity Probe B law.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.drag_vanishes
proofs.doc: In that limit the drag twist vanishes: a light partner barely moves the heavy companion.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.velocity_space_ratio
proofs.doc: Velocity and space twists keep their one-to-two ratio, as in Gravity Probe B.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.double_pulsar_within_error
proofs.doc: Twist bookkeeping gives 5.07; measured 4.77 with +0.66 / −0.65. Within one sigma.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.parts_add
proofs.doc: The three parts: velocity 0.75, space 1.51, drag 2.81, which add to 5.07.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.drag_needed
proofs.doc: **Without the companion's drag** the prediction is 2.26, more than 3σ below 4.77.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.velocity_not_isolated
proofs.doc: Without the velocity twist the prediction is 4.32, still within one sigma: not isolated.

proofs.name: BinaryPulsar.corner_tiny
proofs.doc: The ✳ corner is the product of two first-order twists, each of size about M/r ≈ 4.35e-6, so it is below 1e-10 of a turn, far under the measurement's 14% error.

proofs.name: Behaviour.rw_step
proofs.doc: One Rescorla–Wagner step in units of λ: V ↦ V + a(1 − V) is V ✳₋₁ a.
proofs.statement: V + a * (1 - V) = wAdd (-1) V a

proofs.name: Behaviour.rw_phases
proofs.doc: Two training phases compose by the "or" law.
proofs.statement: wpow (-1) a (m + n) = wAdd (-1) (wpow (-1) a m) (wpow (-1) a n)

proofs.name: Behaviour.hyperbolic_split
proofs.doc: Hyperbolic interest k·D adds over split delays: dial 0.

proofs.name: Behaviour.subadditive
proofs.doc: **Subadditivity.** Discounting a hyperbolic delay in two pieces raises 1/d by k²D₁D₂.
proofs.statement: (1 + k * D₁) * (1 + k * D₂) - (1 + k * (D₁ + D₂)) = k * k * D₁ * D₂

proofs.name: Behaviour.dial_split
proofs.doc: **Dial-stationary discounting.** If 1 + κu multiplies over split delays, u composes by ✳_κ.
proofs.statement: 1 + κ * wAdd κ u₁ u₂ = (1 + κ * u₁) * (1 + κ * u₂)

proofs.name: Behaviour.dial_steps
proofs.doc: An integer-step version: n equal pieces of interest u compose to wpow(κ, u, n).
proofs.statement: 1 + κ * wpow κ u n = (1 + κ * u) ^ n

proofs.name: Behaviour.hyperbolic_factor
proofs.doc: The hyperbolic discount factor is minus the mult-add inverse of the interest.

proofs.name: Behaviour.herrnstein
proofs.doc: Herrnstein's hyperbola r/(r + rₑ) is −inv(r/rₑ).

proofs.name: CellBiology.bliss_or
proofs.doc: Survivals multiply, so effects combine by the "or" law, dial −1.

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_is_wAdd
proofs.statement: ci α v₁ v₂ = wAdd α v₁ v₂

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_loewe
proofs.doc: α = 0: Loewe dose additivity.

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_hsa
proofs.doc: α = −1: the index sits on the additivity line exactly when one factor 1 − vᵢ vanishes, i.e. one drug alone already gives the effect. This is the Highest Single Agent model.

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_nonexclusive
proofs.doc: α = 1: Chou's "mutually nonexclusive" index factors as (1 + v₁)(1 + v₂) − 1.

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_shift
proofs.doc: Moving one drug moves the index by the dial lift of the other.
proofs.statement: ci α v₁ v₂ - ci α v₁ v₂' = (v₂ - v₂') * (1 + α * v₁)

proofs.name: CellBiology.bliss_odds
proofs.doc: **Bliss is plain mult-add on effect odds**, for any shape of dose–response curve.
proofs.statement: odds (1 - (1 - a) * (1 - b)) = odds a ✳ odds b

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_hsa_field
proofs.doc: The Highest Single Agent reading of α = −1, over a field: on the additivity line one of the two drugs is at its own iso-effective dose.

proofs.name: CellBiology.ci_wall
proofs.doc: **The wall makes one drug irrelevant.** At v₂ = −1/α the index is −1/α whatever v₁ is. For α = −1 the wall is v₂ = 1: drug 2 alone already gives the effect.

proofs.name: CellBiology.loewe_slope_one
proofs.doc: Loewe with Hill slope 1: vᵢ = uᵢ/o, so v₁ + v₂ = 1 exactly when the effect odds o are u₁ + u₂, odds adding, dial 0.
proofs.statement: u₁ / o + u₂ / o = 1 ↔ o = u₁ + u₂

proofs.name: Development.gompertz_steps
proofs.doc: **Gompertz steps.** n steps of x ↦ mpow(x, λ) give the single power λⁿ.
proofs.statement: 1 + iter l n x = (1 + x) ^ (l ^ n)

proofs.name: Development.bertalanffy
proofs.doc: Von Bertalanffy growth (power 3): size/asymptote = (1 + x)³ = 1 + mpow(x, 3).

proofs.name: Development.allometry
proofs.doc: Allometry: if x grows by the factor 1 + g, then y ∝ xᵃ grows by 1 + mpow(g, a).
proofs.statement: b * ((1 + g) * x) ^ a = (1 + mpow g a) * (b * x ^ a)

proofs.name: Development.logistic_shortfall
proofs.doc: The logistic shortfall below the asymptote is −inv(x) = x/(1 + x).

proofs.name: Ecology.budget_states
proofs.doc: The four states' weights (search 1, handling x, interfering from search y, interfering from handling k·x·y) sum to the budget.
proofs.statement: 1 + x + y + k * x * y = budget k x y

proofs.name: Ecology.bd
proofs.doc: Beddington–DeAngelis is dial 0.

proofs.name: Ecology.cm
proofs.doc: Crowley–Martin is dial 1, the product of the two saturations.

proofs.name: Ecology.corner
proofs.doc: The dial's excess over BD is exactly the handling–interference corner k·x·y.
proofs.statement: budget k x y - budget 0 x y = k * x * y

proofs.name: Ecology.search_share
proofs.doc: Balance of the predator chain: if the handling share is x times the search share and the other two states are y and k·x·y times it, and the four shares sum to 1, the search share is 1/(1 + x ✳ₖ y).

proofs.name: Ecology.tsallis_two
proofs.doc: q = 2 diversity: ln₂(D) = 1 − 1/D. Hill numbers multiply, so these combine by dial −1.

proofs.name: Ecology.tsallis_wall
proofs.doc: For q = 2 the wall −1/k is 1: an entropy at the ceiling absorbs any other community.

proofs.name: Evolution.generations_add
proofs.doc: Stages split anywhere: t₁ + t₂ generations are t₁ then t₂.
proofs.statement: mpow s (t₁ + t₂) = mpow s t₁ ✳ mpow s t₂

proofs.name: Evolution.mult_null
proofs.doc: The multiplicative null is dial 1.

proofs.name: Evolution.epistasis
proofs.doc: Epistasis against the multiplicative null is (k − 1)·ab.
proofs.statement: wAdd k a b - (a ✳ b) = (k - 1) * a * b

proofs.name: Evolution.order_gap
proofs.doc: Two orders of adding mutations i and j differ by exactly c_j a_i − c_i a_j.
proofs.statement: addMut aⱼ cⱼ (addMut aᵢ cᵢ x) - addMut aᵢ cᵢ (addMut aⱼ cⱼ x) = cⱼ * aᵢ - cᵢ * aⱼ

proofs.name: Evolution.path_consistent_iff
proofs.doc: **Path consistency.** The two orders agree iff c_j a_i = c_i a_j.
proofs.statement: addMut aⱼ cⱼ (addMut aᵢ cᵢ x) = addMut aᵢ cᵢ (addMut aⱼ cⱼ x) ↔ cⱼ * aᵢ = cᵢ * aⱼ

proofs.name: Evolution.add_is_dial
proofs.doc: With slopes proportional to effects, c = k·a, adding a mutation is the dial.
proofs.statement: addMut a (k * a) x = wAdd k x a

proofs.name: Evolution.proportional_consistent
proofs.doc: Proportional slopes are always path-consistent.
proofs.statement: addMut aⱼ (k * aⱼ) (addMut aᵢ (k * aᵢ) x) = addMut aᵢ (k * aᵢ) (addMut aⱼ (k * aⱼ) x)

proofs.name: Evolution.common_slope_gap
proofs.doc: A common slope c for two mutations is consistent only if c·(aᵢ − aⱼ) = 0.
proofs.statement: addMut aⱼ c (addMut aᵢ c x) - addMut aᵢ c (addMut aⱼ c x) = c * (aᵢ - aⱼ)

proofs.name: Evolution.three_mutations
proofs.doc: The dial is associative, so three mutations reach one fitness in any grouping.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (wAdd k x a) b = wAdd k x (wAdd k a b)

proofs.name: Evolution.from_the_wall
proofs.doc: In the shifted coordinate 1 + k·x (fitness measured from the wall) mutations multiply.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wAdd k x a = (1 + k * x) * (1 + k * a)

proofs.name: Evolution.wall_neutral
proofs.doc: At the wall every mutation is neutral: Δ(x) = a(1 + kx) vanishes when 1 + kx = 0.

proofs.name: Evolution.additive_dominance
proofs.doc: Additive dominance (h = ½ written as two equal copies a) is dial 0.

proofs.name: Evolution.consistent_forces_dial
proofs.doc: **Path consistency forces one dial.** If mutation i has a nonzero effect and every mutation j is path-consistent with it, then c_j = k·a_j with the single k = c_i/a_i.

proofs.name: Evolution.wall_at
proofs.doc: The wall: for k ≠ 0, the background x = −1/k makes every mutation neutral.

proofs.name: Genetics.haldane
proofs.doc: No interference: r₁₂ = r₁ + r₂ − 2r₁r₂, the dial at k = −2.
proofs.statement: r₁ + r₂ - 2 * r₁ * r₂ = wAdd (-2) r₁ r₂

proofs.name: Genetics.haldane_lift
proofs.doc: The lift of dial −2 is 1 − 2r, so 1 − 2r multiplies along the chromosome.

proofs.name: Genetics.haldane_star
proofs.doc: In the coordinate u = −2r Haldane is plain mult-add.

proofs.name: Genetics.haldane_three
proofs.doc: Three intervals: the lift is a product of three factors.

proofs.name: Genetics.interference
proofs.doc: With double-recombinant frequency d₁₂ = c·r₁·r₂, the outer recombination fraction is the dial at k = −2c.
proofs.statement: r₁ + r₂ - 2 * (c * r₁ * r₂) = wAdd (-2 * c) r₁ r₂

proofs.name: Genetics.complete_interference
proofs.doc: Complete interference (c = 0) is plain addition of map lengths.

proofs.name: Genetics.reri
proofs.doc: The interaction contrast (RERI) is the dial times the two excess risks.
proofs.statement: wAdd k e₁ e₂ - e₁ - e₂ = k * (e₁ * e₂)

proofs.name: Genetics.risk_additive
proofs.doc: k = 0: excess risks add.

proofs.name: Genetics.haldane_unlinked
proofs.doc: **The wall is "unlinked".** An interval at r = 1/2 makes the combined pair unlinked, whatever the other interval is.

proofs.name: Genetics.lens_unlinked
proofs.doc: **Unlinked absorbs exactly on the line 2k + q = −4.**

proofs.name: Genetics.lens_haldane
proofs.doc: Haldane is the lens law at (−2, 0).
proofs.statement: lens (-2) 0 a b = wAdd (-2) a b

proofs.name: Genetics.lens_kosambi
proofs.doc: Kosambi's addition rule is the lens law at (0, −4).

proofs.name: Genetics.kosambi_lift
proofs.doc: **Kosambi is plain ✳ after a change of variable.** With R = 2r and R₁₂ = (R₁ + R₂)/(1 + R₁R₂), the quantity 1 + w = (1 + R)/(1 − R) multiplies.

proofs.name: Metabolism.wAdd_comm'
proofs.statement: wAdd k a b = wAdd k b a

proofs.name: Metabolism.bisub_is_wAdd
proofs.statement: bisub k uA uB = 1 + wAdd k uA uB

proofs.name: Metabolism.pingpong
proofs.doc: Ping-pong (substituted enzyme): no product term, dial 0. Double-reciprocal lines are parallel.

proofs.name: Metabolism.random_independent
proofs.doc: Random order with independent sites: dial 1, the rate law factors.

proofs.name: Metabolism.bisub_line
proofs.doc: Read as a line in u_A (a double-reciprocal plot at fixed B): intercept 1 + u_B, slope 1 + k·u_B.
proofs.statement: bisub k uA uB = (1 + uB) + uA * (1 + k * uB)

proofs.name: Metabolism.bisub_shift
proofs.doc: Changing B moves V/v by (u_B − u_B')·(1 + k·u_A); the factor is the dial lift.
proofs.statement: bisub k uA uB - bisub k uA uB' = (uB - uB') * (1 + k * uA)

proofs.name: Metabolism.monod_additive
proofs.doc: Additive resistance: 1/μ = 1/θ₁ + 1/θ₂ − 1 = 1 + u₁ + u₂, dial 0.

proofs.name: Metabolism.limitation_or
proofs.doc: The shortfall from full growth, 1 − θ₁θ₂, is the "or" of the two shortfalls.

proofs.name: Metabolism.limitation_or_three
proofs.statement: 1 - θ₁ * θ₂ * θ₃ = wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) (1 - θ₁) (1 - θ₂)) (1 - θ₃)

proofs.name: Metabolism.limitation_pow
proofs.doc: n identical limiting steps: the joint shortfall is a weighted power at dial −1.

proofs.name: Metabolism.ordered_is_dial
proofs.doc: **The ordered mechanism is a weighted mult-add.** With u_A = K_a/A, u_B = K_b/B and k = K_ia/K_a, the textbook rate law V/v = 1 + K_a/A + K_b/B + K_ia·K_b/(A·B) equals 1 + (u_A ✳_k u_B).
proofs.statement: 1 + Ka / A + Kb / B + Kia * Kb / (A * B) = 1 + wAdd (Kia / Ka) (Ka / A) (Kb / B)

proofs.name: Metabolism.lines_meet_at_wall
proofs.doc: **The lines meet at the wall.** At u_A = −1/k the rate no longer depends on B: every double-reciprocal line passes through the point (−1/k, 1 − 1/k).

proofs.name: Metabolism.meeting_point_unique
proofs.doc: Only the wall does this: if two different B give the same rate at u_A, then 1 + k·u_A = 0.

proofs.name: Metabolism.saturation
proofs.doc: Saturation is the mult-add inverse lifted: 1/(1 + u) = 1 + inv(u).

proofs.name: Metabolism.michaelis_menten
proofs.doc: Michaelis–Menten: S/(K + S) = 1 + inv(K/S).

proofs.name: Metabolism.free_fraction
proofs.doc: The free (unbound) fraction is minus the inverse: u/(1 + u) = −inv(u).

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.star_def
proofs.statement: a ✳ b = a + b + a * b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.swap_mul
proofs.statement: swap (mul x y) = mul (swap x) (swap y)

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.swap_pow
proofs.statement: swap (pow x n) = pow (swap x) n

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_ring_relabel
proofs.doc: Relabelling the states does not change any ring's partition function.
proofs.statement: tr (pow (swap (zb σ s)) n) = tr (pow (zb σ s) n)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_is_dial_gas
proofs.doc: **Helix–coil = dial gas.** If k·σ = 1, the relabelled Zimm–Bragg matrix is the Lee–Yang ring matrix with dial k and fugacity σ·s.
proofs.statement: swap (zb σ s) = ringT k (σ * s)

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_ring_eq_dial_ring
proofs.doc: So the helix–coil ring has the same partition function as the dial-gas ring.
proofs.statement: tr (pow (zb σ s) n) = tr (pow (ringT k (σ * s)) n)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_tr
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_odd_ring_wall
proofs.doc: **Wall theorem for helix–coil.** At s = −1 every odd ring vanishes, for every σ.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.zb_free
proofs.doc: σ = 1 (no nucleation penalty): the matrix has determinant 0, so the chain is a free gas whose ring partition function is (1 + s)ⁿ.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_is_wAdd
proofs.statement: bind2 ω a b = 1 + wAdd ω a b

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_independent
proofs.doc: Independent sites (ω = 1): the polynomial factors, plain mult-add.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_exclusive
proofs.doc: Exclusive sites (ω = 0): only one can be filled, plain addition.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_excess
proofs.doc: The deviation from independence is exactly (ω − 1) times the corner cell.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_half
proofs.doc: Half saturation for identical sites: the bound fraction (x + ωx²)/(1 + 2x + ωx²) is 1/2 exactly when ω·x² = 1. Stated without division.
proofs.statement: 2 * (x + ω * x * x) - bind2 ω x x = ω * x * x - 1

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.mwc_R
proofs.doc: R state: the plain mult-add power, lifted.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.mwc_T
proofs.doc: T state: the weighted power at dial c, lifted.
proofs.statement: (1 + c * a) ^ n = 1 + c * wpow c a n

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.mwc_poly
proofs.doc: The MWC binding polynomial (1 + a)ⁿ + L(1 + c·a)ⁿ written as two mult-add powers.
proofs.statement: (1 + a) ^ n + L * (1 + c * a) ^ n = (1 + mpow a n) + L * (1 + c * wpow c a n)

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.mwc_c_one
proofs.doc: With c = 1 both states bind alike and MWC collapses to independent sites.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.catch_two
proofs.doc: A mistake survives two checks only if both miss: catches combine by the "or" law.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.catch_three
proofs.statement: 1 - wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) c₁ c₂) c₃ = (1 - c₁) * (1 - c₂) * (1 - c₃)

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.copy_loss
proofs.doc: Copying a genome of L bases with error μ per base keeps the master with chance (1 − μ)^L = 1 + mpow(−μ, L): the copy loss is a mult-add power.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.eigen_excess
proofs.doc: Eigen: the master's growth factor σ·(1 + l) minus 1 is the mult-add of the advantage s = σ − 1 and the copy loss l.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.eigen_threshold
proofs.doc: **Eigen's error threshold is the mult-add inverse.** Away from the wall (1 + l ≠ 0), the master just holds its own (s ✳ l = 0) exactly when s is the mult-add inverse of l.

proofs.name: MolecularBiology.bind2_wall
proofs.doc: A site sitting at the wall −1/ω makes the binding polynomial forget the other site.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.soma_line
proofs.doc: In the soma-line case B = 1 the two constants sum to −1.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.twoport
proofs.doc: **The two-port theorem, cleared form.** Currents I₁ (synapse i alone), J₂ (synapse j alone) and I, J (both on) solve the network equations of a passive linear network with transfer impedances Z. Then the soma voltage V = Z_si I + Z_sj J obeys the lens law with the constants above, multiplied through by E_i E_j.
proofs.statement: (Zsi * I + Zsj * J) * (Ei * Ej - Zij ^ 2 * I1 * J2) = Ei * Ej * (Zsi * I1 + Zsj * J2) - Zij * (Ei * Zsj + Ej * Zsi) * I1 * J2

proofs.name: NeuroScience.clear_num
proofs.doc: Bookkeeping for the divided two-port theorem: clearing the lens numerator.
proofs.statement: (P + Q + -(x + y) * P * Q) * EE = EE * (P + Q) - (r₁ + r₂)

proofs.name: NeuroScience.clear_den
proofs.doc: Bookkeeping for the divided two-port theorem: clearing the lens denominator.
proofs.statement: (1 - z * P * Q) * EE = EE - r

proofs.name: NeuroScience.div_mul_cancel'
proofs.doc: x / y · y = x for y ≠ 0.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.lens_dial
proofs.doc: With q = 0 the lens law is the dial: Hao et al.'s bilinear rule.
proofs.statement: lens k 0 a b = wAdd k a b

proofs.name: NeuroScience.one_compartment
proofs.doc: **One compartment.** Two synapses sum by the lens law with k = −2, q = 1.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.odds_vss
proofs.doc: In odds v/(1 − v) the conductance comes back: inputs add, dial 0.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.reversal_absorbs
proofs.doc: **Reversal absorbs.** A synapse holding the compartment at its reversal potential makes every other input irrelevant: v = 1 is the lens law's wall.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.factor_A
proofs.doc: **Factorisation.** With k = −(A + B), q = AB: 1 − A·V = (1 − Aa)(1 − Ab)/(1 − ABab).

proofs.name: NeuroScience.factor_B
proofs.doc: The same factorisation with A and B exchanged.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.T_mul
proofs.doc: **Summation becomes multiplication.** In T(v) = (1 − Av)/(1 − Bv) the lens law is a product.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.soma_reversal_absorbs
proofs.doc: **Reversal at the soma absorbs, on any tree.** On the soma line (B = 1, reversal units) an input clamping the soma to its reversal fixes the response at 1.

proofs.name: NeuroScience.twoport_lens
proofs.doc: **The two-port theorem, divided form.** With nonzero reversals and transfer impedances, the soma voltage is exactly the lens law with the geometric constants k and q.
proofs.statement: Zsi * I + Zsj * J = lens (-(Zij / (Ej * Zsi) + Zij / (Ei * Zsj))) (Zij ^ 2 / (Ei * Ej * Zsi * Zsj)) (Zsi * I1) (Zsj * J2)

proofs.name: Physiology.hill_level_set
proofs.doc: In reduced variables Hill's hyperbola (1 + X)(1 + Y) = 1 + X₀ is X ✳ Y = X₀.

proofs.name: Physiology.dose_ratio
proofs.doc: The dose ratio is that partition function; DR − 1 is the weighted mult-add.
proofs.statement: antag ω b₁ b₂ - 1 = wAdd ω b₁ b₂

proofs.name: Physiology.same_site
proofs.doc: Same site: dose ratios add (Paton–Rang additivity).

proofs.name: Physiology.separate_sites
proofs.doc: Independent sites: dose ratios multiply.
proofs.statement: antag 1 b₁ b₂ = antag 1 b₁ 0 * antag 1 0 b₂

proofs.name: Physiology.series_gain
proofs.doc: Splitting clearance across two organs in series beats pooling it in one: (1 + u₁)(1 + u₂) exceeds 1 + u₁ + u₂ by exactly u₁u₂, the corner cell.

proofs.name: Physiology.hill_velocity
proofs.doc: **Velocity is a mult-add difference.** On Hill's curve Y = X₀ ✳ inv(X).

proofs.name: Population.interventions
proofs.doc: Two interventions: transmission kept is (1 − e₁)(1 − e₂) = 1 − (e₁ "or" e₂).

proofs.name: Population.hassell_one
proofs.doc: Hassell with b = 1 is Beverton–Holt's 1 + aN.

proofs.name: Population.survival_assoc
proofs.doc: Three age classes, grouped either way.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) q₁ q₂) q₃ = wAdd (-1) q₁ (wAdd (-1) q₂ q₃)

proofs.name: Population.bh_compose
proofs.doc: **Two seasons are one season.** BH(R₂, m₂) ∘ BH(R₁, m₁) = BH(R₁R₂, m₁ + R₁m₂).
proofs.statement: bh R₂ m₂ (bh R₁ m₁ x) = bh (R₁ * R₂) (m₁ + R₁ * m₂) x

proofs.name: Population.bh_room
proofs.doc: **Room shrinks by 1/R.** With K = (R − 1)/m, the room K/N − 1 after one step is (K/N − 1)/R.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_lift
proofs.doc: Under the lift the mult-add integral is a product integral.
proofs.statement: 1 + mint d n = liftProd d n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_step
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem, part 1: the last step of the integral is the integrand.
proofs.statement: mint d (n + 1) = multAdd (mint d n) (d n)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem, part 2: a path whose mult-add steps are d ends at its start ⊞ the integral of d.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_box
proofs.doc: The same in box form: the end box is the start box times every step.
proofs.statement: 1 + f n = (1 + f 0) * liftProd d n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_const
proofs.doc: Straight lines are exponentials: constant mult-add slope a gives a^(⊞n).
proofs.statement: mint (fun _ => a) n = mpow a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_add
proofs.doc: The integral over two intervals joins by mult-add.
proofs.statement: mint d (a + b) = multAdd (mint d a) (mint (fun j => d (a + j)) b)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.product_rule_step
proofs.doc: Product rule = sum rule: if f steps by d and g steps by e, then f ⊞ g steps by d ⊞ e.
proofs.statement: multAdd (f (k + 1)) (g (k + 1)) = multAdd (multAdd (f k) (g k)) (multAdd (d k) (e k))

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_multAdd
proofs.doc: The integral of d ⊞ e is the integral of d ⊞ the integral of e.
proofs.statement: mint (fun k => multAdd (d k) (e k)) n = multAdd (mint d n) (mint e n)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mpow_mul
proofs.doc: Chain rule for blocks: n blocks of m equal steps is a power of a power.
proofs.statement: mpow a (m * n) = mpow (mpow a m) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.rate_product
proofs.doc: If F grows by the factor (1 + h·p) over a step of size h and G by (1 + h·q), then F·G grows by (1 + h·(p ⊞ₕ q)): relative rates combine by weighted mult-add with weight h. This is time-scale ⊕.
proofs.statement: F' * G' = (F * G) * (1 + h * wAdd h p q)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.rate_product_limit
proofs.doc: Weight 0 (step size 0) is ordinary calculus: rates just add.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_exp
proofs.doc: The time-scale exponential after n steps: 1 + h·p^(⊞ₕn) = (1 + h·p)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: 1 + h * wpow h p n = (1 + h * p) ^ n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_exp_mul
proofs.doc: e_p · e_q = e_(p ⊞ₕ q): the exponential turns weighted mult-add into ×.
proofs.statement: (1 + h * wpow h p n) * (1 + h * wpow h q n) = 1 + h * wpow h (wAdd h p q) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.step_iff
proofs.doc: Ordinary slope = height × mult-add slope (the log-derivative rule f' = (1 + f)·r).
proofs.statement: f (k + 1) = multAdd (f k) (d k) ↔ diff f k = (1 + f k) * d k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.leibniz_corner
proofs.doc: Leibniz's rule with the corner kept: the box f·g grows by two strips and one corner square.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => f j * g j) k = diff f k * g k + f k * diff g k + diff f k * diff g k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.diff_multAdd
proofs.doc: The ordinary difference of f ⊞ g: two lifted strips and the corner.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => multAdd (f j) (g j)) k = diff f k * (1 + g k) + (1 + f k) * diff g k + diff f k * diff g k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.diff_pow
proofs.doc: An exponential's slope is a times itself, exactly.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => (1 + a) ^ j) n = a * (1 + a) ^ n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_add
proofs.doc: The additive fundamental theorem: differences telescope.
proofs.statement: sumTo (diff f) n = f n - f 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.jackson_gap
proofs.doc: Stepping the input by mult-add moves it by h·(1 + x): the gap of Jackson's q-derivative with q = 1 + h, read in lifted coordinates.
proofs.statement: multAdd x h - x = h * (1 + x)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mslope_step
proofs.doc: Away from the wall, the mult-add slope is the step: f(k) ⊞ slope = f(k+1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_mslope
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem with slopes read off: f(n) = f(0) ⊞ ∫ mslope f.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_inverse
proofs.doc: Time-scale inverse ⊖p = −p/(1 + h·p): exists exactly off the wall.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.dif_shift
proofs.doc: Shifting the input commutes with differencing.
proofs.statement: dif k (fun i => f (i + 1)) j = dif k f (j + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.dif_one
proofs.doc: Each difference at 1 is the difference at 0 plus the next difference.
proofs.statement: dif k f 1 = dif k f 0 + dif (k + 1) f 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.isum_add
proofs.statement: isum (fun k => g k + h k) m = isum g m + isum h m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.isum_congr
proofs.statement: isum g m = isum h m
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.pascal_sum
proofs.doc: Pascal inside a weighted sum: the (n+1)-cube's layers split into two n-cubes.
proofs.statement: isum (fun k => (Cube.layer (n + 1) k : Int) * x k) (m + 1) = isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * x k) (m + 1) + isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * x (k + 1)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.newton
proofs.doc: Newton's forward formula: f(n) = Σ_{k ≤ n} layer(n,k) · Δᵏf(0).
proofs.statement: f n = isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * dif k f 0) (n + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.cubes_example
proofs.doc: A worked check: the cubes 0, 1, 8, 27, … have third difference 6 and fourth difference 0, so Newton rebuilds n³ from the numbers 0, 1, 6, 6.
proofs.statement: dif 3 (fun j => (j : Int) ^ 3) 0 = 6 ∧ dif 4 (fun j => (j : Int) ^ 3) 0 = 0

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.wedge_smash
proofs.doc: Pointed sets: the product of A₊ and B₊ has (a+1)(b+1) points; take away the base point and what is left is the wedge (a + b) plus the smash (ab).

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.fm_fst_this
proofs.statement: xs.filterMap (fst ∘ (this : α → These α β)) = xs

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.fm_snd_that
proofs.statement: ys.filterMap (snd ∘ (that : β → These α β)) = ys

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.align_fst
proofs.doc: **Nothing lost**: the left list comes back out of the alignment.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.align_snd
proofs.doc: And so does the right list.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.align_zip
proofs.doc: The ordinary zip is the corner cell of the alignment (the ab term).

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.ev_padd
proofs.statement: ev t (padd xs ys) = ev t xs + ev t ys

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.ev_smul
proofs.statement: ev t (ys.map (c * ·)) = c * ev t ys

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.ev_pmul
proofs.doc: Counting cells is multiplicative: P(X × Y) = P(X)·P(Y) at every t.
proofs.statement: ev t (pmul xs ys) = ev t xs * ev t ys

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.reduced_product
proofs.doc: **The reduced count mult-adds**: P(X×Y) − 1 = (P(X) − 1) ✳ (P(Y) − 1), at every t. At t = 1: non-base cells of a pointed product = wedge + smash. At t = −1: χ̃(X×Y) = χ̃X ✳ χ̃Y.
proofs.statement: ev t (pmul xs ys) - 1 = (ev t xs - 1) ✳ (ev t ys - 1)

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.sphere_rchi
proofs.doc: Spheres sit at ±1: χ̃(Sⁿ) = (−1)ⁿ.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.circle_wall
proofs.doc: **The circle is the wall**: χ̃(S¹ × Y) = −1 for every Y.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.torus_cells
proofs.doc: The torus S¹ × S¹: one 0-cell, two 1-cells, one 2-cell.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.s2_s2
proofs.doc: Even spheres sit at mult-add's 1: χ̃(S² × S²) = 1 ✳ 1 = 3.

proofs.name: CategoryTheory.suspension_split
proofs.doc: Suspension multiplies the reduced count by t, so the splitting Σ(X×Y) ≃ ΣX ∨ ΣY ∨ Σ(X∧Y) has the count t·(a ✳ b) = ta + tb + t·ab.
proofs.statement: t * (ev t (pmul xs ys) - 1) = t * (ev t xs - 1) + t * (ev t ys - 1) + t * ((ev t xs - 1) * (ev t ys - 1))

proofs.name: ChemAcids.isoelectric
proofs.doc: Isoelectric point of a two-group amino acid: if h² = K₁K₂, the carboxylate fraction K₁/(K₁ + h) equals the ammonium fraction h/(K₂ + h). Cleared form.

proofs.name: ChemAcids.mediant_above
proofs.doc: Mixing two buffers: the mediant of b₁/a₁ ≤ b₂/a₂ is at least the smaller ratio (cleared, a's positive).

proofs.name: ChemAcids.mediant_below
proofs.doc: …and at most the larger one.

proofs.name: ChemAcids.fold_three
proofs.doc: The dial folded over three equal sites: x ⊞ₖ x ⊞ₖ x = 3x + 3k x² + k² x³.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (wAdd k x x) x = 3 * x + 3 * k * (x * x) + k * k * (x * x * x)

proofs.name: ChemAcids.pairwise_equal_gaps
proofs.doc: Uniform pairwise interaction: β₁ = 3K, β₂ = 3kK², β₃ = k³K³ satisfy β₁³β₃ = β₂³, which says the two stepwise ratios K₁/K₂ and K₂/K₃ are equal (equal pKa gaps).

proofs.name: ChemAcids.fold_unequal_gaps
proofs.doc: The fold's coefficients 3, 3k, k² break that equality by the factor k: β₁³β₃ − β₂³ = 27k²(1 − k), zero only at k = 0 or k = 1.

proofs.name: ChemAcids.fold_gap_log3
proofs.doc: In the fold, the second and third stepwise constants are 3k/3 = k and k²/(3k) = k/3: their ratio is exactly 3 (a pKa gap of log 3) whatever k ≠ 0 is.

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.yonetani_theorell
proofs.doc: Yonetani–Theorell: with k = 1/α the binding polynomial minus one is a ⊞ₖ b.
proofs.statement: (1 + a + b + k * a * b) - 1 = wAdd k a b

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.independent_lift
proofs.doc: Independent inhibitors (k = 1): mult-add, so 1 + (a ⊞₁ b) = (1 + a)(1 + b).

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.bliss
proofs.doc: …which is Bliss independence for the remaining activity: 1/(1+a) · 1/(1+b) = 1/(1 + a ⊞₁ b).

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.isobole
proofs.doc: The 50% isobole for interaction k: b(1 + k·a) = 1 − a solves a ⊞ₖ b = 1.

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.series_rate
proofs.doc: Irreversible steps in series: times add, so with t = 1/k the turnover time of three steps is t₁ + t₂ + t₃ and the overall rate is its reciprocal (cleared: kcat·(t₁ + t₂ + t₃) = 1).

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.nitrogenase_electrons
proofs.doc: Nitrogenase: 6 of 8 electrons reach ammonia, 3/4.

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.nitrogenase_atp
proofs.doc: 16 ATP per N₂ is 8 per NH₃.

proofs.name: ChemBiochem.calvin_efficiency
proofs.doc: Photosynthesis at the 8-photon limit: 478 kJ stored from 1407 kJ of 680 nm photons lies between 33% and 35%.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.overlap_border
proofs.doc: S = 1 is the border: identical orbitals, coefficients add.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.overlap_opposite
proofs.doc: S = −1: opposite phases, coefficients subtract.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.overlap_orthogonal
proofs.doc: S = 0: orthogonal orbitals, Pythagoras.
proofs.statement: norm2 a b 0 = a * a + b * b

proofs.name: ChemBonding.bonding_norm
proofs.doc: The equal-weight combination φa + φb has length² 2 + 2S = (1+S)·2, the lift of S at weight 1.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.split_asymmetry
proofs.doc: Asymmetric splitting: with bonding (α+β)/(1+S) and antibonding (α−β)/(1−S), rise·(1−S) and fall·(1+S) are both αS − β, so rise/fall = (1+S)/(1−S). Stated cleared of denominators: the two numerators agree.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.one_pow_rat
proofs.doc: 1ⁿ = 1 over Rat (core has no lemma by this name).

proofs.name: ChemBonding.sq_nonneg_rat
proofs.doc: Squares are nonnegative over Rat.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.cassini_step
proofs.doc: Cassini step: the invariant is multiplied by q at each site.
proofs.statement: chainP k q (n + 2) * chainP k q (n + 2) - chainP k q (n + 3) * chainP k q (n + 1) = q * (chainP k q (n + 1) * chainP k q (n + 1) - chainP k q (n + 2) * chainP k q n)

proofs.name: ChemBonding.cassini
proofs.doc: Cassini: P(n+1)² − P(n+2)·P(n) = q^(n+1).
proofs.statement: chainP k q (n + 1) * chainP k q (n + 1) - chainP k q (n + 2) * chainP k q n = q ^ (n + 1)

proofs.name: ChemBonding.huckel_unimodular
proofs.doc: A plain carbon chain (q = 1) has invariant 1 at every length.
proofs.statement: chainP x 1 (n + 1) * chainP x 1 (n + 1) - chainP x 1 (n + 2) * chainP x 1 n = 1

proofs.name: ChemBonding.butadiene
proofs.doc: Butadiene (4 carbons): P 4 = x⁴ − 3x² + 1, whose roots are ±φ, ±1/φ (golden ratio).

proofs.name: ChemBonding.allyl
proofs.doc: Allyl (3 carbons): P 3 = x (x² − 2): levels 0, ±√2.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.band_square
proofs.doc: Completing the square: 4(t² − x t + 1) = (2t − x)² + (4 − x²).

proofs.name: ChemBonding.no_root_in_band
proofs.doc: Turning country: inside the band (x² < 4) the transfer polynomial has no rational root.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.band_edge
proofs.doc: Border: at the band edge x = 2 the root t = 1 is double.

proofs.name: ChemBonding.gap_pair
proofs.doc: Gap (two walls): x = 5/2 has the reciprocal real pair t = 2, 1/2.

proofs.doc: N₂: 8 bonding, 2 antibonding valence electrons → triple bond.

proofs.doc: The dial applied three times, (1 + k e)³ = 1 + k·(triple): the associative ladder the checks test against bond energies (it fits C–C to 3% and misses N–N by 13%).

proofs.name: ChemConservation.lavoisier
proofs.doc: Lavoisier's border: c = 1 gives exactly (m₁ + m₂)².

proofs.name: ChemConservation.deficit
proofs.doc: The mass deficit squared is 2 m₁ m₂ (1 − c).

proofs.name: ChemConservation.binding_exact
proofs.doc: With a binding energy B, M = m₁ + m₂ − B: B(2(m₁+m₂) − B) = 2 m₁ m₂ (1 − c), exactly.

proofs.name: ChemConservation.bound_lighter
proofs.doc: Bound (c < 1) means the whole weighs less than its parts, for positive masses.
proofs.statement: mass2 m1 m2 c < (m1 + m2) * (m1 + m2)

proofs.name: ChemConservation.free_heavier
proofs.doc: Free pairs in motion (c > 1) weigh more than their rest masses.
proofs.statement: (m1 + m2) * (m1 + m2) < mass2 m1 m2 c

proofs.name: ChemConservation.cosine_extra
proofs.doc: The cosine law reads as a weighted mult-add in the masses' squares: with a = m₁², b = m₂² and the corner taken through √(ab) = m₁m₂, the extra piece beyond plain addition is 2c·m₁m₂. At c = 1 it is the perfect square.

proofs.name: ChemConservation.small_angle
proofs.doc: Small-angle form: if c = 1 − t/2 (t = θ²), the squared deficit is m₁m₂·t.

proofs.name: ChemConservation.fugacity_multAdd
proofs.doc: So the excess z^Q − 1 mult-adds.
proofs.statement: pw z (Q1 + Q2) - 1 = (pw z Q1 - 1) ✳ (pw z Q2 - 1)

proofs.name: ChemConservation.neutral_identity
proofs.doc: A neutral system (charge 0) has fugacity 1: excess 0, mult-add's identity.

proofs.name: ChemConservation.circle_closed
proofs.doc: Rotation (the phase e^{iQφ}) in Gaussian-rational coordinates: if both factors lie on the unit circle, so does their product. The excess of a point of the circle is never the wall −1 unless the point is 0.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.luther_balance
proofs.doc: Luther's rule: the combined potential m = (n₁E₁ + n₂E₂)/(n₁ + n₂) balances the two couples.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.luther_idem
proofs.doc: Luther's mean is idempotent: a couple combined with itself gives the same potential, so potentials are averaged, not mult-added.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.two_site
proofs.doc: Two one-electron sites with interaction factor k: Z − 1 = x ⊞ₖ x.
proofs.statement: (1 + 2 * x + k * x * x) - 1 = wAdd k x x

proofs.name: ChemElectro.two_site_disc
proofs.doc: Its discriminant is 4(1 − k): complex zeros exactly when k > 1 (cooperativity).

proofs.name: ChemElectro.nernst_midpoint
proofs.doc: Midpoint of the two-electron Nernst curve: with s² = k, at x = 1/s the mean number of electrons 2x(1 + kx)/(1 + 2x + kx²) equals 1. Cleared form.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.stage_losses3
proofs.doc: Three stages fold the same way, in either grouping.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.kok_mean
proofs.doc: Kok clock: one flash advances 0, 1 or 2 steps with probabilities α, 1 − α − β, β. The mean advance is 1 − α + β.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.kok_damped
proofs.doc: The damping eigenvalue α − β + i(1 − α − β) has squared modulus at most 1 when α, β ≥ 0 and α + β ≤ 1, so the four-flash oscillation never grows.

proofs.name: ChemElectro.zscheme_bounds
proofs.doc: Z-scheme bookkeeping in meV: 4 electrons × 1135 meV stored from 4 × 1823 + 4 × 1771 meV of photons, between 30% and a third.

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.binding_dial
proofs.doc: Two-site binding polynomial minus one is the dial.
proofs.statement: (1 + a + b + ω * a * b) - 1 = wAdd ω a b

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.diacid_gap
proofs.doc: Symmetric diacid, association form: β₁ = 2K, β₂ = ωK², so β₂·4 = ω·β₁².

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.two_site_disc
proofs.doc: Two equal sites: discriminant of ωx² + 2x + 1 is 4(1 − ω).

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.two_site_square
proofs.doc: If ω ≤ 1 the polynomial factors over the reals in principle; for ω > 1 there is no real (here: rational) zero, since ω(ωx² + 2x + 1) = (ωx + 1)² + (ω − 1).

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.cooperative_no_real_zero
proofs.doc: Cooperative pairs (ω > 1) have no real binding zero.

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.independent_double_zero
proofs.doc: Independent pair (ω = 1): the polynomial is (1 + x)², a double zero at x = −1.

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.fold_lift
proofs.doc: The dial folded over n copies of x: 1 + k·(fold) = (1 + kx)^n (library wpow_lift).
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wpow k x n = (1 + k * x) ^ n

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.fold_is_mwc
proofs.doc: MWC with exclusive binding: k·(1 + fold) = (k − 1) + (1 + kx)^n, i.e. L = k − 1.
proofs.statement: k * (1 + wpow k x n) = (k - 1) + (1 + k * x) ^ n

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.four_site_coeffs
proofs.doc: Four sites: the fold's coefficients 4, 6k, 4k², k³ (j ligands carry k^(j−1)).

proofs.name: ChemEquilibrium.haber_pressure
proofs.doc: Mass action: activities multiply into Q, so log Q adds; here Q for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ scales as p⁻² when every partial pressure is multiplied by p.

proofs.name: ChemGas.two_corrections
proofs.doc: The two corrections multiply: (1 + α)(1 − β) = 1 + α ✳ (−β).

proofs.name: ChemGas.corner
proofs.doc: The corner of the two corrections is −αβ.

proofs.name: ChemGas.vdw_inverse_Z
proofs.doc: van der Waals in its own form gives 1/Z = (1 + a/PV²)(1 − b/V).

proofs.name: ChemGas.critical_Z
proofs.doc: vdW critical constants Vc = 3b, RTc = 8a/(27b), Pc = a/(27b²) give Zc = 3/8.

proofs.name: ChemGas.mayer_three
proofs.doc: Mayer for three pairs: (1 + f₁)(1 + f₂)(1 + f₃) = 1 + f₁ ✳ f₂ ✳ f₃.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ChemGas.mayer_clusters
proofs.doc: Expanded, the three-pair fold is the seven nonempty products: singles, pairs and the triangle.

proofs.name: ChemGas.cubic_discriminants
proofs.doc: Their discriminants u² − 4w are 0, 1 and 8.

proofs.name: ChemGas.dalton
proofs.doc: Dalton: partial pressures x·P add up to P when the mole fractions sum to 1.
proofs.statement: x1 * P + x2 * P + x3 * P = P

proofs.name: ChemGas.fugacity_product
proofs.doc: Fugacity coefficients multiply into an equilibrium: here φ₁²/(φ₂ φ₃³) written without division.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.K_excess
proofs.doc: Equilibrium constants multiply; their excesses mult-add.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.K_three
proofs.doc: Three coupled reactions: the excesses fold associatively.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.Z2_dial
proofs.doc: Z − 1 is the weighted mult-add with weight ω.
proofs.statement: Z2 x y ω - 1 = wAdd ω x y

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.exclusion_adds
proofs.doc: Hard exclusion (ω = 0): occupations simply add.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.independent_factors
proofs.doc: No interaction (ω = 1): the sites are independent and Z factors.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.independent_multAdd
proofs.doc: Independent sites: Z − 1 is mult-add.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.covariance
proofs.doc: Covariance identity, cleared of Z²: Z·(ωxy) − (x + ωxy)(y + ωxy) = xy(ω − 1).
proofs.statement: Z2 x y ω * (ω * x * y) - (x + ω * x * y) * (y + ω * x * y) = x * y * (ω - 1)

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.covariance_pos
proofs.doc: With x, y > 0, the covariance is positive exactly when ω > 1.

proofs.name: ChemGibbs.gibbs_adds
proofs.doc: Free energies at a temperature add when reactions add (ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is linear).

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.benzene_charpoly
proofs.doc: Benzene (Hückel 6-ring): x⁶ − 6x⁴ + 9x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2)(x − 1)²(x + 1)².

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.cyclobutadiene_charpoly
proofs.doc: Cyclobutadiene (Hückel 4-ring): x⁴ − 4x² = x²(x − 2)(x + 2), a doubly degenerate zero level.

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.mobius4_charpoly
proofs.doc: Möbius 4-ring: x⁴ − 4x² + 4 = (x² − 2)², levels ±√2, each twice.

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.benzene_resonance
proofs.doc: Benzene's π energy (in β): 2·2 + 4·1 = 8, two more than three ethylenes (6).

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.ee_compose
proofs.doc: Matched selectivities: with e = (r − 1)/(r + 1), multiplying the ratios composes ee by (e₁ + e₂)/(1 + e₁e₂). Cleared form, with e₁, e₂ given by their defining equations.

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.ee_is_landscape
proofs.doc: The ee law is the landscape law at (k, q) = (0, −1): numerator e₁ + e₂, denominator 1 + e₁e₂.

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.ee_two_walls
proofs.doc: Its discriminant k² − 4q is 4: the two-walls country.

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.ee_wall
proofs.doc: ee = 1 is a wall: a perfectly selective step absorbs any other (cleared: 1 + b = 1·(1 + 1·b)).

proofs.name: ChemOrganic.horeau
proofs.doc: Horeau duplication is e ⊕ e: numerator 2e, denominator 1 + e².

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.shell_square
proofs.doc: The shell square: (m + 1)² = 1 + m ✳ m, with m = n − 1.

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.gnomons_fill
proofs.doc: The gnomons fill the square: shell n = m + 1 holds n² orbitals.

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.gnomon
proofs.doc: Each gnomon is corner + two edges of the next square: 2l + 1 = 1 + l + l.

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.shell_capacity
proofs.doc: With spin, shell n holds 2n² electrons.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.two_spins
proofs.doc: SO(4): two independent spins with multiplicity n each give n · n states, and (n − 1) mult-adds with itself.

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.diagCap_closed
proofs.doc: Diagonal s holds 2 · ⌈s/2⌉² electrons, in closed form.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.period_is_diagonal
proofs.doc: Period p (≥ 2) and the diagonal pair it covers agree: periods 2k and 2k+1 have the length of diagonals 2k+1 and 2k+2.

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.q_integer
proofs.doc: n copies of 1 under ⊞ₖ lift to (1 + k)ⁿ: with q = k + 1, that is qⁿ, so the weighted power is the q-integer (qⁿ − 1)/(q − 1).
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wpow k 1 n = (1 + k) ^ n

proofs.name: ChemPeriodic.q_integer_classical
proofs.doc: At k = 0 (q = 1) the weighted power of 1 is n itself: the ordinary shell.

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.fragments_multAdd
proofs.doc: Two independent fragments: the excess amplitude mult-adds.

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.cisd_drops_corner
proofs.doc: What truncated CI drops when two fragments are joined: exactly the corner.

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.three_fragments
proofs.doc: Three fragments: the corner expansion has pairs and one triple, nothing else.
proofs.statement: (a ✳ b) ✳ c = a + b + c + (a * b + a * c + b * c) + a * b * c

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.cisd_drops_three
proofs.doc: What CISD drops from three fragments: every pair and the triple.
proofs.statement: ((a ✳ b) ✳ c) - (a + b + c) = a * b + a * c + b * c + a * b * c

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.cisd_gap
proofs.doc: If e₁ solves the one-molecule problem, N·e₁ misses the N-molecule CISD equation by exactly N(N − 1)e₁², the pairs of molecules both excited.

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.cisd_not_extensive
proofs.doc: So N·e₁ solves N-molecule CISD only when N = 0, N = 1 or e₁ = 0: CISD is not size-extensive.

proofs.name: ChemQuantum.spin_multiplicity
proofs.doc: Multiplicities multiply, so 2s (multiplicity − 1) mult-adds.

proofs.name: ChemRates.parallel_channels
proofs.doc: Parallel channels at a fixed time: survivals multiply too.

proofs.name: ChemRates.second_order_lens
proofs.doc: Second order: with u = a/(1−a), v = b/(1−b), the sum u + v equals c/(1−c) where c = (a + b − 2ab)/(1 − ab). Cleared: (u + v)(1 − c) = c with all denominators multiplied out.
proofs.statement: (a * (1 - b) + b * (1 - a)) * (landDen 1 a b - landNum (-2) a b) = landNum (-2) a b * ((1 - a) * (1 - b))

proofs.name: ChemRates.second_order_border
proofs.doc: (−2, 1) is on the border: k² = 4q.

proofs.name: ChemRates.first_order_point
proofs.doc: First order is the point (−1, 0): the landscape law reduces to wAdd (−1).
proofs.statement: landNum (-1) a b = wAdd (-1) a b

proofs.name: ChemRates.osculating_disc
proofs.doc: The osculating point (−n, n(n−1)/2) has discriminant n(2 − n) (times 1, over Rat).

proofs.name: ChemRates.osculating_small
proofs.doc: Order 0, 1, 2 give q = 0, 0, 1 on that curve.

proofs.name: ChemRates.half_order_wall
proofs.doc: Order ½ empties in finite time: s^(1/2) = 1 − kt/2 hits 0 at t = 2/k. Cleared: k·(2/k) = 2.

proofs.name: ChemRates.arrhenius_steps
proofs.doc: Arrhenius ratios over successive steps multiply (as exponents, they add).

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.loss_two
proofs.doc: Two steps: overall loss is the k = −1 mult-add of the step losses.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.loss_n
proofs.doc: n equal steps: overall loss 1 − (1 − ℓ)^n is the k = −1 power.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.loss_assoc
proofs.doc: Losses compose in any grouping (associativity of the fold).
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) a b) c = wAdd (-1) a (wAdd (-1) b c)

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.ten_steps
proofs.doc: Ten steps at 90%: (9/10)^10 overall, so 1 − (9/10)^10 is lost.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.eight_fragments
proofs.doc: Eight fragments: three levels convergent, seven linear.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.two_atoms
proofs.doc: A two-isotope atom's polynomial p + q x; two atoms multiply to p² + 2pq x + q² x².
proofs.statement: (p + q * x) * (p + q * x) = p * p + 2 * p * q * x + q * q * x * x

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.chlorine_961
proofs.doc: Chlorine at 3 : 1: Cl₂ is 9 : 6 : 1.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.bromine_121
proofs.doc: Bromine at 1 : 1: Br₂ is 1 : 2 : 1.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.mediant_between
proofs.doc: Mediant: combining a:b with c:d gives (a+c):(b+d), which lies between them.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.magnetite
proofs.doc: Fe₃O₄ = FeO + Fe₂O₃: Fe:O 3:4 from 1:1 and 2:3.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.magnetite_between
proofs.doc: 2/3 < 3/4 < 1/1 for Fe:O, by cross-multiplication.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.haber_balanced
proofs.doc: Haber balances: N 2 = 2·1, H 3·2 = 2·3.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.respiration_balanced
proofs.doc: Respiration balances C, H, O: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ → 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O.

proofs.name: ChemStoichiometry.nitrogenase_family
proofs.doc: Nitrogenase's N₂ + 8 H → 2 NH₃ + H₂ balances, and so does N₂ + 6 H → 2 NH₃: stoichiometry alone leaves the H₂ count free.

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.mul_assoc
proofs.statement: B4.mul p q (B4.mul p q x y) z = B4.mul p q x (B4.mul p q y z)

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.u_sq
proofs.doc: The generators obey the defining relations.

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.vector_sq
proofs.doc: A vector squares to the rate form: (xu + yv)² = x² + pxy + qy².

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.theta_sq
proofs.doc: θ = uv squares to pθ − q: the θ-lift is the even part of this Clifford algebra.

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.even_is_tmul
proofs.doc: The even part multiplies exactly like `tmul` (GroupsLie): same algebra.
proofs.statement: B4.mul p q ⟨x, 0, 0, y⟩ ⟨z, 0, 0, w⟩ = ⟨(GroupsLie.tmul p q (x, y) (z, w)).1, 0, 0, (GroupsLie.tmul p q (x, y) (z, w)).2⟩

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.lift_mul
proofs.doc: Two lifts multiply to the landscape law: (1 + aθ)(1 + bθ) = (1 − qab) + (a + b + pab)θ.

proofs.name: CliffordW.B4.lift_multAdd
proofs.doc: At mult-add's point (1, 0) the geometric product of lifts is the lift of a ✳ b.

proofs.name: CliffordW.multAdd_form_split
proofs.doc: Mult-add's rate form x² + xy factors as x(x + y): two light lines (a split form).

proofs.name: CliffordW.tconj_mul
proofs.statement: tconj p (GroupsLie.tmul p q u v) = GroupsLie.tmul p q (tconj p u) (tconj p v)

proofs.name: CliffordW.mul_tconj
proofs.doc: X·X̄ is the scalar x² + pxy + qy² (the norm form, = the rate form).
proofs.statement: GroupsLie.tmul p q u (tconj p u) = (u.1 * u.1 + p * u.1 * u.2 + q * u.2 * u.2, 0)

proofs.name: CliffordW.lift_tconj
proofs.doc: The lift times its conjugate is the rate V(a) = 1 + pa + qa².
proofs.statement: GroupsLie.tmul p q (1, a) (tconj p (1, a)) = (1 + p * a + q * a * a, 0)

proofs.name: CliffordW.multAdd_lift_tconj
proofs.doc: Mult-add: lift times conjugate = 1 + a, so the conjugate (1 + a) − aθ is (1 + a)·(lift of the inverse).

proofs.name: CliffordW.tconj_chart_inverse
proofs.doc: The conjugate of a lift, read in the chart, is the landscape inverse: its θ-slot over its scalar slot, −a/(1 + pa), composes with a to 0 (numerator of F vanishes).

proofs.name: CliffordW.wall_zero_divisor
proofs.doc: Mult-add's wall is a zero divisor: (1 − θ)·θ = 0 when θ² = θ.

proofs.name: CliffordW.theta_idem
proofs.doc: θ is idempotent at mult-add's point.

proofs.name: CliffordW.cmul_assoc
proofs.statement: cmul κ (cmul κ u v) w = cmul κ u (cmul κ v w)

proofs.name: CliffordW.cmul_comm
proofs.statement: cmul κ u v = cmul κ v u

proofs.name: CliffordW.dial_sq
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton: K² = tr(K)·K − N(K).
proofs.statement: cmul κ K K = (ctr K * K.1 - cnorm κ K, ctr K * K.2)

proofs.name: CliffordW.dial_lift
proofs.doc: (1 + aK)(1 + bK) = (1 − N·ab) + (a + b + tr·ab)K: a multivector dial with scalar arguments gives the landscape law with p = tr K, q = N K.
proofs.statement: cmul κ (1 + a * K.1, a * K.2) (1 + b * K.1, b * K.2) = (1 - cnorm κ K * a * b + (a + b + ctr K * a * b) * K.1, (a + b + ctr K * a * b) * K.2)

proofs.name: CliffordW.dial_discriminant
proofs.doc: The class invariant p² − 4q of the dial is 4κk₁²: the country is the sign of κ.
proofs.statement: ctr K * ctr K - 4 * cnorm κ K = 4 * κ * K.2 * K.2

proofs.name: CliffordW.multAdd_dial_null
proofs.doc: Mult-add's dial is null: K = c(1 + e) with e² = 1 has N = 0 and tr = 2c, so K² = 2c·K.
proofs.statement: cnorm 1 (c, c) = 0 ∧ ctr (c, c) = 2 * c ∧ cmul 1 (c, c) (c, c) = (2 * c * c, 2 * c * c)

proofs.name: CliffordW.sq_nonneg'
proofs.doc: Squares are nonnegative (core Int has no named lemma for this).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: CliffordW.complex_no_zero_norm
proofs.doc: κ = −1 (complex numbers): the norm vanishes only at 0, so the wall stays one point.

proofs.name: CliffordW.split_zero_divisor
proofs.doc: κ = +1 (split-complex): (1 + e)(1 − e) = 0, a zero divisor; the wall grows to two lines.

proofs.name: CliffordW.dual_nilpotent
proofs.doc: κ = 0 (dual numbers): e² = 0.

proofs.name: CliffordW.omega_projector
proofs.doc: Clifford's elliptic ω (ω² = 1): (1 + ω)² = 2(1 + ω), so (1 + ω)/2 is idempotent, like θ.

proofs.name: CliffordW.omega_split
proofs.doc: x + yω ↦ (x + y, x − y) turns ω-multiplication into slot-by-slot multiplication: the elliptic biquaternion splits into a left half and a right half.

proofs.name: CliffordW.quaternion_no_zero_norm
proofs.doc: The quaternion case: the norm of x₀ + x₁i + x₂j + x₃k vanishes only at 0.

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.mul_assoc
proofs.statement: G4.mul k1 k2 (G4.mul k1 k2 x y) z = G4.mul k1 k2 x (G4.mul k1 k2 y z)

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.star_lift
proofs.doc: Kept: the left lift. 1 + K(X ✳_K Y) = (1 + KX)(1 + KY).
proofs.statement: G4.add G4.one (G4.mul k1 k2 K (G4.star k1 k2 K x y)) = G4.mul k1 k2 (G4.add G4.one (G4.mul k1 k2 K x)) (G4.add G4.one (G4.mul k1 k2 K y))

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.star_assoc
proofs.doc: Kept: associativity, for every multivector dial K.
proofs.statement: G4.star k1 k2 K (G4.star k1 k2 K x y) z = G4.star k1 k2 K x (G4.star k1 k2 K y z)

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.star_zero
proofs.statement: G4.star k1 k2 K x ⟨0, 0, 0, 0⟩ = x

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.star_comm_defect
proofs.doc: Lost: commutativity. X ✳ Y − Y ✳ X = XKY − YKX.
proofs.statement: G4.sub (G4.star k1 k2 K x y) (G4.star k1 k2 K y x) = G4.sub (G4.mul k1 k2 (G4.mul k1 k2 x K) y) (G4.mul k1 k2 (G4.mul k1 k2 y K) x)

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.vector_comm_wedge
proofs.doc: For two vectors and K = 1 the defect is twice the wedge: 2(x₁y₂ − x₂y₁)e₁₂, twice the oriented area, whatever the squares κ₁, κ₂.

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.vector_corner
proofs.doc: The corner of two vectors (K = 1, Euclidean squares) splits into dot + wedge: x ✳ y = x + y + (x·y) + (x∧y)e₁₂.

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.rev_mul
proofs.doc: Reversion reverses products.
proofs.statement: G4.rev (G4.mul k1 k2 x y) = G4.mul k1 k2 (G4.rev y) (G4.rev x)

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.rev_star
proofs.doc: Reversion turns X ✳_K Y into Ỹ ✳_K̃ X̃.
proofs.statement: G4.rev (G4.star k1 k2 K x y) = G4.star k1 k2 (G4.rev K) (G4.rev y) (G4.rev x)

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.blades_keep
proofs.doc: Information kept: two factors in different directions keep their product on its own blade, a₁e₁ ✳ a₂e₂ = a₁e₁ + a₂e₂ + a₁a₂e₁₂, whatever the squares; the scalar shadow (sum of the parts) is a₁ ✳ a₂.

proofs.name: CliffordW.G4.vector_dial_walls
proofs.doc: Two walls for a vector dial: (1 + a k)(1 − a k) = 1 − a²k² with k = 3e₁ + 4e₂ (k² = 25).

proofs.name: CliffordW.dual_multAdd
proofs.statement: (GroupsLie.tmul 0 0 (a0, a1) (b0, b1)).2 + a1 + b1 = a1 * (1 + b0) + b1 * (1 + a0) ∧ (GroupsLie.tmul 0 0 (a0, a1) (b0, b1)).1 + a0 + b0 = a0 ✳ b0

proofs.name: CliffordW.sig_shift_11
proofs.doc: Cl(p+1, q+1) ≅ M₂(Cl(p, q)): the count doubles.

proofs.name: CliffordW.sig_bott_8
proofs.doc: Bott: eight more positive directions multiply the count by 16 = 2⁴.
proofs.statement: ∀ p < 5, ∀ q < 5, sig (p + 8) q = 16 * sig p q

proofs.name: CliffordW.division_only
proofs.doc: Only R, C, H have no blade squaring to +1 (p + q ≤ 8): the wall of 1 + X stays a single point exactly in the three division algebras Cl(0,0), Cl(0,1), Cl(0,2).

proofs.name: CliffordW.division_cases
proofs.statement: plusBlades 0 0 = 0 ∧ plusBlades 0 1 = 0 ∧ plusBlades 0 2 = 0 ∧ plusBlades 0 3 = 1 ∧ plusBlades 1 0 = 1 ∧ plusBlades 0 4 = 5

proofs.name: FusedRate.ladder
proofs.doc: Ladder lemma: if each rung is the one below it run after one step of `s`, then rung j is the bottom rung run after j steps of `s`. On [1,2] the fused-linear rungs satisfy this with f x = b^x and s x = b^(x-1), which gives H_k(b,x) = b^(s^(k-3)(x)).
proofs.statement: ∀ j x, G j x = f (iter s j x)

proofs.name: FusedRate.grow
proofs.doc: Growth template: if each step multiplies the gap by at least p/q, then after j steps it is at least (p/q)^j times the start.
proofs.statement: ∀ j, p ^ j * d 0 ≤ q ^ j * d j

proofs.name: Combinatorics.groups_length
proofs.doc: The corners of the n-cube: 2ⁿ sub-lists.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.foldMA_replicate
proofs.doc: n copies of a, folded by mult-add, is the mult-add power.
proofs.statement: foldMA (List.replicate n a) = mpow a n

proofs.name: Combinatorics.painted_subsets
proofs.doc: **The dial paints subsets.** The corners of the n-cube, each switched-on axis weighing k, add up to (1 + k)ⁿ: every element is off, or on in one of k colours.
proofs.statement: sumL ((groups (List.replicate n k)).map prodL) = (1 + k) ^ n

proofs.name: Combinatorics.nonempty_subsets_lift
proofs.doc: Mult-add of a with itself n times, at a = 1: the lift of 2ⁿ − 1 nonempty subsets.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.nonempty_subsets
proofs.doc: On Int: 2ⁿ − 1 nonempty subsets.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.alternating_corners
proofs.doc: k = −1: the signed corners cancel (inclusion–exclusion's engine).

proofs.name: Combinatorics.parity_corners
proofs.doc: k = −2: the parity dial gives (−1)ⁿ.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.wfold_lift
proofs.doc: The dial lift of a whole list.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wfold k l = prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + k * x))

proofs.name: Combinatorics.wall_entry_absorbs
proofs.doc: **The wall swallows the fold.** If one entry sits on the wall (1 + k·a = 0), the lift of the whole fold is 0.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.kfold_lift
proofs.statement: 1 + k * kfold k m = rprod k m

proofs.name: Combinatorics.sign_balance
proofs.doc: **Signs of permutations balance.** At k = −1 the entry 1 is on the wall, so the signed count Π(1 − i) of permutations of m + 2 things is 0.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.cube_is_stirling
proofs.doc: **The cube with axis weights 1, …, n−1 has the Stirling cycle numbers as layers** (grade j = permutations with n − j cycles), checked for n = 1 … 8.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.cyc_row_sums
proofs.doc: Row sums are n!.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.bell_is_E_twice
proofs.doc: E(nonempty sets) = all set partitions: the Bell numbers (rung 2 of the flow on x).

proofs.name: Combinatorics.rung_three
proofs.doc: E(Bell) = partitions of partitions (rung 3 of the flow on x).

proofs.name: Combinatorics.graphs_from_connected
proofs.doc: E(connected graphs) = all graphs: 2^C(n,2).

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_order2
proofs.doc: Group law, order 2: Eˢ ∘ Eᵗ = Eˢ⁺ᵗ.
proofs.statement: a2 t + a2 s = a2 (s + t)

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_order3
proofs.doc: Group law, order 3: x³ coefficient of f(g(x)) is b₃ + 2a₂b₂ + a₃.
proofs.statement: a3 t + 2 * a2 s * a2 t + a3 s = a3 (s + t)

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_order4
proofs.doc: Group law, order 4: x⁴ coefficient of f(g(x)) is b₄ + a₂(2b₃ + b₂²) + 3a₃b₂ + a₄.
proofs.statement: a4 t + a2 s * (2 * a3 t + a2 t * a2 t) + 3 * a3 s * a2 t + a4 s = a4 (s + t)

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_at_two
proofs.doc: t = 2 counts set partitions: 2!·a₂ = 2, 3!·a₃ = 5, 4!·a₄ = 15.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_at_three
proofs.doc: t = 3 counts partitions of partitions: 2, 12, 60 (with the factorials).

proofs.name: Combinatorics.flow_at_minus_one
proofs.doc: t = −1 is log(1 + x): signed cyclic orders −1, 2, −6.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.half_rung_x4
proofs.doc: The half rung has a zero x⁴ coefficient ...

proofs.name: Combinatorics.quarter_rung_negative
proofs.doc: ... and a quarter rung has a negative x³ coefficient: fractional rungs do not count.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.S2_rows_bell
proofs.doc: Row sums are the Bell numbers, the t = 2 rung.

proofs.name: Combinatorics.compositions_cube
proofs.doc: Compositions on the cube: m parts, choose which j are nonzero (a corner of the m-cube), then a composition of n into j positive parts. Vandermonde.
proofs.statement: ∀ m : Fin 5, ∀ n : Fin 9, nsum ((List.range (m.val + 2)).map (fun j => if j = 0 then 0 else layer (m.val + 1) j * layer n.val (j - 1))) = layer (n.val + m.val + 1) m.val

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.ma_lift
proofs.doc: The lift on the complex plane.
proofs.statement: add one (ma z w) = mul (add one z) (add one w)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.ma_comm
proofs.statement: ma z w = ma w z

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.ma_assoc
proofs.statement: ma (ma z w) u = ma z (ma w u)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.wall_fixed
proofs.doc: The wall −1 absorbs: it is the fixed point of every map z ↦ z ✳ w.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.spin_about_wall
proofs.doc: Seen from the wall, z ↦ z ✳ w is multiplication by 1 + w: a spin and a stretch.
proofs.statement: sub (ma z w) wall = mul (add one w) (sub z wall)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.step_is_turned_w
proofs.doc: The step from z to z ✳ w is the vector w turned and stretched by 1 + z (so triangle (−1, 0, w) and triangle (−1, z, z ✳ w) are similar).
proofs.statement: sub (ma z w) z = mul (add one z) w

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.normSq_mul
proofs.doc: Lengths multiply (Brahmagupta–Fibonacci two-square identity).
proofs.statement: normSq (mul z w) = normSq z * normSq w

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.wall_distance_mul
proofs.doc: Squared distances from the wall multiply under mult-add.
proofs.statement: normSq (add one (ma z w)) = normSq (add one z) * normSq (add one w)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.circle_closed
proofs.doc: The circle |1 + z| = 1 (centre the wall, through 0) is closed under mult-add.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.circle_equation
proofs.doc: The same circle as an equation: 2x + x² + y² = 0, the k = 1 rotation condition of the linear-algebra page.
proofs.statement: normSq (add one z) - 1 = 2 * z.re + (z.re * z.re + z.im * z.im)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.affine_fixing_wall
proofs.doc: An affine map z ↦ αz + β that fixes −1 is mult-add by α − 1.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.affine_compose
proofs.doc: Composing two of them mult-adds their parameters.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.mroot_of_unity
proofs.doc: If ζⁿ = 1 then ζ − 1 is an n-th mult-add root of 0.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.gauss_root_four
proofs.doc: n = 4: i − 1 mult-added four times is 0 (any commutative ring).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.gauss_root_steps
proofs.doc: …but not before: twice gives −2, three times gives −1 − i (on the integers).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.gauss_roots_total
proofs.doc: The four roots of the square mult-add to −2 (even n).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.gauss_roots_on_circle
proofs.doc: All four lie on the circle |1 + z| = 1.
proofs.statement: normSq (add one (⟨-1, 1⟩ : Cx Int)) = 1 ∧ normSq (add one (⟨-2, 0⟩ : Cx Int)) = 1 ∧ normSq (add one (⟨-1, -1⟩ : Cx Int)) = 1 ∧ normSq (add one (zero : Cx Int)) = 1

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.Eis.ext'

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.omega_cubed
proofs.doc: ω really is a cube root of 1: ω·ω·ω = 1.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.eis_root_three
proofs.doc: n = 3: ω − 1 mult-added three times is 0.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.eis_roots_total
proofs.doc: The three roots 0, ω − 1, ω² − 1 = −2 − ω mult-add to 0 (odd n).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.fixed_points_are_walls
proofs.doc: The fixed points of b ↦ F(a,b) solve a·(1 + p·b + q·b²) = 0: the walls, for every a.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.Mob.ext'

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.trans_compose
proofs.doc: Translations compose by the law itself: T(a)∘T(b) = T(a + b + p·ab over 1 − q·ab).
proofs.statement: Mob.comp (trans p q a 1) (trans p q b 1) = trans p q (a + b + p * a * b) (1 - q * a * b)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.trans_det
proofs.doc: det T(a) is the wall polynomial: the translation degenerates exactly at a wall.
proofs.statement: (trans p q a 1).α * (trans p q a 1).δ - (trans p q a 1).β * (trans p q a 1).γ = 1 + p * a + q * a * a

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.trans_type
proofs.doc: tr² − 4·det = N²(p² − 4q): the discriminant alone sets every translation's type.
proofs.statement: ((trans p q N D).α + (trans p q N D).δ) * ((trans p q N D).α + (trans p q N D).δ) - 4 * ((trans p q N D).α * (trans p q N D).δ - (trans p q N D).β * (trans p q N D).γ) = N * N * (p * p - 4 * q)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.two_walls_lift
proofs.doc: Two walls (reciprocals r₁, r₂, so p = −(r₁ + r₂), q = r₁r₂): ζ(x) = (1 − r₁x)/(1 − r₂x) turns the law into multiplication. Cross-multiplied, with F = N/D.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.two_walls_multAdd
proofs.doc: Mult-add is the case of one wall at −1 and the other at infinity (r₁ = −1, r₂ = 0).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.cayley_tan
proofs.doc: Cayley: the tan law (p, q) = (0, 1) has walls ±i, and (1 + i·x)/(1 − i·x) multiplies.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.double_wall_adds
proofs.doc: One double wall (p = 2c, q = c²): ψ(x) = x/(1 + cx) turns the law into addition.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.fold_wall_of_mem
proofs.doc: If one piece sits on the wall, the whole fold sits on the wall.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.prodL_eq_zero_int
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.fold_wall_iff_int
proofs.doc: On the integers the converse holds too: a fold hits the wall only if a piece does (the zeros of a product are the zeros of its factors).

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.corner_bound
proofs.doc: The size bound for one corner: if |a| ≤ A and |b| ≤ B then |a ✳ b| ≤ A ✳ B.
proofs.statement: -(A ✳ B) ≤ a ✳ b ∧ a ✳ b ≤ A ✳ B

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.size_nonneg
proofs.doc: Sizes are never negative under mult-add of sizes.

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.fold_bound
proofs.doc: Weierstrass's bound: the fold of the pieces is bounded by the fold of their sizes, |(a₁ ✳ … ✳ aₙ)| ≤ |a₁| ✳ … ✳ |aₙ| = ∏(1 + |aᵢ|) − 1.
proofs.statement: ∀ (l : List (Rat × Rat)), (∀ x ∈ l, -x.2 ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 ≤ x.2) → -(foldMA (l.map Prod.snd)) ≤ foldMA (l.map Prod.fst) ∧ foldMA (l.map Prod.fst) ≤ foldMA (l.map Prod.snd)

proofs.name: ComplexAnalysis.tate_glue
proofs.doc: Gluing (1 + a) ~ q(1 + a) respects mult-add, so the punctured plane folds into a torus.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.either
proofs.doc: k = −1 is "at least one of two independent events".

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.mpow_lift
proofs.doc: The mult-add power climbs the cube: 1 + k·(a ⊕ₖ … ⊕ₖ a) = (1 + k·a)^n.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wpow k a n = pw (1 + k * a) n

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.mpow_lift1
proofs.statement: 1 + wpow 1 a n = pw (1 + a) n

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.step_formula
proofs.doc: The step a = r − 1 written without division.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.half_is_identity
proofs.doc: At the 51% line the step is exactly the mult-add identity.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.depth_useless
proofs.doc: Powers of the identity do nothing: at q = 1/2 waiting more blocks buys no security.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.quarter_six
proofs.doc: Catch-up probability as a mult-add power, checked exactly for q = 1/4, z = 6: r = 1/3, a = −2/3, and 1 + a^(⊕6) = (1/3)^6.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.three_quorums
proofs.doc: Three quorums sharing an honest validator need f < n/4.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.one_quorum
proofs.doc: The longest-chain rule needs only a majority: one "quorum" against the rest.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.maj3_drift
proofs.doc: The pull toward 0 below 1/2 and toward 1 above it.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.additive_split
proofs.doc: An additive weight is split-proof: n equal accounts weigh what one does.
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Nat, f ((n : Rat) * s) = (n : Rat) * f s

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.coin_age_flip
proofs.doc: Coin age s·(1+t): the 20% attacker outweighs the 80% honest side.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.fused_age_flip
proofs.doc: Fused exponent (1+s)^(1+t) − 1: the same flip, more strongly.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.linear_keeps
proofs.doc: Plain stake keeps the honest majority.

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.caught
proofs.doc: m independent watchers each catching a double vote with chance d: caught = d ⊕₋₁ d ⊕₋₁ … = 1 − (1 − d)^m. Same for the share of an old validator set that has left after t epochs at churn c.
proofs.statement: wpow (-1) d m = 1 - pw (1 - d) m

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.dbl_lift
proofs.statement: 1 + dbl n a = pw (1 + a) (2 ^ n)

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.pietrzak_halves
proofs.statement: pw (pw x (2 ^ m)) (2 ^ n) = pw x (2 ^ (m + n))

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.merge_cut
proofs.doc: Ethereum before the Merge ~23 TWh, after ~0.0026 TWh (CCRI 2022): over 99.98% less.

proofs.name: DarkSector.redshift_power
proofs.doc: n equal stretches: (1+z)^n = 1 + (z ⊕ z ⊕ … ⊕ z).

proofs.name: DarkSector.redshift_compose_int
proofs.doc: The same with integers, so blueshifts (negative z) are covered too.

proofs.name: DarkSector.lcdm_is_weighted_cube
proofs.doc: Flat ΛCDM, exactly: Ωm(1+z)³ + (1-Ωm) = 1 + Ωm·(z ⊕ z ⊕ z). The cosmological constant is the unit cube; matter is the weighted shell of the (1+z) cube around it.

proofs.name: DarkSector.pow_growth_trivial
proofs.doc: The same in the unshifted form: a(t+s) = a(t)^a(s) with a(0) = 1 forces a ≡ 1.

proofs.name: DarkSector.foldMA_ge_sum
proofs.statement: ∀ l : List Nat, l.sum ≤ foldMA l

proofs.name: DarkSector.corner_le_quarter
proofs.doc: The corner is at most a quarter of the square on the sum: 4ab ≤ (a+b)². In units of the scale s, the extra pull relative to the plain sum is at most (a+b)/4 of it, so it fades as the fields weaken. Dark matter shows up in exactly the opposite place: where fields are weakest.

proofs.name: DarkSector.simple_mond_square
proofs.doc: Simple-MOND law g_N = g·μ(g/a₀) written without division is g·g = g_N·g + g_N·a₀ : the square on the observed pull equals two rectangles, g_N by g and g_N by a₀.
proofs.statement: g * g = gN * g + gN * a0

proofs.name: DarkSector.deep_mond_square
proofs.doc: Deep-MOND limit: the observed pull is the side of the square whose area is the rectangle g_N × a₀.
