proofs.name: DataCenterFused.lifts_append
proofs.statement: lifts (xs ++ ys) = lifts xs * lifts ys

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.foldMA_swap
proofs.doc: Swapping two neighbouring stages never changes the total: blame by position is not physical.
proofs.statement: foldMA (xs ++ a :: b :: ys) = foldMA (xs ++ b :: a :: ys)

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.foldMA_split
proofs.doc: Splitting the foldMA at the IT meter: (outside ⊕ inside) is the whole foldMA (TUE = PUE·ITUE).

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.scale_anywhere
proofs.doc: Position independence: scaling one stage's factor scales the facility total by the same amount, wherever that stage sits.
proofs.statement: lifts xs * (f * k) * lifts ys = k * (lifts xs * f * lifts ys)

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.additive_books_corner
proofs.doc: The additive breakdown PUE = 1 + PLF + CLF books the corner as cooling: CLF = c + p*c.
proofs.statement: it * (1 + p) * (1 + c) = it + it * p + (it * c + it * p * c)

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.loss_costs_one_plus_c
proofs.doc: One watt of electrical loss removed saves (1 + c) watts at the meter.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.unit_gap
proofs.doc: Exact gap: k(k+1)·[cost(k) − cost(k+1)] = c X² − k(k+1) a.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.add_unit_iff
proofs.doc: So add a unit exactly when X² passes (a/c)·k(k+1): the switch point is x*·√(k(k+1)), the geometric mean of k and k+1 in units of the sweet spot x* = √(a/c).

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.equal_share
proofs.doc: Equal sharing is best for a square loss: shifting d from one unit to the other costs 2d².

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.cube_layers
proofs.doc: Layers 1, 3, 3, 1 of the fused cube (1+d)³ − 1 = 3d + 3d² + d³.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.spread
proofs.doc: k fans each moving q: k·q³·k² = (k·q)³, i.e. total power = Q³/k² for total flow Q = k q.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.spare_fan
proofs.doc: N+1 fans at speed N versus N fans at speed N+1 (same total flow N(N+1)): power ratio N² : (N+1)², so running the spare always helps.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_append
proofs.doc: Two independent groups of modes: the fold of the whole is the dial sum of the parts.
proofs.statement: fold k (A ++ B) = wAdd k (fold k A) (fold k B)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_lift
proofs.doc: The hole lift: 1 + k·fold = ∏(1 + k·μᵢ), the determinant det(I + kK).
proofs.statement: 1 + k * fold k l = prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + k * x))

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_scale
proofs.doc: k·fold is plain mult-add of the scaled eigenvalues k·μᵢ.
proofs.statement: k * fold k l = foldMA (l.map (fun x => k * x))

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_poisson
proofs.doc: Poisson (k = 0): the fold is the expected count Σμ.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_fermion
proofs.doc: Fermions (k = −1): the fold is P(at least one point) = 1 − ∏(1 − μᵢ).

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_boson
proofs.doc: Bosons (k = +1): the fold is plain mult-add of the eigenvalues.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_swap
proofs.doc: Order of the modes never matters.
proofs.statement: fold k (x :: y :: l) = fold k (y :: x :: l)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fold_two
proofs.doc: Two modes, written out: the corner carries the dial weight.
proofs.statement: fold k [a, b] = a + b + k * a * b

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.wall_mode_fills
proofs.doc: An eigenvalue on the wall −1/k (k·μ = −1) kills the lift: 1 + k·fold = 0, so the hole probability (1 + k·fold)^(−1/k) is 0 for k < 0.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.wall_absorbs
proofs.doc: The wall absorbs the fold: once one mode is at −1/k, so is the whole.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.slots_full
proofs.doc: k = −1/m with eigenvalue m (the wall): each of the m slots is filled for sure.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.modeVar_expand
proofs.statement: modeVar k x = x + k * (x * x)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.modeVar_wall
proofs.doc: On the wall the count is fixed: no variance.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.modeVar_poisson
proofs.doc: Poisson: variance equals mean.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.mode_fano
proofs.doc: Fano factor of a mode, Var/mean = 1 + kμ (the lift).
proofs.statement: modeVar k x / x = 1 + k * x

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fermion_subpoisson
proofs.doc: Fermion side (k ≤ 0) is sub-Poisson, boson side (k ≥ 0) super-Poisson.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.var_formula
proofs.doc: Var N = Σμ + k·Σμ² = tr K + k·tr K².
proofs.statement: varL k l = sumL l + k * sqL l

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fano_line
proofs.doc: The Fano line: variance is affine in k, through the Poisson value at k = 0.
proofs.statement: varL k l = varL 0 l + k * sqL l

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.var_append
proofs.doc: Disjoint groups of modes: variances add.
proofs.statement: varL k (A ++ B) = varL k A + varL k B

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.fact2_formula
proofs.statement: fact2 k l = sumL l * sumL l + k * sqL l

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.var_from_fact2
proofs.doc: Var = E N(N−1) + E N − (E N)², checked against the two formulas.
proofs.statement: varL k l = fact2 k l + sumL l - sumL l * sumL l

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.dial_rescale
proofs.doc: The dial identity behind it: scaling values by c and the weight by 1/c.
proofs.statement: c * wAdd k a b = wAdd (k / c) (c * a) (c * b)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.lifted_kernel_same
proofs.doc: The lifted kernel k·K is what the count sees: unchanged by (k, K) ↦ (k/c, cK).

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.modeVar_rescale
proofs.statement: modeVar (k / c) (c * x) = c * modeVar k x

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.var_superpose
proofs.doc: Variance of m superposed copies: Var(k/m, mK) = m·Var(k, K).
proofs.statement: varL (k / c) (l.map (fun x => c * x)) = c * varL k l

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.two_fermion_copies
proofs.doc: Two fermion copies, each with eigenvalue μ/2, leave a mode empty with chance (1 − μ/2)²: the k = −1/2 hole with eigenvalue μ.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.tilt_in_ruler
proofs.doc: Tilted mean: weighting a mode's count by tᴺ gives mean μt/(1 + kμ(1 − t)). Read in the ruler (mean − μ)/Var it is u/(1 − kμ·u), u = t − 1.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.tilt_lens
proofs.doc: Tilts compose by mult-add in u, and by the lens law in the ruler: p = 1 + 2s, q = s(1 + s).
proofs.statement: ruler s (u ✳ v) = lens (1 + 2 * s) (s * (1 + s)) (ruler s u) (ruler s v)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.count_parabola
proofs.doc: Every dial count lands on one parabola: p² − 4q = 1, two real walls.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.count_walls
proofs.doc: Its two walls are the empty mode and the full mode: 1 + p·x + q·x² = (1 + s·x)(1 + (1+s)·x).

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.rate_shift
proofs.doc: The mean's rate, re-centred: V(μ + h) = V(μ) + (1 + 2kμ)h + k·h².
proofs.statement: modeVar k (x + h) = modeVar k x + (1 + 2 * k * x) * h + k * (h * h)

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.shape_is_fano
proofs.doc: Shape p = 2·Fano − 1 (Fano = 1 + s), so the units-free shape p²/(p² − 4q) = (2F − 1)².

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.particle_hole
proofs.doc: Particle-hole: s and −1 − s give the same shape.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.empty_mode_multadd
proofs.doc: s = 0 (rare points, Poisson): mult-add.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.full_mode_union
proofs.doc: s = −1 (a full fermion mode): the union of failures, k = −1 on the dial line.

proofs.name: DialPointProcesses.half_mode_velocity
proofs.doc: s = −1/2 (a half-filled fermion mode): velocity addition with speed limit 2.

proofs.name: DialPotential.dial_flip
proofs.doc: Flip: the dial −k is the dial k seen through a ↦ −a.

proofs.name: DialPotential.dial_rescale
proofs.doc: Rescaling: if k'·s = k, the dial k' on (s·a, s·b) is s times the dial k on (a, b).
proofs.statement: wAdd k' (s * a) (s * b) = s * wAdd k a b

proofs.name: DialPotential.dial_zero
proofs.doc: At weight zero the dial is plain addition: the symmetric point.

proofs.name: DialPotential.multAdd_mirror
proofs.doc: A dial against its mirror: k ✳ (−k) = −k².

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_eq
proofs.statement: well k0 k = (k0 * k0 - k * k) * (k0 * k0 - k * k)

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_even
proofs.doc: The well is even: it respects the flip.

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_dips
proofs.doc: Zero at both dips.

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_hump
proofs.doc: The hump at the symmetric point k = 0 has height k0⁴.

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_at_dip
proofs.doc: Expansion at the dip: no linear term, curvature 8k0² (twice the h² coefficient 4k0²).
proofs.statement: well k0 (k0 + h) = 4 * k0 * k0 * (h * h) + 4 * k0 * (h * h * h) + h * h * h * h

proofs.name: DialPotential.scale_covariant_is_power
proofs.doc: A potential that scales as V(s·k) = sⁿ V(k) is a single power: V(k) = V(1)·kⁿ.

proofs.name: DialPotential.well_breaks_scale
proofs.doc: The double well cannot respect the rescaling for any power n: a scale from outside sets k0.
proofs.statement: ¬ (∀ s k : Rat, well 1 (s * k) = s ^ n * well 1 k)

proofs.name: DialPotential.quartic_mass
proofs.doc: (λ/4)((v + x)² − v²)² = ½(2λv²)x² + λv x³ + (λ/4)x⁴: the mass squared is 2λv².

proofs.name: DialPotential.hump_height
proofs.doc: Hump height = m²v²/8 with m² = 2λv².

proofs.name: DialPotential.exp_fixed_point
proofs.doc: With x² = λ²/6 and y² = 1 − λ²/6 (L = λ²): Ω_φ = x² + y² = 1 and x² − y² = L/3 − 1, so w = L/3 − 1.

proofs.name: DialPotential.w_conformal_one
proofs.doc: Conformal slope n = 1 (λ² = 2/3): w = −7/9 at the fixed point.

proofs.name: DialPotential.w_conformal_two
proofs.doc: Conformal slope n = 2 (λ² = 8/3): w = −1/9 at the fixed point.

proofs.name: DialPotential.exp_fixed_point_exists
proofs.doc: The fixed point exists (y² ≥ 0) only for λ² ≤ 6.

proofs.name: DialPotential.cw_mass_negative
proofs.doc: Coleman–Weinberg (Gildener–Weinberg) Higgs: 6mW⁴ + 3mZ⁴ − 12mt⁴ < 0, so m_h² < 0, with mW = 80.37, mZ = 91.19, mt = 172.57 GeV. Holds with a wide margin (factor 22).

proofs.name: DialPotential.cw_mass_negative_robust
proofs.doc: Even with the top 10 GeV lighter and W, Z 10 GeV heavier the sign stays negative.

proofs.name: DialPotential.veltman_too_heavy
proofs.doc: Veltman: 4mt² − 2mW² − mZ² > 4·mH² (mH = 125.20 GeV), so the Veltman Higgs is over twice as heavy.

proofs.name: DialPotential.conformal_gamma
proofs.doc: A conformal dial couples to matter with α0² = 1/6 (the same factor that gives slope √(2/3)); then PPN γ = 1 − 2α0²/(1 + α0²) = 5/7, against Cassini's 1 ± 2.3·10⁻⁵.

proofs.name: DialPotential.slope_coupling
proofs.doc: Slope and coupling are tied: for V ∝ kⁿ the slope is n·√(2/3), so λ² = (2/3)n² = 4n²·α0².

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.units_change_weight
proofs.doc: In units λ times bigger, weight k becomes weight k·λ.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (l * a) (l * b) = l * wAdd (k * l) a b

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.weight_to_one
proofs.doc: With units 1/k the weight becomes 1: every nonzero k is mult-add in its own units.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (a / k) (b / k) = (1 / k) * multAdd a b

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.odds_union
proofs.doc: Odds t ↦ probability t/(1+t); "in A or in B" (independent) has odds t ✳ s.
proofs.statement: 1 - multAdd t s / (1 + multAdd t s) = (1 - t / (1 + t)) * (1 - s / (1 + s))

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.odds_complement
proofs.doc: The complement of a subset with odds t has odds 1/t.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.exponent_ruler
proofs.doc: The uniform dial 2^a − 1 is the exponent a read through the mult-add ruler: dials mult-add exactly when exponents add.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.kRise_succ
proofs.statement: kRise k (e + 1) = kRise k e * (1 + (e : Rat) * k)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.kRise_fermi
proofs.doc: k = −1: an element may appear at most once (subsets).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.kRise_poisson
proofs.doc: k = 0: kRise is 1, so the coefficient is 1/e! (the exponential, Poisson).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.fct_succ
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.kRise_bose
proofs.doc: k = +1: kRise is e!, so every multiplicity has weight 1 (multisets).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.kRise_parafermi
proofs.doc: k = −1/m: m^e · kRise = m(m−1)…(m−e+1).
proofs.statement: m ^ e * kRise (-1 / m) e = fall m e

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.fall_vanish
proofs.doc: At m (a whole number) the falling product vanishes past e = m: with k = −1/m no element appears more than m times.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.fall_full
proofs.doc: At e = m it does not vanish: m copies are allowed.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.cyclotomic_z2
proofs.doc: z² coefficient: (1 − z)^(−M1) gives M1(M1+1)/2, (1 − z²)^(−M2) gives M2; together k². Every two-letter word splits uniquely into Lyndon words.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.cyclotomic_z3
proofs.doc: z³ coefficient: k(k+1)(k+2)/6 + k·M2 + M3 = k³.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.fermi_exponents
proofs.doc: k = −1: exponents M/k on ζ(Ns) are 1, −1, 0: Z = ζ(s)/ζ(2s). k = +1: exponents 1, 0, 0: Z = ζ(s).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialSurvey.necklace_whole
proofs.doc: For whole k the necklace counts are whole: k² − k is even, k³ − k divisible by 3.
proofs.statement: 2 ∣ k * k - k ∧ 3 ∣ k * k * k - k

proofs.name: DialSweep.scale2
proofs.statement: M2.smul k (M2.wmadd k x y) = M2.madd (M2.smul k x) (M2.smul k y)

proofs.name: DialSweep.scale3
proofs.statement: M3.smul k (M3.wmadd k x y) = M3.madd (M3.smul k x) (M3.smul k y)

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_one_sub_2
proofs.doc: k = −1 is the characteristic polynomial at 1 (Fredholm's λ is −k).

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_top
proofs.doc: The top of the dial: det(I + kA) − k³·det A has only lower powers of k.
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul k x)) - k * k * k * M3.det x = 1 + k * M3.tr x + k * k * M3.e2 x

proofs.name: DialSweep.orth_neg_one
proofs.doc: At k = −1 the rotation condition is X + Xᵀ − XᵀX = 0: I − X is orthogonal.
proofs.statement: M3.mul (M3.transpose (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) x))) (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) x)) = M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) (M3.wmadd (-1) (M3.transpose x) x))
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: DialSweep.dialU_sq
proofs.statement: M2.mul (dialU k q) (dialU k q) = M2.sub (M2.smul k (dialU k q)) (M2.smul q M2.one)

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_product
proofs.doc: (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 − q·ab)·I + (a + b + k·ab)·U: the landscape law, lifted.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (dialU k q))) = M2.add (M2.smul (1 - q * a * b) M2.one) (M2.smul (a + b + k * a * b) (dialU k q))

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_det
proofs.doc: det(I + aU) = 1 + k·a + q·a², the landscape's wall polynomial.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) = 1 + k * a + q * a * a

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_det_eigen
proofs.doc: With eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂ (k = λ₁ + λ₂, q = λ₁λ₂) the walls are a = −1/λᵢ.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU (l1 + l2) (l1 * l2)))) = (1 + a * l1) * (1 + a * l2)

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_discriminant
proofs.doc: The three countries are the sign of the discriminant, the squared eigenvalue gap.

proofs.name: DialSweep.or_line
proofs.doc: The "or" line: a wall at certainty a = 1 exactly when 1 + k + q = 0.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul 1 (dialU k q))) = 1 + k + q

proofs.name: DialSweep.unitU_sq
proofs.statement: M2.mul (unitU κ) (unitU κ) = M2.smul κ M2.one

proofs.name: DialSweep.unit_product
proofs.doc: (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 + κ·ab)·I + (a + b)·U: projected, (a + b)/(1 + κ·ab).
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (unitU κ))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (unitU κ))) = M2.add (M2.smul (1 + κ * a * b) M2.one) (M2.smul (a + b) (unitU κ))

proofs.name: DialSweep.boost_walls
proofs.doc: κ = 1 (boosts): det(I + aU) = (1 − a)(1 + a), walls at the speed of light ±1.

proofs.name: DialSweep.rotation_no_wall
proofs.doc: κ = −1 (rotations): det(I + aU) = 1 + a², no real wall.

proofs.name: DialSweep.shear_is_add
proofs.doc: κ = 0 (shears): det(I + aU) = 1, and the law is plain addition.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (unitU 0))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (unitU 0))) = M2.add M2.one (M2.smul (a + b) (unitU 0))

proofs.name: DialSweep.kmadd_lift
proofs.statement: M2.add M2.one (M2.mul (kmadd kk x y) kk) = M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul x kk)) (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul y kk))

proofs.name: DialSweep.sylvester2
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul x kk)) = M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul kk x))

proofs.name: DialSweep.sylvester3
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.mul x kk)) = M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.mul kk x))

proofs.name: DialSweep.rank_one3
proofs.doc: A rank-one weight leaves no corner terms: det(I + u·vᵀ) = 1 + vᵀu.
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (outer3 u1 u2 u3 v1 v2 v3)) = 1 + (v1 * u1 + v2 * u2 + v3 * u3)

proofs.name: DialSweep.rank_one_dial3
proofs.doc: The matrix determinant lemma: det(I + A·u·vᵀ) = 1 + vᵀ·A·u.

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_charpoly2
proofs.doc: det(I + kA) = k²·p_A(−1/k) (2×2), for k ≠ 0.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k x)) = k * k * charpoly2 x (-1 / k)

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_charpoly3
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul k x)) = -(k * k * k) * charpoly3 x (-1 / k)

proofs.name: DialSweep.wall_iff_eigen2
proofs.doc: The matrix sits on the wall of weight k exactly when −1/k is an eigenvalue.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k x)) = 0 ↔ charpoly2 x (-1 / k) = 0

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_lens
proofs.doc: The landscape lens law comes out of the dial matrix: off the wall 1 − q·ab ≠ 0, (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 − q·ab)·(I + cU) with c = (a + b + k·ab)/(1 − q·ab).
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (dialU k q))) = M2.smul (1 - q * a * b) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul ((a + b + k * a * b) / (1 - q * a * b)) (dialU k q)))

proofs.name: DialSweep.cayley_weighted
proofs.doc: The weighted Cayley transform (I + kS)⁻¹(I − kS) is the Cayley transform of k·s.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.inv (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k (M2.skew s)))) (M2.sub M2.one (M2.smul k (M2.skew s))) = M2.cayley (k * s)

proofs.name: DialSweep.winv
proofs.doc: The weighted inverse: off the weighted wall, a ⊞ₖ (−a/(1 + k·a)) = 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.words_4
proofs.doc: Words of length 4 split by period: 4·M4 + 2·M2 + 1·M1 = k^4.
proofs.statement: 4 * M4 k + 2 * M2 k + M1 k = k * k * k * k

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.words_5
proofs.statement: 5 * M5 k + M1 k = k * k * k * k * k

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.words_6
proofs.statement: 6 * M6 k + 3 * M3 k + 2 * M2 k + M1 k = k * k * k * k * k * k

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.bose_all_zero
proofs.doc: k = +1: every necklace count from length 2 on is 0 (only ζ(s) is left).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.fermi_from_three
proofs.doc: k = -1: from length 3 on every count is 0; length 2 gives 1 (the ζ(2s) of ζ(s)/ζ(2s)).

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.cancel_half
proofs.doc: The cancellation: three contributors with one zero each cancel at k = -1/2.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.half_exponent
proofs.doc: k = 1/2: the exponent at ρ/2 is M2/k = -1/4, not a whole number, so a branch point.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.copies_len2
proofs.doc: Copies points, length 2: 2 m² M2(-1/m) = 1 + m.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.copies_len3
proofs.doc: Copies points, length 3: 3 m³ M3(-1/m) = m² - 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.unit_plus_multiple_ne_zero
proofs.doc: Rational root step: ±1 + m·A is never 0 for a whole m ≥ 2.

proofs.name: MultAdd.DialWall.one_contributor
proofs.doc: On the critical line ρ/N has real part 1/(2N); N'·ρ/N is back on the line only for N' = N.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.dmap_formula
proofs.statement: dmap Q t = dnum Q t / dden Q t

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.dmap_even
proofs.doc: Series squares, so the step is even.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.quotient_rule
proofs.doc: The quotient rule: N'D − ND' = 4t(1 − t²)(1 + (Q−1)t²).

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.crit_colour
proofs.doc: Critical points besides 0, ±1: where t² = 1/(1−Q), i.e. 1 + (Q−1)t² = 0.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.wall_one
proofs.doc: The perfect bond t = 1 absorbs under the parallel law.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.colour_bond
proofs.doc: The colouring bond v = −1 sits at t = 1/(1 − Q).

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.wall_colour
proofs.doc: The second wall: t = 1/(1 − Q) absorbs under the parallel law.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.colour_wall_doubles
proofs.doc: The parallel law doubles its own colouring wall to itself: the critical value of T.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.lift_mul
proofs.doc: **The lift turns parallel into multiplication.**
proofs.statement: lift Q (lens (Q - 2) (1 - Q) a b) = lift Q a * lift Q b

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.lift_weight
proofs.doc: The lift of a bond's transmissivity is 1/(1 + v) = e^{−K}.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.lift_dmap
proofs.doc: So one diamond step squares in t, then squares in the lift.
proofs.statement: lift Q (dmap Q t) = lift Q (t * t) * lift Q (t * t)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.disc_square
proofs.doc: **The bend's discriminant is a square**: p² − 4q = Q² on the "or" line.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.wall_gap
proofs.doc: The two walls 1 and 1/(1−Q) differ by −Q/(1−Q): they merge only at Q = 0.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.bend_recip
proofs.doc: The bend is the reciprocal of the second wall.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.fixed_factor
proofs.doc: **T(t) − t factors**: the nontrivial fixed points solve (Q−1)t³ + t² + t − 1 = 0.
proofs.statement: dnum Q t - t * dden Q t = -t * (t - 1) * ((Q - 1) * t ^ 3 + t ^ 2 + t - 1)

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.param_cubic
proofs.doc: Writing Q = (y−1)²(y+1) solves the cubic in y.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.param_fixed
proofs.doc: ... and t = 1/y solves the fixed-point cubic.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.dmap_fixed_param
proofs.doc: **Every nontrivial fixed point is t = 1/y with Q = (y−1)²(y+1).**

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.crs_cubic
proofs.doc: The fixed point in the Chang–Roeder–Shrock form q² + 2qv − v³ = 0, v = y² − 1.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.dden_at_fixed
proofs.doc: At a nontrivial fixed point the denominator factors: D = (1 + t)²(1 − t).

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.slope_at_fixed
proofs.doc: **The slope at every nontrivial fixed point is 4/(1 + t)².**

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.golden_slope
proofs.doc: Percolation (Q = 1): at the golden point t² = 1 − t the slope is 4 − 4t.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.ising_slope
proofs.doc: Ising (Q = 2, tribonacci point t³ + t² + t = 1): slope 4/(1 + t)².

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.fold_identity
proofs.doc: **The fold**: Q(y) = (y−1)²(y+1) touches 32/27 at y = −1/3.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.fold_ferro_fixed
proofs.doc: At Q = 32/27 the ferromagnetic point is t* = 3/5 (y = 5/3), slope 25/16.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.fold_neutral
proofs.doc: At the fold the slope factor 2y/(y + 1) is −1: neutral.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.attract_identity
proofs.doc: Attracting exactly when (1 − y)(1 + 3y) > 0: (y + 1)² − (2y)² = (1 − y)(1 + 3y).

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.fold_point
proofs.doc: The fold point in t and in x = e^K: t = 1/y = −3 and x = y² = 1/9.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_zero_map
proofs.doc: Q = 0, where the two walls merge (p² = 4q): T = 2t²/(1 + t²) ...

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_zero_double
proofs.doc: ... whose fixed point t = 1 is double: T(t) − t = −t(t − 1)²/(1 + t²) ...

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_zero_parabolic
proofs.doc: ... and parabolic: the derivative 4t/(1 + t²)² of 2t²/(1 + t²) is 1 at t = 1.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_one_poly
proofs.doc: Q = 1: the second wall moves to infinity, the series wall, and T is a polynomial.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_two_inversion
proofs.doc: Q = 2: walls 0, ∞, 1, −1 are harmonic and T(1/t) = T(t).

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.q_three_mirror
proofs.doc: Q = 3: the colouring wall −1/2 is the mirror of the critical point 1/2, so it lands on it.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.mirror_only_three
proofs.doc: The colouring wall mirrors the critical point (1/(1−Q) = −1/y) only for y = 2, i.e. Q = 3.

proofs.name: DiamondLattice.parallel_weights
proofs.doc: The mult-add tie: parallel joins bond weights by mult-add, so the lift 1 + v multiplies.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.rmul_form
proofs.doc: Turns keep the conic: form(uv) = form(u)·form(v).
proofs.statement: form K (rmul K u v) = form K u * form K v

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.rmul_comm
proofs.statement: rmul K u v = rmul K v u

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.rmul_assoc
proofs.statement: rmul K (rmul K u v) w = rmul K u (rmul K v w)

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.central_chart
proofs.doc: Central chart, cleared of denominators: if s₁ = r₁c₁ and s₂ = r₂c₂ then the turned point has x = c₁c₂(r₁ + r₂) and t = c₁c₂(1 − K r₁ r₂), so x/t = F(0, K)(r₁, r₂).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.central_chart_unit
proofs.doc: The same with the chart point written as (1, r): (1, r₁)(1, r₂) = (1 − K r₁r₂, r₁ + r₂).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.flat_adds
proofs.doc: Flat case K = 0: the line t = 1 is carried to itself and chart values add (Galilean shear).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.sphere_closed
proofs.doc: Sphere K = 1: the unit circle is closed under turns (complex multiplication).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.hyperbola_closed
proofs.doc: Hyperbola K = −1: t² − x² = 1 is closed under boosts.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.dbl_is_self
proofs.doc: Doubling is the law applied to (a, a).
proofs.statement: dN a = a + a ∧ dD q a = 1 - q * a * a

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.dbl_num
proofs.doc: The doubled numerators combine to the doubled sum: 2a(1 − qb²) + 2b(1 − qa²) = 2(a + b)(1 − qab).
proofs.statement: dN a * dD q b + dN b * dD q a = dN (a + b) * (1 - q * a * b)

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.dbl_den
proofs.doc: ... and the denominators: (1 − qa²)(1 − qb²) − q(2a)(2b) = (1 − qab)² − q(a + b)².
proofs.statement: dD q a * dD q b - q * dN a * dN b = (1 - q * a * b) * (1 - q * a * b) - q * (a + b) * (a + b)

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.dbl_of_sum
proofs.doc: Together, dbl_num and dbl_den say doubling respects the law: dbl(F(a,b)) has numerator 2(a + b)(1 − qab) and denominator (1 − qab)² − q(a + b)², the same as F(dbl a, dbl b) after clearing (1 − qa²)(1 − qb²). Here is the doubled sum itself, cleared by (1 − qab)².
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.poincare_klein
proofs.doc: Poincaré to Klein (q = −1): r_K = 2r_P/(1 + r_P²) is the doubling of the velocity law.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.stereo_gnomonic
proofs.doc: Stereographic to gnomonic (q = 1): tan θ = 2 tan(θ/2)/(1 − tan²(θ/2)).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.curv_chart_free
proofs.doc: Chart changes x ↦ x/(1 − cx) move (p, q) to (p + 2c, q + pc + c²) and keep 4q − p².
proofs.statement: curv4 (p + 2 * c) (q + p * c + c * c) = curv4 p q

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.curv_scale
proofs.doc: Scaling the line by λ scales the curvature by λ² (so the radius by 1/λ).
proofs.statement: curv4 (l * p) (l * l * q) = l * l * curv4 p q

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.multAdd_curv
proofs.doc: Mult-add: conformal curvature −1 (the half plane), projective curvature −1/4.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.dial_curv
proofs.doc: The dial line: curvature −k², flat only at k = 0.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.tan_vel_curv
proofs.doc: Tangent addition (0, 1) is a sphere, velocity addition (0, −1) a hyperbolic plane.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.parity_curv
proofs.doc: Parity (−2, 0) has the same curvature as velocity addition.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.walls_curv
proofs.doc: With walls 1/u and 1/v (so p = −(u+v), q = uv), 4q − p² = −(u − v)²: real walls mean negative curvature.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.cr_base
proofs.doc: With 0 as base point: CR(0, x; P, Q) = P(x − Q)/(Q(x − P)).
proofs.statement: CR 0 x P Q = (P * (x - Q)) / (Q * (x - P))

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.cr_num
proofs.doc: With walls P = 1/u and Q = 1/v the two halves are the lens factors: P(x − Q) = −PQ(1 − vx) ...

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.cr_den
proofs.doc: ... and Q(x − P) = −PQ(1 − ux), so CR(0, x; 1/u, 1/v) = (1 − vx)/(1 − ux), the lens.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.lens_factor
proofs.doc: The lens multiplies under the law (numerator form): with p = −(u+v), q = uv, 1 − qab − v(a + b + pab) = (1 − va)(1 − vb).

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.halfplane_isometry
proofs.doc: Dilations keep the half-plane metric (dX² + dY²)/Y² (cleared: λ²(dx² + dy²)·y² = (dx² + dy²)·(λy)²).
proofs.statement: (l * dx) * (l * dx) * (y * y) + (l * dy) * (l * dy) * (y * y) = (dx * dx + dy * dy) * ((l * y) * (l * y))

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.halfplane_horizon
proofs.doc: The wall x = −1 is the horizon y = 0, and dilations never move it.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.mobius_collinear
proofs.doc: Möbius (Poincaré) addition of collinear a, b: ((1 + 2ab + b²)a + (1 − a²)b)/(1 + 2ab + a²b²) equals (a + b)/(1 + ab), cleared of denominators.

proofs.name: DiffGeometry.mobius_den
proofs.doc: Its denominator is the square (1 + ab)².

proofs.name: Dynamics.msq_lift
proofs.doc: The lift conjugates mult-add squaring to z ↦ z².
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Dynamics.pow_mul_R
proofs.doc: (a^m)^n = a^(mn) for any commutative ring.

proofs.name: Dynamics.iter_msq_lift
proofs.doc: n steps: 1 + fⁿ(x) = (1 + x)^(2ⁿ).
proofs.statement: 1 + iter msq n x = (1 + x) ^ (2 ^ n)

proofs.name: Dynamics.mpow_mpow
proofs.doc: Mult-add powers compose like ordinary powers: (x^(✳m))^(✳n) = x^(✳mn).
proofs.statement: mpow (mpow x m) n = mpow x (m * n)

proofs.name: Dynamics.dial_square_units
proofs.doc: Every dial square is mult-add squaring in other units: k·(x ✳ₖ x) = (kx) ✳ (kx).
proofs.statement: k * wAdd k x x = msq (k * x)

proofs.name: Dynamics.dial_power_units
proofs.doc: Dial powers too: k·x^(✳ₖn) = (kx)^(✳n).
proofs.statement: k * wpow k x n = mpow (k * x) n

proofs.name: Dynamics.parity_logistic
proofs.doc: k = −2 (parity): the dial square is the logistic map at r = 2.

proofs.name: Dynamics.failure_square
proofs.doc: k = −1 (failure union): the dial square is 1 − (1 − x)².

proofs.name: Dynamics.wall_superattracting
proofs.doc: The wall is superattracting: (−1 + h) ✳ (−1 + h) = −1 + h² (multiplier 0).

proofs.name: Dynamics.identity_repelling
proofs.doc: The identity repels: h ✳ h = 2h + h² (multiplier 2).

proofs.name: Dynamics.iter_wall
proofs.doc: The wall stays put under every iterate.

proofs.name: Dynamics.iter_zero
proofs.doc: So does the identity.

proofs.name: Dynamics.periodic_iff
proofs.doc: Periodic points: fⁿ(x) = x exactly when (1 + x)^(2ⁿ) = 1 + x.
proofs.statement: iter msq n x = x ↔ (1 + x) ^ (2 ^ n) = 1 + x

proofs.name: Dynamics.wall_fixed_mpow
proofs.doc: Higher mult-add powers: the wall is fixed by x ↦ x^(✳(n+1)).

proofs.name: Dynamics.iter_jet_fst
proofs.statement: (iter msqJet n p).1 = iter msq n p.1

proofs.name: Dynamics.iter_jet_ruler
proofs.doc: In the log ruler L = log(1+x) every step doubles slopes: the slope of fⁿ divided by 1 + fⁿ(x) is 2ⁿ times the starting slope divided by 1 + x (Lyapunov exponent log 2).
proofs.statement: (iter msqJet n p).2 * (1 + p.1) = 2 ^ n * p.2 * (1 + (iter msqJet n p).1)

proofs.name: Dynamics.flow_time_law
proofs.doc: Flows: running y′ = 1 + y for time s then t is mult-adding the two lifts' parts: (a ✳ (e₁ − 1)) ✳ (e₂ − 1) = a ✳ (e₁e₂ − 1), with eᵢ = e^(tᵢ).

proofs.name: Dynamics.cheb_joukowski
proofs.doc: If 2u = z + z⁻¹ then 2·Tₙ(u) = zⁿ + z⁻ⁿ.
proofs.statement: 2 * cheb u n = z ^ n + zi ^ n ∧ 2 * cheb u (n + 1) = z ^ (n + 1) + zi ^ (n + 1)

proofs.name: Dynamics.logistic_T2
proofs.doc: The logistic map at r = 4, read in u = 1 − 2x, is T₂.

proofs.name: Dynamics.cheb_comp
proofs.doc: Chebyshev maps commute like powers: T₂ ∘ T₃ = T₃ ∘ T₂ = T₆.
proofs.statement: cheb (cheb u 3) 2 = cheb u 6 ∧ cheb (cheb u 2) 3 = cheb u 6

proofs.name: Dynamics.sum_is_neg_product
proofs.doc: Since w ✳ ι(w) = 0, the sum and product of w and its inverse are negatives.

proofs.name: Dynamics.inv_inv
proofs.doc: The mult-add inverse undoes itself.

proofs.name: Dynamics.fold_inv
proofs.doc: The fold is 2-to-1: w and ι(w) land on the same point.

proofs.name: Dynamics.msq_inv
proofs.doc: Squaring commutes with the inverse: ι(w) ✳ ι(w) = ι(w ✳ w).

proofs.name: Dynamics.logistic_fold
proofs.doc: The logistic map at r = 4 is mult-add squaring folded: 4X(1 − X) = X(w ✳ w).
proofs.statement: 4 * fold w * (1 - fold w) = fold (msq w)

proofs.name: Dynamics.joukowski_multAdd
proofs.doc: Joukowski in mult-add terms: z + 1/z = 2 + (w + ι(w)) for z = 1 + w.

proofs.name: Dynamics.dial_wall_superattracting
proofs.doc: The dial's wall −1/k is the superattracting fixed point of x ✳ₖ x.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (-1 / k + h) (-1 / k + h) = -1 / k + k * h * h

proofs.name: Dynamics.pflow_add
proofs.statement: pflow s (pflow t x) = pflow (s + t) x

proofs.name: Dynamics.pflow_ruler
proofs.doc: Its Abel ruler −2/x adds the time: −2/φₜ(x) = −2/x + t (Fatou's coordinate, exactly).

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.layer_mul_fact
proofs.doc: **Picking with order.** C(n,k)·k! = n(n-1)…(n-k+1).
proofs.statement: ∀ k, layer n k * fact k = fall n k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.fall_le_pow
proofs.statement: ∀ k, fall n k ≤ n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.layer_fact_le
proofs.doc: **The layer bound.** C(n,k)·k! ≤ nᵏ: distinct picks are at most all picks.
proofs.statement: layer n k * fact k ≤ n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.collisions
proofs.doc: **Collisions are few.** n·nᵏ ≤ n·fall n k + C(k,2)·nᵏ: the ordered picks that repeat an axis number at most C(k,2)·nᵏ⁻¹.
proofs.statement: ∀ k, k ≤ n → n * n ^ k ≤ n * fall n k + tri k * n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.bernoulli
proofs.doc: **Bernoulli, with room to spare.** (c+1)^(k+2) + (k+1)(c+1)^k ≤ c^(k+2) + (k+2)(c+1)^(k+1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_nat_lt
proofs.doc: **The staircase climbs** (cleared of fractions): (n+1)^(2n+1) < nⁿ·(n+2)^(n+1) for n ≥ 1, i.e. (1+1/n)ⁿ < (1+1/(n+1))ⁿ⁺¹.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_add
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum (fun k => f k + g k) m = rsum f m + rsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_mul
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum (fun k => c * f k) m = c * rsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_shift
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum f (m + 1) = f 0 + rsum (fun k => f (k + 1)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_le
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → f k ≤ g k) → rsum f m ≤ rsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_nonneg
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → 0 ≤ f k) → 0 ≤ rsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_mono
proofs.doc: More nonnegative terms, bigger sum.
proofs.statement: rsum f m ≤ rsum f m'

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.binomial
proofs.doc: **The cube's corner count.** (1 + x)ⁿ = Σₖ C(n,k)·xᵏ.
proofs.statement: (1 + x) ^ n = rsum (fun k => (layer n k : Rat) * x ^ k) (n + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.natcast_ne
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.inv_pow_mul
proofs.statement: ∀ k : Nat, (1 / N) ^ k * N ^ k = 1

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.wt_le
proofs.doc: **Each layer is at most 1/k!.** C(n,k)/nᵏ ≤ 1/k!.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.wt_ge
proofs.doc: **Each layer is at least 1/k! minus its collisions.** 1/k! ≤ C(n,k)/nᵏ + C(k,2)/(n·k!).
proofs.statement: 1 / (fact k : Rat) ≤ wt n k + (tri k : Rat) / ((n : Rat) * (fact k : Rat))

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.s_lt_three
proofs.doc: **The partial sums never reach 3.**

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.u_step
proofs.doc: **The upper partner only comes down.** u (N+1) ≤ u N for N ≥ 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_le_u
proofs.doc: **The ceiling.** Every step of the staircase sits under every u N.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.s_le_stair
proofs.doc: **The floor.** For n ≥ N, the staircase is within 3·C(N,2)/n of s N.
proofs.statement: s N - 3 * (tri N : Rat) / (n : Rat) ≤ stair n

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_lt_succ
proofs.doc: **The staircase climbs.** (1 + 1/n)ⁿ < (1 + 1/(n+1))ⁿ⁺¹ for n ≥ 1.

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.nonempty_subsets
proofs.doc: non-empty choices: a set of m things has 2^m − 1 non-empty subsets; joining two separate sets combines those counts by mult-add (pick from either, or both, but not nothing)
proofs.statement: multAdd ((2 : Int) ^ m - 1) ((2 : Int) ^ n - 1) = (2 : Int) ^ (m + n) - 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.product_error
proofs.doc: relative errors in a product combine by mult-add, exactly (the textbook rule "they add" is the k = 0 shadow that drops the corner e₁e₂)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.product_error_corner
proofs.doc: the corner that the first-order rule drops
proofs.statement: multAdd e1 e2 - (e1 + e2) = e1 * e2

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.constant_product
proofs.doc: if one factor of a constant product grows by a, the other must change by b with a ⊞ b = 0: the lever (weight × arm) and Boyle (pressure × volume) are the same picture
proofs.statement: (P * (1 + a)) * (V * (1 + b)) = P * V ↔ multAdd a b = 0

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.boyle_partner
proofs.doc: on a field the partner change is the mult-add inverse −a/(1 + a)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.boyle_gain_loss
proofs.doc: pressure gains combine at k = +1 while the matching volume losses combine at k = −1: if (1 + a)(1 − d₁) = 1 and (1 + b)(1 − d₂) = 1 then the totals match the same way
proofs.statement: (1 + multAdd a b) * (1 - wAdd (-1) d1 d2) = 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.kepler_third
proofs.doc: T² ∝ a³ on percent changes: (1 + t)² = (1 + α)³ is t ⊞ t = α ⊞ α ⊞ α (the square's gnomon equals the cube's layers)
proofs.statement: (1 + t) * (1 + t) = (1 + α) * (1 + α) * (1 + α) ↔ multAdd t t = multAdd (multAdd α α) α

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.inverse_square
proofs.doc: gravity: when the distance grows by ρ the force changes by the mult-add inverse of ρ ⊞ ρ

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.cooling
proofs.doc: each step closes a fraction a of the temperature gap; after n steps the part closed is 1 − (1 − a)ⁿ, the union-of-failures power

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.lenses_in_contact
proofs.doc: two lenses in contact: powers add (the point (0, 0))

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.lenses_apart
proofs.doc: two lenses a distance d apart: total power P₁ + P₂ − d·P₁P₂, weighted mult-add at k = −d

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.squeeze_multiplies
proofs.doc: each lens's squeeze factor 1 − d·P (how much a parallel beam narrows over the gap) multiplies

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.field_lens
proofs.doc: the wall: a first lens that focuses exactly on the second (d·P₁ = 1) makes the second lens change nothing: the field lens of telescope eyepieces

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.parallel_is_inverted_addition
proofs.doc: parallel resistors (or springs in series, capacitors in series) are addition read through the inversion lens x ↦ 1/x: (RS/(R + S))·(1/R + 1/S) = 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_fib
proofs.doc: n sections ending in a short circuit give F(2n)/F(2n − 1): 1, 3/2, 8/5, 21/13, ...

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_walls
proofs.doc: the walls of one section are its fixed points: Z = (1 + 2Z)/(1 + Z) ⇔ Z² = Z + 1, the golden ratio and −1/golden ratio (two real walls)
proofs.statement: (2 * n + d) * d = n * (n + d) ↔ n * n = n * d + d * d

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_hyperbola
proofs.doc: every ladder value sits on the hyperbola n² − nd − d² = −1, which hugs the golden wall: so Z² − Z − 1 = −1/d² and the ladder walks into the wall
proofs.statement: (ladder k).1 * (ladder k).1 - (ladder k).1 * (ladder k).2 - (ladder k).2 * (ladder k).2 = -1

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.wave_cross_zero_iff
proofs.doc: Cross-term coefficient of ∂_X∂_T in ∂_t² − c²∂_x² after the dial boost (divided by −2g²).

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.galilean_cross
proofs.doc: Galilean boosts (q = 0) leave a cross term −2g²v: the wave equation is not Galilean.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.wave_speed_kept
proofs.doc: At c²q = −1 the T-T coefficient is −1/c² times the X-X coefficient: same wave speed.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.EB.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.gam_sq
proofs.doc: γ² − (γv)² = 1.
proofs.statement: gam D * gam D - gv D * gv D = 1

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.lc_plus
proofs.doc: **Light-cone part 1**: E_y + B_z is scaled by 1/D.
proofs.statement: (boost D f).ey + (boost D f).bz = (f.ey + f.bz) / D

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.lc_minus
proofs.doc: **Light-cone part 2**: E_y − B_z is scaled by D.
proofs.statement: (boost D f).ey - (boost D f).bz = D * (f.ey - f.bz)

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.lc_pair2
proofs.doc: The other pair: E_z − B_y scaled by 1/D, E_z + B_y by D.
proofs.statement: (boost D f).ez - (boost D f).by_ = (f.ez - f.by_) / D ∧ (boost D f).ez + (boost D f).by_ = D * (f.ez + f.by_)

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.lc_ratio
proofs.doc: The ratio of the two light-cone parts is multiplied by D², the mult-add lift.
proofs.statement: ((boost D f).ey - (boost D f).bz) * (f.ey + f.bz) = (D * D) * ((f.ey - f.bz) * ((boost D f).ey + (boost D f).bz))

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.dop_vD
proofs.doc: D² is the lift of the speed: D² = (1 + v)/(1 − v), and dop v = D² − 1.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.doppler_multAdd
proofs.doc: **D² − 1 composes by mult-add**: (D₁D₂)² − 1 = (D₁² − 1) ✳ (D₂² − 1).

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.dop_compose
proofs.doc: So the field's light-cone ratio, under two boosts, rides the mult-add of the two d's.
proofs.statement: dop (vD (D1 * D2)) = dop (vD D1) ✳ dop (vD D2)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.vD_mul
proofs.doc: **Speeds of composed boosts add by Einstein's rule**: v(D₁D₂) = v(D₁) ⊕ v(D₂).

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.inv1_boost
proofs.doc: **E² − B² is the same in every frame.**

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.inv2_boost
proofs.doc: **E·B is the same in every frame.**

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.null_stays_null
proofs.doc: Light stays light: a null field (E² = B², E ⊥ B) is null in every frame.
proofs.statement: inv1 (boost D f) = 0 ∧ inv2 (boost D f) = 0
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.wave_boost
proofs.doc: **The wave's amplitude is Doppler-shifted**: after the boost it is the wave of amplitude a/D.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.wave_energy
proofs.doc: Its energy density (E² + B²)/2 = a² is divided by D², the inverse mult-add lift.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.purcell
proofs.doc: **Magnetism from electricity**: a pure E_y, boosted, gets B_z = −γv E_y.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.maC_conj
proofs.doc: **a ✳ ā = |1 + a|² − 1** (real): so a is a unit phase exactly when a ✳ ā = 0.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.maC_lift
proofs.doc: The lift of a ✳ b is the product of lifts (complex multiplication).
proofs.statement: C.add C.one (maC a b) = C.mul (C.add C.one a) (C.add C.one b)

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.nsq_mul
proofs.doc: |xy|² = |x|²|y|² for complex pairs.
proofs.statement: C.nsq (C.mul u w) = C.nsq u * C.nsq w

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.phase_closed
proofs.doc: **Unit phases are closed under mult-add**: if a ✳ ā = 0 and b ✳ b̄ = 0, the same holds for a ✳ b.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.wall_not_phase
proofs.doc: The wall a = −1 is never a phase: |1 + (−1)|² = 0.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.maS_conj
proofs.doc: **The boost version of the same rule**: a ✳ ā = (|1 + a|²_Lorentz − 1).

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.maS_lift
proofs.statement: S.add S.one (maS a b) = S.mul (S.add S.one a) (S.add S.one b)

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.S_nsq_mul
proofs.statement: S.nsq (S.mul u w) = S.nsq u * S.nsq w

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.boost_closed
proofs.doc: Boosts (a ✳ ā = 0 in the split plane) are closed under mult-add too.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.half_charts
proofs.doc: Half-angle charts: (1 + i t₁)(1 + i t₂) = (1 − t₁t₂) + i(t₁ + t₂) and (1 + j s₁)(1 + j s₂) = (1 + s₁s₂) + j(s₁ + s₂): the landscape law at q = +1 and q = −1.
proofs.statement: TwistedBoosts.C.mul ⟨1, t1⟩ ⟨1, t2⟩ = ⟨1 - t1 * t2, t1 + t2⟩ ∧ S.mul ⟨1, t1⟩ ⟨1, t2⟩ = ⟨1 + t1 * t2, t1 + t2⟩

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.plaquette
proofs.doc: **A plaquette is the mult-add of its links**, the two backward links entering as mult-add inverses: 1 + (a₁ ✳ a₂ ✳ a₃⁻ ✳ a₄⁻) = (1 + a₁)(1 + a₂)/((1 + a₃)(1 + a₄)).
proofs.statement: 1 + (a1 ✳ a2 ✳ multAddInv a3 ✳ multAddInv a4) = (1 + a1) * (1 + a2) / ((1 + a3) * (1 + a4))

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.stokes
proofs.doc: **Discrete Stokes**: with link lifts b₁, s, t₁, l (left square) and b₂, r, t₂, s (right square, sharing s), the two plaquettes multiply to the big rectangle and the shared link cancels.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.stokes_multAdd
proofs.doc: In mult-add form: the big loop's value is the ✳ of the two plaquette values.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.charge_conserved
proofs.doc: **k_μ k_ν F^{μν} = 0 for any antisymmetric F**: in momentum space, k·J = 0 follows from J = k·F alone.
proofs.statement: sum4 (fun i => sum4 (fun j => k i * k j * F i j)) = 0

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.bi_cap
proofs.doc: With E² = b²D²/(b² + D²), the field stays below the wall b² (stated with the positive denominator cleared): b²·D² < b²·(b² + D²).
proofs.statement: b * b * (D * D) < b * b * (b * b + D * D)

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.bi_den_pos
proofs.doc: The denominator b² + D² is positive.

proofs.name: Electromagnetism.bi_inverse
proofs.doc: And the exact inverse: with e = E²/b² = D²/(b² + D²), D²/b² = e/(1 − e).

proofs.name: EllipticLead.node_param
proofs.doc: every line y = t·x through the double point meets the curve again at x = t² + a1 t − a2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.walls_are_branches
proofs.doc: the walls are the node's branches: with z = −1/t (so z·t = −1), t²·(1 + k z + q z²) − (t² + a1 t − a2) is a multiple of (z t + 1), with k = −a1, q = −a2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.slopes_factor
proofs.doc: the two tangent slopes m1, m2 factor the slope polynomial: a1 = −(m1+m2), a2 = −m1·m2, so k = m1 + m2 and q = m1·m2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.wall_poly_factor
proofs.doc: the wall polynomial in z factors through the branches: 1 + k z + q z² = (1 + m1 z)(1 + m2 z)

proofs.name: EllipticLead.slope_discriminant
proofs.doc: discriminant of the slopes equals the map's k² − 4q

proofs.name: EllipticLead.nodal_w
proofs.doc: the nodal curve's formal group: w = −1/y as a function of z is rational, w·(1 − a1 z − a2 z²) = z³ is the curve equation w = z³ + a1 z w + a2 z² w
proofs.statement: w = z * z * z + a1 * z * w + a2 * z * z * w

proofs.name: EllipticLead.tate_q0_law
proofs.doc: with z = 1 − v (v = 1/u, Tate's parameter inverted), the law z1 + z2 − z1 z2 is v1·v2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.tate_q0_is_multAdd
proofs.doc: and a = −z turns it into mult-add exactly

proofs.name: EllipticLead.d4_weight
proofs.statement: d4 (u * a1) (u * u * a2) (u * u * u * a3) (u * u * u * u * a4) = u * u * u * u * d4 a1 a2 a3 a4

proofs.name: EllipticLead.d5_weight
proofs.statement: d5 (u * a1) (u * u * a2) (u * u * u * a3) (u * u * u * u * a4) = u * u * u * u * u * d5 a1 a2 a3 a4

proofs.name: EllipticLead.multAdd_curve_d
proofs.doc: mult-add's own curve (a1 = −1, a2 = a3 = a4 = 0) has d_n = (−1)^n: the differential dz/(1+z), the log of mult-add, through layer 6

proofs.name: EllipticLead.ochanine_nodal_num
proofs.doc: Ochanine's elliptic genus at ε = δ² (the nodal case): numerator a√R(b) + b√R(a) with √R(x) = 1 − δx² equals (a + b)(1 − δab), so the law is (a + b)/(1 + δab): the signature at δ = 1

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_discriminant
proofs.doc: Frey curve y² = x(x − A)(x + B) = x³ + (B − A)x² − AB·x: 16 × discriminant of the cubic

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_c4
proofs.doc: c4 = b2² − 24 b4 with b2 = 4(B − A), b4 = −2AB

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_c4_at_A
proofs.doc: semistable: at a prime dividing A (A ≡ 0) c4/16 is B²; dividing A + B (B ≡ −A) it is A². Either is nonzero mod the prime when gcd(A, B) = 1, so the reduction is a node, never a cusp.

proofs.name: EllipticLead.euler_factor_walls
proofs.doc: Euler factors are wall polynomials: 1 − a T + p T² = (1 − αT)(1 − βT) when a = α + β, p = αβ

proofs.name: EllipticLead.hasse_turning
proofs.doc: Hasse (a² < 4p) puts the point (k, q) = (−a, p) in the turning country: k² − 4q < 0

proofs.name: EllipticLead.euler_units
proofs.doc: units: scaling T by λ moves (k, q) to (λk, λ²q), the landscape's units action
proofs.statement: 1 + k * (lam * T) + q * (lam * T) * (lam * T) = 1 + (lam * k) * T + (lam * lam * q) * T * T

proofs.name: EllipticLead.gap6_whole
proofs.doc: no other whole rung passes layer 6

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_shift_one
proofs.doc: one-step shift: U(a+1)U(a+e) − U(a)U(a+e+1) = Q^a · U(e)
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (a + 1) * lucas P Q (a + e) - lucas P Q a * lucas P Q (a + e + 1) = Q ^ a * lucas P Q e

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_exchange_pair
proofs.doc: the general exchange identity: U(a+c)U(a+e) − U(a)U(a+e+c) = Q^a · U(c) · U(e)
proofs.statement: (lucas P Q (a + c) * lucas P Q (a + e) - lucas P Q a * lucas P Q (a + e + c) = Q ^ a * lucas P Q c * lucas P Q e) ∧ (lucas P Q (a + (c + 1)) * lucas P Q (a + e) - lucas P Q a * lucas P Q (a + e + (c + 1)) = Q ^ a * lucas P Q (c + 1) * lucas P Q e)

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_exchange
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (a + c) * lucas P Q (a + e) - lucas P Q a * lucas P Q (a + e + c) = Q ^ a * lucas P Q c * lucas P Q e
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_catalan
proofs.doc: Catalan's identity in the form used below: U(n+d)² − U(d)·U(2n+d) = Q^d · U(n)²
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (d + n) * lucas P Q (d + n) - lucas P Q d * lucas P Q (d + n + n) = Q ^ d * lucas P Q n * lucas P Q n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_eds
proofs.doc: **Lucas counting is elliptic counting, weighted by Q^(n−1).** Writing n = f + 1 and m = f + e + 2 (so m > n ≥ 1): Q^(n−1)·U(m+n)·U(m−n) = U(m+1)U(m−1)U(n)² − U(n+1)U(n−1)U(m)². This is the elliptic divisibility recurrence (with U(1) = 1), with the extra factor Q^(n−1).
proofs.statement: Q ^ f * (lucas P Q (2 * f + e + 3) * lucas P Q (e + 1)) = lucas P Q (f + e + 3) * lucas P Q (f + e + 1) * (lucas P Q (f + 1) * lucas P Q (f + 1)) - lucas P Q (f + 2) * lucas P Q f * (lucas P Q (f + e + 2) * lucas P Q (f + e + 2))

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_eds_unit
proofs.doc: with Q = 1 the Lucas sequence satisfies the elliptic divisibility recurrence exactly
proofs.statement: lucas P 1 (2 * f + e + 3) * lucas P 1 (e + 1) = lucas P 1 (f + e + 3) * lucas P 1 (f + e + 1) * (lucas P 1 (f + 1) * lucas P 1 (f + 1)) - lucas P 1 (f + 2) * lucas P 1 f * (lucas P 1 (f + e + 2) * lucas P 1 (f + e + 2))

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.lucas_somos4
proofs.doc: the Somos-4 edge (n = 2): Q·U(m+4)U(m) = P²·U(m+3)U(m+1) − (P² − Q)·U(m+2)²
proofs.statement: Q * (lucas P Q (m + 4) * lucas P Q m) = P * P * (lucas P Q (m + 3) * lucas P Q (m + 1)) - (P * P - Q) * (lucas P Q (m + 2) * lucas P Q (m + 2))

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.tate5_disc
proofs.doc: Tate normal form with a point of order 5: y² + (1−b)xy − by = x³ − bx². Its discriminant is b⁵(b² − 11b − 1), so it pinches only at b = 0 and b² = 11b + 1.

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.tate5_golden_pinch
proofs.doc: the pinch points b² − 11b − 1 = 0 are φ⁵ = 5φ + 3 and −φ⁻⁵ = 8 − 5φ, for any φ with φ² = φ + 1

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.golden_fifth_power
proofs.doc: and 5φ + 3 really is φ⁵

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_seeds
proofs.doc: the seeds are the curve's division polynomials at (0, 0): a = (0, 0, 1, −1, 0)

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_point
proofs.doc: (0, 0) is on y² + y = x³ − x

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_somos4
proofs.doc: Somos-4: W(n+4)W(n) = W(n+3)W(n+1) + W(n+2)²

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_eds
proofs.doc: the elliptic divisibility recurrence, for 1 ≤ n < m, m + n ≤ 24

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_strong_div
proofs.doc: strong divisibility, like Fibonacci: gcd(W m, W n) = |W gcd(m, n)|
proofs.statement: ∀ m, m < 21 → ∀ n, n < 21 → Int.gcd (w37 m) (w37 n) = (w37 (Nat.gcd m n)).natAbs

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.w37_odd_somos
proofs.doc: its odd terms are the classic Somos-4 numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 23, 59, 314, 1529, 8209 (up to sign)

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.order_five_points
proofs.doc: its multiples, all on the curve: P = (0,0), 2P = (1,−1), 3P = (1,0), 4P = (0,−1), and 3P = −2P, 4P = −P (negation is y ↦ −y − 1), so 5P = O

proofs.name: EllipticCounting.order_five_lines
proofs.doc: why: the tangent at P is y = 0, cutting x³ − x² = x²(x − 1), so −2P = (1, 0); the chord through P and 2P is y = −x, cutting x(x − 1)², so P + 2P = −(1, −1) = (1, 0)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_11
proofs.doc: top-left entry: (1 + ka)(1 + kb) − q a b = D + k N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_12
proofs.doc: top-right entry: (1 + ka) b + a = N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_21
proofs.doc: bottom-left entry: −q a (1 + kb) − q b = −q N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_22
proofs.doc: bottom-right entry: −q a b + 1 = D

proofs.name: EllipticS3.cayley_hamilton
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton for G: G² = kG − qI, entry by entry

proofs.name: EllipticS3.multAdd_is_1x1
proofs.doc: mult-add is the 1×1 case G = [1]: (1 + a)(1 + b) = 1 + (a ⊞ b)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.nonsplit_frob_is_inverse
proofs.doc: turning (non-split) torus: u^(p+1) = 1, so v = u^p satisfies v·u = 1 and the mult-add of v − 1 and u − 1 is 0: Frobenius sends the point to its mult-add inverse (a_p = −1)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.split_frob_fixes
proofs.doc: split torus: u^p = u, Frobenius fixes the lift (a_p = +1)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.quat_det_re
proofs.doc: det U: real part w² + x² + y² + z², imaginary part 0

proofs.name: EllipticS3.quat_discriminant
proofs.doc: trace U = 2w; its wall discriminant is −4 times the squared radius of its latitude 2-sphere: how deep a prime sits in the turning country is how big the sphere of rotations with its angle is

proofs.name: EllipticS3.middle_minus_neighbour
proofs.doc: middle layer minus its neighbour: 20 − 15 = 5 and 70 − 56 = 14

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.mul_bound
proofs.doc: |a·b| ≤ u whenever |a| ≤ u and |b| ≤ 1, written without `abs`.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.certainty_absorbs_iff
proofs.doc: Certainty swallows everything, a ⊕ₖ 1 = 1 for every a, exactly when k = −1. The statistics page's "or" laws are the line k + q_L = −1 of lens laws; the Tsallis laws have no denominator (q_L = 0), so they meet it only here.
proofs.statement: (∀ a : Rat, wAdd k a 1 = 1) ↔ k = -1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.escort_powers
proofs.doc: Raising every entry to a then to b is raising to a·b: escorts of escorts.
proofs.statement: (l.map (fun x => x ^ a)).map (fun y => y ^ b) = l.map (fun x => x ^ (a * b))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.lsum_div
proofs.statement: InfoFused.lsum (l.map (fun y => y / c)) = InfoFused.lsum l / c

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.div_pow'
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Nat, (x / c) ^ n = x ^ n / c ^ n

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.pow_ne_zero'
proofs.doc: Escort of an escort: P_b(P_a(p)) = P_{ab}(p), when the normalizers are nonzero.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.escort_escort
proofs.statement: escort b (escort a l) = escort (a * b) l

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_parseval
proofs.doc: Parseval on the tetrahedron: Σp² = (1 + |λ|²)/4.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.linear_entropy_choi
proofs.doc: The Choi state's linear entropy 1 − Σp² is (3 − |λ|²)/4: zero at the corners, largest (3/4) at the centre, constant on spheres about the centre.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.midsphere_iff
proofs.doc: Σp² ≤ ½ (collision entropy at least one bit) exactly inside the midsphere.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.edge_midpoint
proofs.doc: The edge midpoint (X with chance ½) is (1, 0, 0): on the cube's face, the sphere and the octahedron at once, with collision sum exactly ½.
proofs.statement: edgeMid.lx = 1 ∧ edgeMid.ly = 0 ∧ edgeMid.lz = 0 ∧ coll edgeMid = 1/2 ∧ len2 edgeMid = 1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.octahedron_in_ball
proofs.doc: Octahedron inside the ball: |x| + |y| + |z| ≤ 1 gives x² + y² + z² ≤ 1.
proofs.statement: x * x + y * y + z * z ≤ 1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.ball_in_cube
proofs.doc: Ball inside the cube.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.compose_stays_in_ball
proofs.doc: Composition multiplies coordinates (QuantumNoise.comp_lx …), and a coordinate of a real channel lies in [−1, 1]. So composing never leaves the ball …
proofs.statement: (ax * bx) * (ax * bx) + (ay * b_y) * (ay * b_y) + (az * bz) * (az * bz) ≤ ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.compose_stays_in_octahedron
proofs.doc: … nor the octahedron …
proofs.statement: (ax * bx ≤ u ∧ -(ax * bx) ≤ u) ∧ (ay * b_y ≤ v ∧ -(ay * b_y) ≤ v) ∧ (az * bz ≤ w ∧ -(az * bz) ≤ w)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.compose_stays_in_cube
proofs.doc: … nor any cube max|λᵢ| ≤ c about the centre (classical capacity cannot rise).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_series
proofs.doc: Series: the collision sum of a composed channel, through Parseval.
proofs.statement: coll (p.comp q) = (1 + (p.lx * q.lx) * (p.lx * q.lx) + (p.ly * q.ly) * (p.ly * q.ly) + (p.lz * q.lz) * (p.lz * q.lz)) / 4

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.map_sq_outer
proofs.statement: (InfoFused.outer xs ys).map (fun t => t * t) = InfoFused.outer (xs.map (fun t => t * t)) (ys.map (fun t => t * t))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_parallel
proofs.doc: Parallel (two qubits, independent faults): the 16 joint fault chances' collision sum is the product, so linear entropy composes by the union rule.
proofs.statement: InfoFused.lsum ((InfoFused.outer [p.i, p.x, p.y, p.z] [q.i, q.x, q.y, q.z]).map (fun t => t * t)) = coll p * coll q

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.depol_point
proofs.statement: (depol s).lx = 1 - 4/3 * s ∧ (depol s).ly = 1 - 4/3 * s ∧ (depol s).lz = 1 - 4/3 * s

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.diagonal_crossings
proofs.doc: Along the diagonal (λ, λ, λ) the octahedron's face is λ = 1/3 and the midsphere is λ² = 1/3, so the octahedron is strictly inside there.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.bit_collision
proofs.doc: One bit-flip channel's collision sum in the polarization λ = 1 − 2p.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.pattern_linear_entropy
proofs.doc: The n-fold fault pattern (a corner of the n-cube) has collision sum cⁿ, so its linear entropy climbs at weight −1: 1 − cⁿ = (1 − c)^{⊕₋₁ n}.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.cancellation_hides
proofs.doc: The net channel after n stacked flips is purer than its fault pattern: ((1 + x)/2)ⁿ ≤ (1 + xⁿ)/2 for x = λ² in [0, 1].

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.gap_two
proofs.doc: At n = 2 the purity gap is a perfect square.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.synd_antipodal
proofs.doc: Opposite corners give the same syndrome …
proofs.statement: ∀ a b c : Bool, synd (!a) (!b) (!c) = synd a b c

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.synd_diagonal
proofs.doc: … and corners with the same syndrome are equal or opposite: each syndrome is one body diagonal of the 3-cube.
proofs.statement: ∀ a b c d e f : Bool, synd a b c = synd d e f → (a = d ∧ b = e ∧ c = f) ∨ (a = !d ∧ b = !e ∧ c = !f)

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.syndromes_total
proofs.doc: No alarm: both ends of the main diagonal. Alarm: each of the three other diagonals.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.decoder_failure
proofs.doc: The vote picks the lighter end of each diagonal; the failures add up to the top two layers of the cube (QuantumNoise.maj3).

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.alarm_one_coin
proofs.doc: After an alarm, the leftover doubt is exactly one fresh coin of chance p.
proofs.statement: p * q * q / (p * q * q + p * p * q) = q

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.chain_rule_pair
proofs.doc: The chain rule on one diagonal, for any L with L(xy) = L(x) + L(y) (log is one): a·L(a) + b·L(b) = s·L(s) + [a·L(a/s) + b·L(b/s)] with s = a + b. Entropy of the faults = entropy of the syndrome + entropy left on the diagonal.
proofs.statement: a * L a + b * L b = (a + b) * L (a + b) + (a * L (a / (a + b)) + b * L (b / (a + b)))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.nishimori_tanh
proofs.doc: On the Nishimori line e^{−2K} = w = p/(1 − p). Then tanh K = (1 − w)/(1 + w) = 1 − 2p.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.kw_lens_polar
proofs.doc: The Kramers–Wannier lens M(t) = (1 − t)/(1 + t) sends λ = 1 − 2p to p/(1 − p).

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.frey_c6
proofs.doc: A1. 2·c6 of the Frey model is (A − B)(A + 2B)(2A + B).
proofs.statement: 2 * c6 (freyModel a2 a4) = (A - B) * (A + 2 * B) * (2 * A + B)

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.frey_j_identity
proofs.doc: A2. The polynomial identity behind j − 1728: 4c4³ − (2c6)² = 27(ABC)².

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.frey_c4_c6_disc
proofs.doc: A3. c4³ − c6² = 1728·Δ for the Frey model.
proofs.statement: (freyModel a2 a4).c4 ^ 3 - c6 (freyModel a2 a4) ^ 2 = 1728 * (freyModel a2 a4).disc

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.frey_j_denominator
proofs.doc: A4. No prime dividing Δ divides c4³, so j = c4³/Δ is in lowest terms with denominator Δ: every bad prime is a pole of j (potentially multiplicative reduction, Tate's curve).

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.odd_prime_coprime_256
proofs.doc: An odd prime does not divide 256 (so it can be cancelled from 256·Δ).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.frey_bad_primes
proofs.doc: B1. With A odd and 32 ∣ B, a prime divides Δ exactly when it divides ABC. Because the curve is semistable (FreyPieces 3e), its conductor is the product of these primes, rad(ABC) = rad(abc).
proofs.statement: (q : Int) ∣ (freyModel a2 a4).disc ↔ (q : Int) ∣ A * B * C

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.disc_two_part
proofs.doc: C1. If b = 2^v·m then ((a·b·c)²)^p = 256 · 2^(2pv − 8) · ((a·m·c)²)^p, once 2pv ≥ 8. With a, m, c odd this says the minimal discriminant (256·Δ = ((abc)²)^p) has exactly 2^(2pv − 8) as its 2-part.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.two_exponent_not_multiple
proofs.doc: C2. For a prime p ≥ 5 and v ≥ 1, p never divides 2pv − 8: the exponent of 2 in the minimal discriminant is never a multiple of p, so the mod-p representation stays ramified at 2 and the level cannot drop below 2. (The odd primes all drop: FreyPieces 3g.)

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.g12_table
proofs.doc: D2. 12·genus for N = 1, …, 13: zero except at 11 (genus 1, the first weight-2 cusp form).

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.squeeze
proofs.doc: E1. The squeeze: the four arrows leave no room for a counterexample.
proofs.statement: ∀ p a b c, ¬ Counterexample p a b c

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.flt_of_deep_arrows
proofs.doc: E2. With FermatRoute, the four arrows give Fermat's Last Theorem for every n ≥ 3.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.fake_passes_mod
proofs.doc: F1. No congruence can rule a counterexample out: for every modulus n ≠ 0 the fake triple (−1, 32n, −1) has a ≡ 3 mod 4, 32 ∣ b, gcd(a, b) = 1, abc ≠ 0, and a^p + b^p ≡ c^p mod n.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.germain_residues
proofs.doc: F2a. Fifth powers mod 11 are only 0, 1, 10.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.germain_mod_11
proofs.doc: F2b. Sophie Germain's auxiliary prime for p = 5: x⁵ + y⁵ = z⁵ forces 11 ∣ x, y or z. This pushes divisibility around (it is how case I is proved) but can never contradict: case II, where p divides abc, escapes every such prime.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.abc_lt_cube
proofs.doc: F3a. For a + b = c with a, b ≥ 1: abc < c³ (so rad of a Fermat triple is below c³).
proofs.statement: a * b * c < c * c * c

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.explicit_abc_kills
proofs.doc: F3b. An explicit abc bound of the shape c^p < (abc)² applied to (a^p, b^p, c^p) leaves only p < 6. (abc itself is not proved, so this is a conditional route, not a proof.)

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.sq_mod_five
proofs.doc: F4a. Squares mod 5 are 0, 1, 4.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.no_norm_two_three
proofs.doc: F4b. Lamé's gap (1847): in Z[√−5] nothing has norm x² + 5y² equal to 2 or 3, so 2 and 3 are irreducible there, yet 6 = 2·3 has the second factorisation (1 + √−5)(1 − √−5). Unique factorisation, which elementary descent needs, fails; for Fermat it fails in Z[ζ_p] from p = 23 on (class number of Q(ζ23) is 3, cited).

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.znorm_mul
proofs.doc: F4c. The norm is multiplicative.
proofs.statement: znorm (zmul x y) = znorm x * znorm y

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.six_two_ways
proofs.doc: F4d. The two factorisations of 6.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.irregular_37
proofs.doc: F5a. Kummer's gap: 37 divides the numerator 7709321041217 of B_32 (B_32 = −7709321041217/510), so 37 is irregular and Kummer's 1850 proof does not cover it.

proofs.name: CounterexampleMap.wieferich_1093_3511
proofs.doc: F5b. The Wieferich primes: 2^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p² for p = 1093 and 3511. Wieferich (1909) showed case I needs this; it holds for these two, so the criterion alone cannot finish.

proofs.name: FunctionalAnalysis.cube_zero_qi

proofs.name: GRBridges.boost_product
proofs.doc: The product (1 + β₁σ)(1 + β₂σ) with σ² = 1 has scalar part 1 + β₁β₂ and σ-part β₁ + β₂.

proofs.name: GRBridges.forward_part_multAdd
proofs.doc: The forward light-cone part (scalar + σ) of a product is 1 + (β₁ ✳ β₂).

proofs.name: GRBridges.backward_part_multAdd
proofs.doc: The backward light-cone part is 1 + ((−β₁) ✳ (−β₂)).

proofs.name: GRBridges.boost_norm
proofs.doc: The norm (1 + βσ)(1 − βσ) = 1 − β²: zero exactly at β = ±1, the wall (light speed).

proofs.name: GRBridges.sand_lift
proofs.doc: **The lift holds for every matrix weight k:** 1 + k(a ✳ b) = (1 + k a)(1 + k b).
proofs.statement: add one (mul k (sand k a b)) = mul (add one (mul k a)) (add one (mul k b))

proofs.name: GRBridges.sand_assoc
proofs.doc: **The sandwich law is associative for every k.**
proofs.statement: sand k (sand k a b) c = sand k a (sand k b c)

proofs.name: GRBridges.front_not_assoc
proofs.doc: The front-loaded law fails associativity for a non-central weight (explicit witness).

proofs.name: GRBridges.front_eq_sand_scalar
proofs.doc: A central (scalar) weight makes the front-loaded law agree with the sandwich law.
proofs.statement: front ⟨s, 0, 0, s⟩ a b = sand ⟨s, 0, 0, s⟩ a b

proofs.name: GRBridges.schur_factor
proofs.doc: (n−1)(n−2)/2 is 0 in dimension 2 and positive from dimension 3 on.

proofs.name: GRBridges.isotropic_einstein
proofs.doc: Isotropic curvature: G = ((n−1) − n(n−1)/2)·q·g = −(n−1)(n−2)/2·q·g.

proofs.name: GRBridges.bundle_area
proofs.doc: Bundle area from two transverse stretches.

proofs.name: GRBridges.flat_focusing
proofs.doc: Straight rays (a = αλ, b = βλ): the second difference of the area is the cross term 2αβ.

proofs.name: GRBridges.focusing_split
proofs.doc: Focusing split: θ²/2 + σ² = θ₁² + θ₂², with θ = θ₁ + θ₂ and σ² = (θ₁ − θ₂)²/2.

proofs.name: GRBridges.focusing_cross
proofs.doc: The cross term: θ² − (θ₁² + θ₂²) = 2θ₁θ₂ (the ab part of mult-add, in rates).

proofs.name: GRBridges.three_way_layers
proofs.doc: Three-way mult-add = sum + pairwise layer (e2) + triple layer.
proofs.statement: a ✳ (b ✳ c) = (a + b + c) + (a*b + b*c + c*a) + a*b*c

proofs.name: GRBridges.e2_from_traces
proofs.doc: e2 from traces: (tr K)² − tr K² = 2 e2.

proofs.name: GRBridges.spherical_shell
proofs.doc: Spherical river (rates v′, v/r, v/r, with q = v/r): r²·e2 = v² + 2 r v v′ = (r v²)′.

proofs.name: GRBridges.schwarzschild_constraint
proofs.doc: Schwarzschild river: radial rate p = −q/2 makes e2 vanish, (tr K)² = K·K.

proofs.name: GRBridges.aether_constraint
proofs.doc: Aether river: (1 + c₂)(tr K)² − (1 − c₁₃) K·K = (c₂ + c₁₃)(tr K)² when (tr K)² = K·K.

proofs.name: GRBridges.null_null_2d
proofs.doc: In a 2D slice, X(k,k) = 0 for both light directions k = (1, ±1) forces X₀₁ = 0, X₁₁ = −X₀₀ (X = φ·η).

proofs.name: GameTheory.dfold_lift
proofs.statement: 1 + k * dfold k l = prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + k * x))

proofs.name: GameTheory.dfold_append
proofs.statement: dfold k (S ++ T) = wAdd k (dfold k S) (dfold k T)

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_compose
proofs.doc: Two bets at fraction f: the returns combine by the dial with k = f.
proofs.statement: (1 + f * r₁) * (1 + f * r₂) = 1 + f * wAdd f r₁ r₂

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_many
proofs.doc: Many bets: wealth is 1 + f·(r₁ ✳_f r₂ ✳_f … ✳_f rₙ).
proofs.statement: prodL (rs.map (fun r => 1 + f * r)) = 1 + f * dfold f rs

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_stake
proofs.doc: In money terms the stakes' returns f·r mult-add plainly.
proofs.statement: f * wAdd f r₁ r₂ = (f * r₁) ✳ (f * r₂)

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_ruin
proofs.doc: Ruin is the wall: one outcome with f·r = −1 leaves nothing, whatever follows.

proofs.name: GameTheory.hedge_step
proofs.doc: One round on two experts: the new total is the old total plus ε times the algorithm's gain.

proofs.name: GameTheory.dial_game_union
proofs.doc: Sugeno's rule: disjoint coalitions combine by the dial. The excess over adding is the corner.
proofs.statement: dfold k (S ++ T) - dfold k S - dfold k T = k * dfold k S * dfold k T

proofs.name: GameTheory.marginal
proofs.doc: Joining coalition S is worth x·(1 + k·v(S)).
proofs.statement: dfold k (x :: S) - dfold k S = x * (1 + k * dfold k S)

proofs.name: GameTheory.corners3
proofs.doc: The three-player worth expanded over the cube: corners weighted by k^(size − 1).
proofs.statement: dfold k [x, y, z] = (x + y + z) + k * (x * y + x * z + y * z) + k * k * (x * y * z)

proofs.name: GameTheory.multilinear2
proofs.doc: Owen's multilinear extension, two players: everyone present with chance t gives the dial fold of t·x.
proofs.statement: (1 - t) * t * x + t * (1 - t) * y + t * t * wAdd k x y = wAdd k (t * x) (t * y)

proofs.name: GameTheory.multilinear3
proofs.doc: Three players.
proofs.statement: (1 - t) * (1 - t) * t * (x + y + z) + (1 - t) * t * t * (dfold k [x, y] + dfold k [x, z] + dfold k [y, z]) + t * t * t * dfold k [x, y, z] = dfold k [t * x, t * y, t * z]

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_win_lift
proofs.doc: Kelly's fraction f = p − q/b makes the win lift p(1 + b) (= p/π, π = 1/(1 + b)).

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_loss_lift
proofs.doc: … and the loss lift q(1 + b)/b (= q/(1 − π)).

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_ratio
proofs.doc: The bookmaker's chance π = 1/(1 + b): the win lift is your chance over theirs.

proofs.name: GameTheory.kelly_foc
proofs.doc: First-order condition: d/df [p log(1 + bf) + q log(1 − f)] = pb/(1 + bf) − q/(1 − f) vanishes.

proofs.name: GameTheory.odds_multAdd
proofs.doc: Odds multiply along a chain, so odds − 1 mult-adds.

proofs.name: GameTheory.edge_compose
proofs.doc: Edges compose like relativistic velocities: landscape point (k, q) = (0, −1).
proofs.statement: edge (O₁ * O₂) = (edge O₁ + edge O₂) / (1 + edge O₁ * edge O₂)

proofs.name: GameTheory.odds_is_lift
proofs.doc: The odds are the edge's lift (1 + s)/(1 − s): relativity's Doppler factor squared.

proofs.name: GameTheory.prob_compose
proofs.doc: Win chances compose by p₁p₂/(p₁p₂ + q₁q₂).
proofs.statement: prob (O₁ * O₂) = prob O₁ * prob O₂ / (prob O₁ * prob O₂ + (1 - prob O₁) * (1 - prob O₂))

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley2_eq
proofs.statement: shapley2 k x y = x + k * x * y / 2

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley2_efficient
proofs.statement: shapley2 k x y + shapley2 k y x = dfold k [x, y]

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley2_union
proofs.doc: k = −1, "some cause strikes": each cause keeps its own chance minus half the overlap (the actuarial UDD split).
proofs.statement: shapley2 (-1) x y = x - x * y / 2

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley3_eq
proofs.doc: Closed form: x·(1 + k·e₁/2 + k²·e₂/3) over the other two: each corner shared equally.
proofs.statement: shapley3 k x y z = x * (1 + k * (y + z) / 2 + k * k * (y * z) / 3)

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley3_efficient
proofs.statement: shapley3 k x y z + shapley3 k y x z + shapley3 k z x y = dfold k [x, y, z]

proofs.name: GameTheory.shapley3_corners
proofs.doc: Corner by corner: singletons whole, each pair corner k·xy halved, the triple k²xyz in thirds.
proofs.statement: shapley3 k x y z = x + (k * x * y) / 2 + (k * x * z) / 2 + (k * k * x * y * z) / 3

proofs.name: GameTheory.bonus_gap
proofs.doc: Bonus ratios φᵢ/xᵢ differ by (x₂ − x₁)(k/2 + k²x₃/3): it is your partners' size that counts.

proofs.name: GameTheory.banzhaf3_eq
proofs.statement: banzhaf3 k x y z = x * (1 + k * y / 2) * (1 + k * z / 2)

proofs.name: GameTheory.bigger_smaller_bonus
proofs.doc: With synergy (k ≥ 0) the bigger player gets the smaller bonus ratio.

proofs.name: GameTheory.run_total
proofs.statement: ∀ (rounds : List (Rat × Rat)) (u v : Rat), 0 < u → 0 < v → Good ε rounds → (run ε rounds (u, v)).1 + (run ε rounds (u, v)).2 = (u + v) * algFactor ε rounds (u, v)

proofs.name: GameTheory.run_expert
proofs.statement: ∀ (rounds : List (Rat × Rat)) (u v : Rat), (run ε rounds (u, v)).1 = u * expertFactor ε rounds

proofs.name: GameTheory.run_pos
proofs.statement: ∀ (rounds : List (Rat × Rat)) (u v : Rat), 0 < u → 0 < v → Good ε rounds → 0 < (run ε rounds (u, v)).2

proofs.name: GameTheory.lifted_regret
proofs.doc: The lifted regret bound: starting from equal weights, the best expert's growth is at most 2 = n times the algorithm's. Taking logs gives Σ log(1 + ε g) ≤ Σ log(1 + ε r) + log 2.
proofs.statement: expertFactor ε rounds ≤ 2 * algFactor ε rounds (1, 1)

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.boosts_close
proofs.doc: **Two boosts close on a rotation, with coefficient −q** (the twist, made infinitesimal).

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.galilean_boosts_commute
proofs.doc: At the Galilean point the boosts commute: no twist.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.boost_x_keeps_form
proofs.doc: The boost along x keeps the dial's form: Kᵀ G + G K = 0.
proofs.statement: add (mul (tr (Kx q)) (Gq q)) (mul (Gq q) (Kx q)) = zero

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.boost_y_keeps_form
proofs.statement: add (mul (tr (Ky q)) (Gq q)) (mul (Gq q) (Ky q)) = zero

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.rotation_keeps_form
proofs.doc: The rotation keeps the form too, for every q.
proofs.statement: add (mul (tr Rxy) (Gq q)) (mul (Gq q) Rxy) = zero

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.lapse_bracket_is_rotation
proofs.doc: **The hypersurface bracket with linear lapses** N = b·x, M = c·x: the shift N∇M − M∇N is the rigid rotation field x ↦ (b × c) × x … written out by components.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.dial_only_half_bending
proofs.doc: **Any dial-only theory (space left flat, γ = 0) bends light by exactly half, whatever β.**

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.dial_only_perihelion
proofs.doc: Its perihelion is 2/3 of GR's for A = 1 − 2U (β = 0) and 1/3 for A = e^{−2U} (β = 1).

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.conformal_dial
proofs.doc: A conformal dial (Nordström, γ = −1): no bending, perihelion backwards by a third.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.full_bending_iff
proofs.doc: Full bending forces γ = 1: space must curve as much as time.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.static_clock
proofs.doc: Static clocks run at 1/γ of the river: 1 − v² = 1 − 2M/r = −g_tt.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.static_ruler
proofs.doc: Static radial rulers stretch by γ of the river: 1/(1 − v²) = g_rr.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.deficits_inverse
proofs.doc: **The two deficits are mult-add inverses**: (−g_tt − 1) ✳ (g_rr − 1) = 0, i.e. (−2x) ✳ (2x/(1 − 2x)) = 0. One boost, the same factor for time and space.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.metric_product
proofs.doc: Equivalently g_tt · g_rr = −1: (1 − 2x) · 1/(1 − 2x) = 1.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.horizon_is_wall
proofs.doc: **The horizon is the river at light speed** (the velocity wall): 2M/r = 1 ↔ r = 2M.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.isotropic_radius
proofs.doc: Isotropic radius: with r = ρ(1 + u)² and M = 2uρ, 1 − 2M/r = ((1 − u)/(1 + u))², written without division: (1 + u)²·ρ − 2M equals (1 − u)²·ρ.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.friedmann_newton
proofs.doc: Friedmann is Newton's escape speed for a uniform ball (π kept as a symbol p): (H R)²/2 = ((4/3) p R³ ρ)/R ↔ H² = (8/3) p ρ, for R ≠ 0.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.gpb_through_river
proofs.doc: **Gravity Probe B's factor is the gyroscope's speed through the river**: composing the river (radial, v_r² = 2x) with the orbit (tangential, v_o² = x/(1 − 2x)) at right angles, 1 − w² = (1 − v_r²)(1 − v_o²) = 1 − 3x.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.perpendicular_fuse
proofs.doc: Perpendicular speeds compose by mult-add on −v²: −w² = (−u²) ✳ (−v²) when w² = u² + v²(1 − u²).

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.redshifts_fuse
proofs.doc: **Redshifts mult-add**: if 1 + z = (1 + z₁)(1 + z₂) then z = z₁ ✳ z₂ (any chain of gravitational, Doppler and cosmological shifts).

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.infall_light
proofs.doc: Light falling in from far away, seen by the river: blueshift γ² times Doppler² equals 1/(1 + v)², i.e. γ·√((1 − v)/(1 + v)) = 1/(1 + v). Stated without division.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.einstein_combination
proofs.doc: **Lovelock's step in one line**: if ∇·Ric = ½ dR (contracted Bianchi) and the combination a·Ric + b·R·g is to be divergence-free where dR ≠ 0, then b = −a/2.

proofs.name: GeneralRelativity.einstein_divergence_free
proofs.doc: And the Einstein combination is divergence-free: ½dR − ½dR = 0.

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.rectangle_corner
proofs.doc: the rectangle: (1 + a)(1 + b) = the unit square + two strips + the corner square

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.gnomon
proofs.doc: Euclid II.4, the gnomon: mult-add of a with itself is the L-shaped strip 2a + a²
proofs.statement: multAdd a a = 2 * a + a * a

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.euclid_II_4
proofs.doc: Euclid II.4 in full: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
proofs.statement: (a + b) * (a + b) = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.cube_layers
proofs.doc: the cube: mult-add three times gives the layers 3, 3, 1 (with the unit cube, 1, 3, 3, 1)
proofs.statement: multAdd (multAdd a a) a = 3 * a + 3 * (a * a) + a * a * a

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.box_corners
proofs.doc: the box: three different sides give the corners a+b+c, ab+bc+ca, abc
proofs.statement: multAdd (multAdd a b) c = (a + b + c) + (a * b + b * c + c * a) + a * b * c

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.square_cube
proofs.doc: Galileo's square-cube law (1638): grow every length by a; area grows by A = a ⊞ a and volume by A ⊞ a, so weight per unit of strength grows by the factor 1 + a
proofs.statement: 1 + multAdd (multAdd a a) a = (1 + multAdd a a) * (1 + a)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.fall_is_gnomon
proofs.doc: each step's distance is the gnomon that grows an n-square into an (n+1)-square

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.fallen_square
proofs.doc: so the distance fallen is the square of the time: d ∝ t²

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.gnomon_lift
proofs.doc: the gnomon step is mult-add's lift on Nat: (n ⊞ n) + 1 = (n + 1)²
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.pythagoras_from_areas
proofs.doc: Pythagoras by the "bride's chair": the square on a + b holds the tilted square on c and four right triangles of area ab/2. Given that area count, c² = a² + b².
proofs.statement: c * c = a * a + b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triangles_compose
proofs.doc: the right triangle 1 + x·i: mult-adding two of them multiplies squared hypotenuses, (1 + x²)(1 + y²) = (1 − xy)² + (x + y)²; its new slope is (x + y)/(1 − xy)
