proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triangles_compose_norm
proofs.statement: norm 0 1 (mre 1 1 x 1 y) (mu 0 1 x 1 y) = norm 0 1 1 x * norm 0 1 1 y
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.euclid_triple_parts
proofs.doc: Euclid's triples: square the triangle q + p·i (mult-add power 2 in the complex lift)
proofs.statement: mre 1 q p q p = q * q - p * p ∧ mu 0 q p q p = 2 * p * q

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.angle_addition
proofs.doc: angle addition: (cos α + i sin α)(cos β + i sin β) at the complex point (0, 1)
proofs.statement: mre 1 c1 s1 c2 s2 = c1 * c2 - s1 * s2 ∧ mu 0 c1 s1 c2 s2 = c1 * s2 + s1 * c2

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.unit_circle_closed
proofs.doc: cos² + sin² = 1 survives angle addition: the unit circle is closed under the product

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.tangent_addition
proofs.doc: tangent addition is the landscape law at (0, 1): numerator x + y, denominator 1 − xy
proofs.statement: LandscapeMap.num 0 x y = x + y ∧ LandscapeMap.den 1 x y = 1 - x * y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.double_angle
proofs.doc: double angle: (1 + x i)² = (1 − x²) + 2x·i, so tan 2θ = 2t/(1 − t²)
proofs.statement: mre 1 1 x 1 x = 1 - x * x ∧ mu 0 1 x 1 x = 2 * x

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triple_angle
proofs.doc: triple angle: (1 + x i)³ = (1 − 3x²) + (3x − x³)·i: the cube's layers 1, 3, 3, 1 land alternately on the real and the i axis, with the signs of i², i³
proofs.statement: mre 1 (mre 1 1 x 1 x) (mu 0 1 x 1 x) 1 x = 1 - 3 * (x * x) ∧ mu 0 (mre 1 1 x 1 x) (mu 0 1 x 1 x) 1 x = 3 * x - x * x * x

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.law_of_cosines_norm
proofs.doc: the law of cosines is the norm on the line q = 1, with k = −2 cos C: c² = a² + k·ab + b². At k = 0 it is Pythagoras.
proofs.statement: norm k 1 a b = a * a + k * a * b + b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.law_of_cosines_right_angle
proofs.statement: norm 0 1 a b = a * a + b * b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.flat_triangle_open
proofs.doc: on the border (k = ±2, angle 180° or 0°) the triangle is flat: c = a + b or c = a − b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triangle_lengths_real
proofs.doc: inside the turning country (k² ≤ 4) every side-squared is a true length, never negative

proofs.name: GraphTheory.parallel_join
proofs.doc: Two parallel bonds join their ends with weight v₁ + v₂ + v₁v₂: one, the other, or both.
proofs.statement: v₁ + v₂ + v₁ * v₂ = v₁ ✳ v₂
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: GraphTheory.series_local
proofs.doc: Series pair through a middle vertex: "ends not joined" weighs Q + v₁ + v₂ (middle alone, or tied to one end), "ends joined" weighs v₁v₂. One bond of weight v with the factor Q + v₁ + v₂ gives the same two numbers.
proofs.statement: (Q + v₁ + v₂) * 1 = Q + v₁ + v₂ ∧ (Q + v₁ + v₂) * (v₁ * v₂ / (Q + v₁ + v₂)) = v₁ * v₂

proofs.name: GraphTheory.add_div'
proofs.statement: Q + x / S = (Q * S + x) / S

proofs.name: GraphTheory.series_tr
proofs.doc: **Series multiplies transmissivity.**
proofs.statement: tr Q (v₁ * v₂ / (Q + v₁ + v₂)) = tr Q v₁ * tr Q v₂

proofs.name: GraphTheory.parallel_tr
proofs.doc: **Parallel is a landscape law.** With tᵢ = vᵢ/(Q + vᵢ), the joined bond v₁ ✳ v₂ has t = (t₁ + t₂ + (Q − 2)t₁t₂)/(1 − (1 − Q)t₁t₂) = F_{Q−2, 1−Q}(t₁, t₂).
proofs.statement: tr Q (v₁ ✳ v₂) = lens (Q - 2) (1 - Q) (tr Q v₁) (tr Q v₂)

proofs.name: GraphTheory.parallel_lift
proofs.doc: The lift of the parallel law is 1 + v: (1 + (Q − 1)t)/(1 − t) = 1 + v.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.q_one
proofs.doc: Q = 1: percolation and reliability, the failure union a ✳₋₁ b.
proofs.statement: lens (1 - 2) (1 - 1) a b = wAdd (-1) a b

proofs.name: GraphTheory.q_two
proofs.doc: Q = 2: Ising, velocity addition (tanh addition).

proofs.name: GraphTheory.q_zero_cusp
proofs.doc: Q = 0: the spanning-forest end, the cusp k² = 4q of the landscape.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.potts_is_amh
proofs.doc: **Potts parallel is AMH union**, with dependence θ = 1 − Q: the two bonds "fail" together like AMH-dependent events.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.perfect_bond_absorbs
proofs.doc: Wall 1: a perfect bond t = 1 swallows anything put in parallel with it.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.colouring_bond
proofs.doc: The proper-colouring bond v = −1 has t = −1/(Q − 1).

proofs.name: GraphTheory.colouring_wall_absorbs
proofs.doc: Wall 2: that bond swallows anything in parallel (a forbidden pair stays forbidden).

proofs.name: GraphTheory.colouring_is_wall
proofs.doc: In weights, the colouring bond is mult-add's own wall −1.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.series_odds
proofs.doc: In odds against, u = 1/p − 1, series is plain mult-add.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.wheatstone
proofs.doc: **The Wheatstone bridge** has no series or parallel pair; pivot on the middle bond: contracted, it is two parallel pairs in series; deleted, two series pairs in parallel.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.golden_fixed
proofs.doc: **The golden fixed point.** If p² = 1 − p (p = (√5 − 1)/2), the diamond step fixes p.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.golden_slope
proofs.doc: Slope there: 4p − 4p³ = 4 − 4p (≈ 1.528 > 1, so the fixed point repels).

proofs.name: GraphTheory.ising_fixed
proofs.doc: Ising (Q = 2): if t³ + t² + t = 1, the diamond step fixes t.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.three_state_fixed
proofs.doc: Three colours: the diamond fixed point is exactly 1/2.

proofs.name: GraphTheory.strong_entry
proofs.doc: Closed adjacency entries multiply: (a + i)(b + j) − i·j = a·j + i·b + a·b. With i = j = 1 (same vertex in both) this is a ✳ b; the three terms are the Cartesian pieces A⊗I, I⊗B and the tensor corner A⊗B.
proofs.statement: (a + i) * (b + j) - i * j = a * j + i * b + a * b

proofs.name: GraphTheory.strong_count
proofs.doc: Edge counts: 2m + n multiplies.
proofs.statement: 2 * (n₁ * m₂ + n₂ * m₁ + 2 * m₁ * m₂) + n₁ * n₂ = (2 * m₁ + n₁) * (2 * m₂ + n₂)

proofs.name: GraphTheory.join_adds
proofs.doc: A join lets a set use only one side, so I − 1 adds (dial k = 0).

proofs.name: GraphTheory.c4_indep
proofs.doc: C₄ is the join of two non-edges: I = (1 + x)² + (1 + x)² − 1 = 1 + 4x + 2x².

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.factors_multiply
proofs.doc: **The factors multiply to the known total** (squared): (1 − 2x)·(1/γ²) = 1 − 3x.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.fractions_fuse
proofs.doc: **The precession fractions mult-add**: if 1 − p = (1 − a)(1 − b) then −p = (−a) ✳ (−b).

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.fuse_factors
proofs.doc: And back: the mult-add form gives the product of factors.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.fuse_weight_minus_one
proofs.doc: The same law is the dial's weight −1: p = a + b − ab ("either twist").

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.weak_split
proofs.doc: First-order parts: space 1·x, velocity ½·x, total 3/2·x.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.corner_is_second_order
proofs.doc: The fused total differs from the plain sum only by the corner a·b (second order).

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.ppn_geodetic
proofs.doc: In PPN form the geodetic coefficient is γ_PPN + ½; general relativity's γ_PPN = 1 gives 3/2.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.thirds
proofs.doc: The velocity part alone is one third, the space part alone two thirds.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.geodetic_within_error
proofs.doc: Twist bookkeeping at r = 7027.4 km gives 6603.9; GP-B measured 6601.8 ± 18.3.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.geodetic_parts
proofs.doc: Space part 4402.6 + velocity part 2201.3 = 6603.9.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.parts_alone_ruled_out
proofs.doc: Either part alone misses the measurement by more than 100 standard errors.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.frame_dragging_within_error
proofs.doc: Frame dragging: about 40.8 against the measured 37.2 ± 7.2.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.polar_average_four
proofs.doc: 3 sin² − 1 averaged at the quarter points (sin² = 0, 1, 0, 1) is ½.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.polar_average_eight
proofs.doc: And at the eighth points (sin² = 0, ½, 1, ½, …) it is ½ too.

proofs.name: GravityProbeB.polar_average_pair
proofs.doc: Any orbit point and its quarter-turn partner have sin² + cos² = 1, so a pair averages (3·s − 1 + 3·(1 − s) − 1)/2 = ½ whatever s is: the average is ½ for every set of points closed under quarter turns.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.M2.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_linear
proofs.doc: mob a = I + a·X: each translation is one step along the generator.
proofs.statement: mob p q a = M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (gen p q))

proofs.name: GroupsLie.gen_sq
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton for the generator: X² = pX − qI.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (gen p q) (gen p q) = M2.sub (M2.smul p (gen p q)) (M2.smul q M2.one)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_mul
proofs.doc: The law is matrix multiplication up to the scale 1 − qab: mob a · mob b = (1 − qab)·I + (a + b + pab)·X.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (mob p q a) (mob p q b) = M2.add (M2.smul (Dn q a b) M2.one) (M2.smul (N p a b) (gen p q))

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_mul_entries
proofs.doc: Same statement entry by entry: the product is (1 − qab)·mob(F(a,b)) with F = N/Dn.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (mob p q a) (mob p q b) = ⟨Dn q a b + p * N p a b, N p a b, -(q * N p a b), Dn q a b⟩

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_dial
proofs.doc: On the dial line (q = 0) there is no scale at all: matrices multiply exactly as ✳ₖ.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (mob k 0 a) (mob k 0 b) = mob k 0 (wAdd k a b)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_multAdd
proofs.doc: Mult-add itself as 2×2 matrices [[1 + a, a], [0, 1]].

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_comm
proofs.doc: Landscape matrices commute: the corner cannot twist inside one landscape law.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (mob p q a) (mob p q b) = M2.mul (mob p q b) (mob p q a)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mob_acts
proofs.doc: Acting on a point: the Möbius map of mob a sends b to F(a,b) (cross-multiplied).
proofs.statement: (mob p q a).a * b + (mob p q a).b = N p a b ∧ (mob p q a).c * b + (mob p q a).d = Dn q a b

proofs.name: GroupsLie.theta_lift
proofs.doc: (1 + aθ)(1 + bθ) = (1 − qab) + (a + b + pab)θ: the landscape law is θ-multiplication.
proofs.statement: tmul p q (1, a) (1, b) = (Dn q a b, N p a b)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.tmul_comm
proofs.statement: tmul p q u v = tmul p q v u

proofs.name: GroupsLie.tmul_assoc
proofs.statement: tmul p q (tmul p q u v) w = tmul p q u (tmul p q v w)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.theta_multAdd
proofs.doc: p = 1, q = 0: θ² = θ, and the first slot of (1 + aθ)(1 + bθ) is the lift of a ✳ b.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.theta_dual
proofs.doc: p = q = 0: dual numbers, θ² = 0, plain addition.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.theta_tan
proofs.doc: p = 0, q = 1: θ² = −1, the complex numbers; the law is tan addition (a + b)/(1 − ab).

proofs.name: GroupsLie.theta_velocity
proofs.doc: p = 0, q = −1: θ² = 1, split-complex numbers; velocity addition (a + b)/(1 + ab).

proofs.name: GroupsLie.tnorm_mul
proofs.statement: tnorm p q (tmul p q u v) = tnorm p q u * tnorm p q v

proofs.name: GroupsLie.tnorm_one_theta
proofs.doc: The norm of 1 + aθ is the rate V(a).
proofs.statement: tnorm p q (1, a) = V p q a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.rate_mul
proofs.doc: Rate law: V(a)·V(b) = (1 − qab)²·V(F(a,b)), cross-multiplied.
proofs.statement: V p q a * V p q b = Dn q a b * Dn q a b + p * N p a b * Dn q a b + q * N p a b * N p a b

proofs.name: GroupsLie.deriv_numerator
proofs.doc: The b-derivative of F has numerator ∂N·Dn − N·∂Dn = V(a).
proofs.statement: (1 + p * a) * Dn q a b - N p a b * (-(q * a)) = V p q a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.invariant_ruler
proofs.doc: Invariant ruler: ∂F/∂b · V(b) = V(F), cross-multiplied by Dn² (so the tick spacing dx/V(x) is carried along by every translation).
proofs.statement: ((1 + p * a) * Dn q a b - N p a b * (-(q * a))) * V p q b = Dn q a b * Dn q a b + p * N p a b * Dn q a b + q * N p a b * N p a b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: GroupsLie.rate_walls
proofs.doc: The rate splits over its walls: 1 − (u+v)x + uvx² = (1 − ux)(1 − vx).

proofs.name: GroupsLie.Fld.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: GroupsLie.br_antisymm
proofs.statement: br f g = ⟨-(br g f).al, -(br g f).be, -(br g f).ga⟩

proofs.name: GroupsLie.Bl_invariant
proofs.doc: Ad-invariance: B([g,f], h) + B(f, [g,h]) = 0, so the light cone Q = 0 is a Lie-theoretic object.
proofs.statement: Bl (br g f) h + Bl f (br g h) = 0

proofs.name: GroupsLie.landscape_Q
proofs.doc: The landscape point (p, q) is the field 1 + px + qx²; its form is the discriminant.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.br_dilation_translation
proofs.doc: Translation ∂ and dilation x∂ bracket to a translation: [x∂, ∂] = −∂.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.br_dial
proofs.doc: Two dial generators 1 + kx and 1 + k'x bracket to a pure translation (k' − k)·∂.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.shift_rate
proofs.doc: In the chart y = x/(1 − cx) the rate becomes 1 + (p + 2c)y + (q + pc + c²)y².

proofs.name: GroupsLie.shift_conj_num
proofs.doc: The chart change carries one law to the other. Write ψ(y) = y/(1 + cy) for the way back (ψ undoes φ(x) = x/(1 − cx)). Then F_{p,q}(ψA, ψB) = ψ(F_{p+2c, q+pc+c²}(A, B)): after clearing the factors (1 + cA)(1 + cB), the numerators agree ...

proofs.name: GroupsLie.shift_conj_den
proofs.doc: ... and so do the denominators: (1 + cA)(1 + cB) − qAB = D' + c·N'.
proofs.statement: (1 + c * A) * (1 + c * B) - q * A * B = Dn (q + p * c + c * c) A B + c * N (p + 2 * c) A B

proofs.name: GroupsLie.T_eq_wAdd
proofs.statement: T k a x = wAdd k a x

proofs.name: GroupsLie.T_comp
proofs.statement: T k a (T k b x) = T k (wAdd k a b) x

proofs.name: GroupsLie.T_scale
proofs.doc: Scaling conjugation moves the dial: T^k_{λa}(λx) = λ·T^{kλ}_a(x).
proofs.statement: T k (l * a) (l * x) = l * T (k * l) a x

proofs.name: GroupsLie.T_dilation
proofs.doc: About the wall −1/k every translation is a pure dilation by 1 + ka.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.T_zero_no_fixed
proofs.doc: At k = 0 a nonzero translation has no fixed point, so it is no dilation.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.maM_bracket
proofs.doc: The failure of matrix mult-add to commute is exactly the commutator AB − BA.
proofs.statement: M2.sub (maM x y) (maM y x) = M2.sub (M2.mul x y) (M2.mul y x)

proofs.name: GroupsLie.bracket_trace
proofs.doc: Brackets are trace-free: they land in sl₂.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.landscape_no_twist
proofs.doc: On the landscape, a·X and b·X mult-add the same in either order.
proofs.statement: maM (M2.smul a (gen p q)) (M2.smul b (gen p q)) = maM (M2.smul b (gen p q)) (M2.smul a (gen p q))

proofs.name: GroupsLie.twist_example
proofs.doc: A 2×2 pair where the twist is visible: [[0,1],[0,0]] and [[0,0],[1,0]].

proofs.name: GroupsLie.mersenne
proofs.doc: n copies of 1 under mult-add are the Mersenne number 2ⁿ − 1.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.f5_cyclic
proofs.doc: (F₅ minus the wall 4, ✳) is a 4-cycle generated by 1.
proofs.statement: mpow (1 : Fin 5) 4 = 0 ∧ ∀ a : Fin 5, a ≠ 4 → ∃ j : Fin 4, mpow (1 : Fin 5) j.val = a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.f7_cyclic
proofs.doc: Mod 7, 1 has order 3 (2 is not a primitive root), but 2 generates all six.
proofs.statement: mpow (1 : Fin 7) 3 = 0 ∧ mpow (2 : Fin 7) 6 = 0 ∧ ∀ a : Fin 7, a ≠ 6 → ∃ j : Fin 6, mpow (2 : Fin 7) j.val = a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.f11_cyclic
proofs.statement: mpow (1 : Fin 11) 10 = 0 ∧ ∀ a : Fin 11, a ≠ 10 → ∃ j : Fin 10, mpow (1 : Fin 11) j.val = a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.f13_cyclic
proofs.statement: mpow (1 : Fin 13) 12 = 0 ∧ ∀ a : Fin 13, a ≠ 12 → ∃ j : Fin 12, mpow (1 : Fin 13) j.val = a

proofs.name: GroupsLie.circle_counts
proofs.doc: The finite circle: p + 1 points when p ≡ 3 mod 4, p − 1 when p ≡ 1 mod 4.

proofs.name: GroupsLie.circle7_closed
proofs.doc: The circle over F₇ is closed under complex multiplication (the circle group).
proofs.statement: ∀ a b c d : Fin 7, a * a + b * b = 1 → c * c + d * d = 1 → (a * c - b * d) * (a * c - b * d) + (a * d + b * c) * (a * d + b * c) = 1

proofs.name: Infinities.evalL_addL
proofs.statement: ∀ p q : List Nat, evalL t (addL p q) = evalL t p + evalL t q

proofs.name: Infinities.wOnes_spec
proofs.statement: t * wOnes t n + 1 = (1 + t) ^ n

proofs.name: Infinities.cantor
proofs.statement: ∃ g : α → Bool, ∀ a, f a ≠ g
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Infinities.half_iter_upper
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → g n ≤ h (h n)

proofs.name: Infinities.half_iter_lower
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → h (h n) ≤ g n

proofs.name: Infinities.half_not_poly
proofs.doc: If a half rung stayed under n^k, the whole rung would stay under n^(k·k). Since the whole rung (exponential) outgrows every polynomial, no half rung is polynomial.
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → g n ≤ n ^ (k * k)

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlogN_mul
proofs.doc: The q-logarithm turns products into the dial with k = m.
proofs.statement: qlogN m (x * y) = wAdd (m : Rat) (qlogN m x) (qlogN m y)

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlogN_lift
proofs.doc: Its lift is the plain power: 1 + m·ln(x) = x^m.
proofs.statement: 1 + (m : Rat) * qlogN m x = x ^ m

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlogN_one_weight
proofs.doc: k = 1 (Tsallis q = 0): ln x = x − 1, the "count minus one".

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlog_of_root
proofs.doc: The q-exponential inverts it: if y^m = 1 + m·x then ln y = x.

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlog_neg_one
proofs.doc: k = −1 (Tsallis q = 2): ln x = 1 − 1/x, and it obeys the union rule.

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlog_dual
proofs.doc: Duality: ln_{2−q}(x) = −ln_q(1/x).

proofs.name: InformationFull.qlogNeg_mul
proofs.doc: The dual logarithm turns products into the dial with the opposite weight.
proofs.statement: qlogNeg m (x * y) = wAdd (-(m : Rat)) (qlogNeg m x) (qlogNeg m y)

proofs.name: InformationFull.qexpN_mul
proofs.doc: It turns the dial into multiplication: e(x)·e(y) = e(x ✳_{1/n} y).
proofs.statement: qexpN n x * qexpN n y = qexpN n (wAdd (1 / (n : Rat)) x y)

proofs.name: InformationFull.qexp_climb
proofs.doc: Compound interest: e_q(x) − 1 is n mult-add steps of x/n (rung 2).
proofs.statement: qexpN n x - 1 = mpow (x / n) n

proofs.name: InformationFull.shan_map_w
proofs.statement: shan s (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * lsum ys * s x + x * shan s ys + k * (x * s x) * shan s ys

proofs.name: InformationFull.outer_shan_w
proofs.doc: For any surprise s that turns products into ⊞ₖ, the joint "entropy" Σ p·s(p) of independent sources is (Σr)·S_A + (Σp)·S_B + k·S_A·S_B. k = 0 is the information page's outer-log lemma (Shannon); any k is Tsallis.
proofs.statement: shan s (outer xs ys) = lsum ys * shan s xs + lsum xs * shan s ys + k * shan s xs * shan s ys

proofs.name: InformationFull.tsallis_engine
proofs.doc: Tsallis' pseudo-additivity, proved as "expectation passes through the dial": S(A × B) = S(A) ✳ₖ S(B) for normalized independent sources.
proofs.statement: shan s (outer xs ys) = wAdd k (shan s xs) (shan s ys)

proofs.name: InformationFull.sm_compose
proofs.doc: If R adds over independent sources and E turns + into ⊞ₖ, then E∘R composes by ⊞ₖ. With R = Rényi of order α and E(x) = (e^{kx} − 1)/k this is Sharma–Mittal H_{α,β}, k = 1 − β.
proofs.statement: E RAB = wAdd k (E RA) (E RB)

proofs.name: InformationFull.flip_weight
proofs.doc: Flipping the weight: the dial at −k is the dial at k read on negatives.

proofs.name: InformationFull.leaves_lift
proofs.doc: The lift: leaves = 1 + inner nodes.

proofs.name: InformationFull.graft_leaves
proofs.statement: leaves (graft a b) = leaves a * leaves b

proofs.name: InformationFull.graft_inner
proofs.statement: inner (graft a b) = inner a + leaves a * inner b

proofs.name: InformationFull.graft_multAdd
proofs.doc: Grafting composes internal nodes (decisions) by mult-add.
proofs.statement: inner (graft a b) = inner a ✳ inner b

proofs.name: InformationFull.full_inner
proofs.doc: It has 2^n − 1 = the mult-add power of 1 internal nodes: the q-number [n]₂.

proofs.name: InformationFull.dary_graft
proofs.doc: D-ary trees by counts: graft (leaves 1 + c·I) — internal nodes compose by the dial c = D − 1.
proofs.statement: IA + (1 + c * IA) * IB = wAdd c IA IB

proofs.name: InformationFull.dary_leaves
proofs.doc: ... and leaves multiply: the lift of the dial.
proofs.statement: (1 + c * IA) * (1 + c * IB) = 1 + c * wAdd c IA IB

proofs.name: InformationFull.dary_full
proofs.doc: The complete D-ary tree of depth n: c·[n]_D + 1 = D^n, with D = 1 + c.
proofs.statement: 1 + c * wpow c 1 n = (1 + c * 1) ^ n

proofs.name: InformationFull.channel_cascade
proofs.doc: Cascade of [[1−a, a], [b, 1−b]] and [[1−a₂, a₂], [b₂, 1−b₂]]: the new crossover sum is (a + b) ✳₋₁ (a₂ + b₂).

proofs.name: InformationFull.channel_det
proofs.doc: The determinant 1 − s multiplies.

proofs.name: InformationFull.bsc_from_union
proofs.doc: The binary symmetric channel (s = 2p): the union rule on 2p is the parity rule on p.

proofs.name: InformationFull.z_cascade
proofs.doc: The Z-channel (b = 0): its crossover composes by the union rule.

proofs.name: InfoFused.climb
proofs.doc: K2, climb: the mult-add power climbs the cube.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wpow k a n = pw (1 + k * a) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.linearize
proofs.doc: K4, linearize: any map that turns products into sums turns ⊕ₖ into + in the coordinate 1 + k·a. Taking L = log gives log(1 + k·a).
proofs.statement: L (1 + k * wAdd k a b) = L (1 + k * a) + L (1 + k * b)

proofs.name: InfoFused.lsum_append
proofs.statement: lsum (xs ++ ys) = lsum xs + lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.lsum_map
proofs.statement: lsum (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.outer_sum
proofs.doc: K5, outer sum: the grid's total is the product of the two edges.
proofs.statement: lsum (outer xs ys) = lsum xs * lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.shan_append
proofs.statement: shan L (xs ++ ys) = shan L xs + shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.shan_map
proofs.statement: shan L (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * lsum ys * L x + x * shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.outer_shan
proofs.doc: K6, outer log.
proofs.statement: shan L (outer xs ys) = lsum ys * shan L xs + lsum xs * shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_rule
proofs.doc: Union rule for independent events: P(A or B) = p + q − pq = p ⊕₋₁ q.

proofs.name: InfoFused.survival
proofs.doc: Survival multiplies (K1 at k = −1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_is_flipped_madd
proofs.doc: The k = −1 rule is mult-add read on the negatives (K3).

proofs.name: InfoFused.incl_excl3
proofs.doc: Inclusion–exclusion for three independent events falls out of associativity: the signed corners of the mult-add cube.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) p q) r = p + q + r - p*q - p*r - q*r + p*q*r

proofs.name: InfoFused.series_system
proofs.doc: A series system of n parts, each failing with chance p, fails with chance 1 − (1 − p)ⁿ (K2).
proofs.statement: wpow (-1) p n = 1 - pw (1 - p) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.hazards_add
proofs.doc: Survival multiplies, so cumulative hazard −log(1 − p) adds (K4).

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_grows
proofs.doc: Adding an independent part never lowers the chance of a failure.

proofs.name: InfoFused.hartley
proofs.doc: Hartley: typical-set sizes multiply, so bits add (log₂ of 2ᵐ·2ⁿ is m + n).
proofs.statement: pw (2 : Rat) (m + n) = pw (2 : Rat) m * pw (2 : Rat) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.shannon_additive
proofs.doc: Shannon additivity for independent sources, H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y), proved for any L with L(xy) = L(x) + L(y) and both distributions summing to 1.
proofs.statement: shan L (outer ps rs) = shan L ps + shan L rs

proofs.name: InfoFused.joint_sums_to_one
proofs.doc: The joint distribution of independent sources is a distribution (K5).

proofs.name: InfoFused.power_sums_multiply
proofs.doc: Power sums multiply. With xᵢ = pᵢ^q and yⱼ = rⱼ^q (and (pr)^q = p^q·r^q for real powers), this is Σ (pᵢrⱼ)^q = (Σ pᵢ^q)(Σ rⱼ^q) (K5).
proofs.statement: lsum (outer ws vs) = lsum ws * lsum vs

proofs.name: InfoFused.tsallis
proofs.doc: Tsallis pseudo-additivity, S_q(A,B) = S_A + S_B + (1 − q)·S_A·S_B. With k = 1 − q, Tsallis entropy is S = (P − 1)/k where P is the power sum. Stated with the k cleared: if k·S_A = P − 1, k·S_B = R − 1 and k·S_AB = P·R − 1, then k·S_AB = k·(S_A ⊕ₖ S_B).
proofs.statement: k * SAB = k * wAdd k SA SB

proofs.name: InfoFused.renyi_additive
proofs.doc: Rényi additivity: Rényi entropy is L(1 + k·S)/k, so it adds where Tsallis mult-adds (K1 + K4). Stated with the 1/k cleared.
proofs.statement: L (1 + k * wAdd k SA SB) = L (1 + k * SA) + L (1 + k * SB)

proofs.name: InfoFused.gini_simpson
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 2 (k = −1): Gini–Simpson G = 1 − Σp² is the chance two draws differ. Collision sums multiply, so G composes by the union rule: "the pair differs" = "A differs or B differs".

proofs.name: InfoFused.support_count
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 0 (k = 1): S₀ = N − 1, support sizes multiply, so N − 1 mult-adds: the N×M grid minus its unit corner.

proofs.name: InfoFused.shannon_weight
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 1 (k = 0): Shannon, plain addition.

proofs.name: InfoFused.uniform_tsallis_is_fused_power
proofs.doc: Rung 2: for N equally likely outcomes and k = 1 − q a whole number m, 1 + k·S = Nᵐ, so k·S is the fused power (N − 1)^⊕m (K2 with k = 1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.kraft_slack
proofs.doc: Kraft sums of two prefix codes multiply when you concatenate codewords (K5), and the slack 1 − K composes like failure chances (k = −1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.kraft_product
proofs.doc: The concatenated code still satisfies Kraft.

proofs.name: InfoFused.campbell
proofs.doc: Campbell's exponential cost: M = Σ pᵢ·D^(t·ℓᵢ) multiplies for concatenated independent sources (K5 on the weights), so M − 1 composes by plain mult-add.

proofs.name: InfoFused.lengths_add
proofs.doc: Expected length adds for concatenated codes (the k = 0 shadow of Campbell): Σᵢⱼ pᵢrⱼ(ℓᵢ + mⱼ) = Σ pℓ + Σ rm when both sum to 1. Stated on the grid sums.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_cascade
proofs.doc: Binary symmetric channel cascade: the off-diagonal entry of the product of [[1−p, p],[p, 1−p]] and [[1−q, q],[q, 1−q]] is p ⊕₋₂ q.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_polarization
proofs.doc: Polarization 1 − 2p multiplies along a cascade (K1 at k = −2).

proofs.name: InfoFused.piling_up
proofs.doc: Matsui's piling-up lemma: biases ε = 1/2 − p combine as 2·ε₁·ε₂.

proofs.name: InfoFused.n_flips
proofs.doc: n identical flips: 1 − 2·P(odd) = (1 − 2p)ⁿ (K2).
proofs.statement: 1 - 2 * wpow (-2) p n = pw (1 - 2 * p) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.qary_cascade
proofs.doc: The q-ary symmetric channel. An error moves a symbol to one of the other letters at random; a second error lands back on the right letter with chance c = 1/(alphabet − 1). Right after two hops: both right, or wrong then sent back. The error composes with weight k = −(1 + c).

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_never_cancel
proofs.doc: c = 0, letters never cancel (huge alphabet, or erasures): the union rule.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-(1 + 0)) e1 e2 = wAdd (-1) e1 e2

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_binary
proofs.doc: c = 1, two letters: a second wAdd_flip always undoes the first.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-(1 + 1)) e1 e2 = wAdd (-2) e1 e2

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_four
proofs.doc: c = 1/3, four letters: the depolarizing qubit channel's −4/3.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bec_capacity
proofs.doc: Binary erasure channel: erasures compose by the union rule and capacity 1 − e multiplies exactly.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bec_dpi
proofs.doc: BEC: capacity of the cascade ≤ capacity of each link.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_dpi
proofs.doc: BSC (crossovers taken ≤ 1/2): the cascade's crossover is at least each link's.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_stays_below_half
proofs.doc: …and still ≤ 1/2, so it stays on the side where capacity 1 − h(p) falls as p rises. (That monotonicity is real analysis and is not checked here.)

proofs.name: InfoFused.sdpi_multiplies
proofs.doc: Strong data processing: the contraction coefficient (1 − 2p)² multiplies.

proofs.name: InfoFused.parallel_capacity
proofs.doc: Parallel channels: distinguishable messages multiply, capacities add (Hartley).
proofs.statement: pw (2 : Rat) (C1 + C2) = pw (2 : Rat) C1 * pw (2 : Rat) C2

proofs.name: InfoFused.parity3
proofs.doc: Parity of three noisy bits: the odd layers of the mult-add cube (1·3·3·1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.cube_corners
proofs.doc: Every corner of the cube {0,1}ⁿ: (1 + 1)ⁿ − 1 nonempty corners (K2 at k = 1, a = 1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.hamming_perfect
proofs.doc: Hamming codes are perfect: with n = m + r and n + 1 = 2ʳ, the 2ᵐ balls of radius 1 (a corner plus its n neighbours: layers 0 and 1) tile the n-cube.

proofs.name: InfoFused.check_node
proofs.doc: Check node: −2·(p ⊕₋₂ q) = (−2p) ⊕ (−2q), plain mult-add.
proofs.statement: -2 * wAdd (-2) p q = multAdd (-2 * p) (-2 * q)

proofs.name: InfoFused.variable_node
proofs.doc: Variable node: posterior odds multiply, so o − 1 mult-adds.

proofs.name: InfoFused.odds_to_velocity
proofs.doc: Odds product in ρ coordinates (ρ = (o−1)/(o+1)), with denominators cleared: numerator and denominator of the velocity sum.

proofs.name: InfoFused.velocity_corners
proofs.doc: Velocity addition lifts to mult-add on both corners: (1 + ab) + (a + b) = (1 + a)(1 + b) and (1 + ab) − (a + b) = (1 − a)(1 − b), so (1 + v)/(1 − v), the odds, multiplies.

proofs.name: InfoFused.vadd_assoc
proofs.statement: vadd (vadd x y) z = vadd x (vadd y z)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wmul_comm
proofs.statement: wmul k x y = wmul k y x

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wmul_assoc
proofs.statement: wmul k (wmul k x y) z = wmul k x (wmul k y z)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.eps_sq
proofs.doc: ε² = kε: the corner weight is the square of the infinitesimal.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.units_wAdd
proofs.doc: **Units multiply by weighted mult-add**: (1 + aε)(1 + bε) = 1 + (a ⊞ₖ b)ε.
proofs.statement: wmul k ⟨1, a⟩ ⟨1, b⟩ = ⟨1, wAdd k a b⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.units_multAdd
proofs.doc: With weight 1 the units multiply by plain mult-add.
proofs.statement: wmul 1 ⟨1, a⟩ ⟨1, b⟩ = ⟨1, multAdd a b⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.dual_units_add
proofs.doc: With weight 0 (dual numbers, 1-jets) the corner is dropped: relative slopes add. This is the logarithmic derivative of a product.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.twoPt_mul
proofs.doc: **The weighted dual numbers are two points.** Reading an element at x and at x + k turns the twisted product into the plain product at each point.
proofs.statement: twoPt k (wmul k x y) = ((twoPt k x).1 * (twoPt k y).1, (twoPt k x).2 * (twoPt k y).2)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.twoPt_weight_zero
proofs.doc: At weight 0 the two points coincide: the secant has become the tangent.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.diff_leibniz
proofs.doc: **Discrete Leibniz with the corner.** If f(x+h) = f₀ + h·f' and g(x+h) = g₀ + h·g', then (fg)(x+h) = f₀g₀ + h·(the ε-part of the product in R[ε]/(ε² − hε)). The forward difference of a product is that ε-part.
proofs.statement: (f₀ + h * f') * (g₀ + h * g') = f₀ * g₀ + h * (wmul h ⟨f₀, f'⟩ ⟨g₀, g'⟩).du

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.dual_inverse
proofs.doc: The dual numbers have no wall: 1 + aε always has the inverse 1 − aε.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wall_no_inverse
proofs.doc: **The wall is a zero at the second point.** If 1 + ka = 0, the unit 1 + aε has no inverse in R[ε]/(ε² − kε): read at x + k, it is 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.off_wall_inverse
proofs.doc: Off the wall, the inverse is the weighted mult-add way back −a/(1 + ka).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.leibniz2
proofs.doc: The jet product is the product of functions: second-order Leibniz, (fg)'' = f''g + 2f'g' + fg'' (with f'' = 2·c2).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.jma_lift
proofs.doc: Mult-add of jets is multiplication through 1 + x, as everywhere else.
proofs.statement: jmul ⟨1 + x.c0, x.c1, x.c2⟩ ⟨1 + y.c0, y.c1, y.c2⟩ = ⟨1 + (jma x y).c0, (jma x y).c1, (jma x y).c2⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cube_depth_two
proofs.doc: **Jet order = cube depth.** Three relative 2-jets (no constant term) mult-add to their sum plus the three pair corners; the triple corner, which would sit at ε³, is gone.
proofs.statement: jma ⟨0, a₁, b₁⟩ (jma ⟨0, a₂, b₂⟩ ⟨0, a₃, b₃⟩) = ⟨0, a₁ + a₂ + a₃, (b₁ + b₂ + b₃) + (a₁ * a₂ + a₁ * a₃ + a₂ * a₃)⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cube_depth_one
proofs.doc: At order 1 only layer 1 survives: relative jets just add.
proofs.statement: wmul 0 (wmul 0 ⟨1, a₁⟩ ⟨1, a₂⟩) ⟨1, a₃⟩ = ⟨1, a₁ + a₂ + a₃⟩
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.nilpotent_inverse
proofs.doc: **No wall in jet space.** A relative jet ν has the finite way back −ν + ν² (the geometric series stops because ε³ = 0).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_one_add_smul
proofs.doc: **The volume change of a step is the mult-add cube.** det(I + h∇u) = 1 + h·P + h²·Q + h³·R.
proofs.statement: (X.step h).det = 1 + h * X.tr + h^2 * X.e2 + h^3 * X.det

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_diag_cube
proofs.doc: **In principal axes the step's volume change is literally mult-add:** det(I + h·diag(a,b,c)) = 1 + (ha ⊞ hb ⊞ hc).
proofs.statement: ((diag3 a b c).step h).det = 1 + multAdd (multAdd (h * a) (h * b)) (h * c)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.diag_layers
proofs.doc: The layers of a diagonal gradient are the cube's layers of (a, b, c).
proofs.statement: (diag3 a b c).tr = a + b + c ∧ (diag3 a b c).e2 = a*b + a*c + b*c ∧ (diag3 a b c).det = a*b*c

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cayley_hamilton
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton, entrywise: X³ − P·X² + Q·X − R·I = 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_sq_traceless
proofs.doc: For an incompressible gradient, tr(X²) = −2Q.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_cube_traceless
proofs.doc: For an incompressible gradient, tr(X³) = 3R.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.e2_vorticity_strain
proofs.doc: **Layer 2 is rotation against strain.** For P = 0: 8Q = 2|ω|² − |T|², that is, Q = ¼|ω|² − ½|S|².

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_vorticity_strain
proofs.doc: **Layer 3, the far corner, is strain self-amplification plus vortex stretching.** For P = 0: 8R = det T + ω·Tω, that is, R = det S + ¼ ω·Sω.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_tr_cube
proofs.doc: For a symmetric traceless S (a pure strain), tr(S³) = 3·det S.
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_e2_sumsq
proofs.doc: For a pure traceless strain, −2Q is the sum of the squares of its entries.
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sq_nonneg_int
proofs.doc: A square is never negative (core Lean has no ready-made lemma for it).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_e2_nonpos
proofs.doc: So on the integers (and likewise any ordered ring) Q ≤ 0 for a pure strain: the strain's second layer only ever dissipates.
proofs.statement: (⟨a, b, c, b, e, f, c, f, -a - e⟩ : M3 Int).e2 ≤ 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.e2_expand
proofs.doc: dE2 really is the first-order part of Q.
proofs.statement: (X.addS Y t).e2 = X.e2 + t * dE2 X Y + t^2 * Y.e2

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_expand
proofs.doc: dDet really is the first-order part of det (the second-order part is dDet Y X).
proofs.statement: (X.addS Y t).det = X.det + t * dDet X Y + t^2 * dDet Y X + t^3 * Y.det

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_traceless
proofs.doc: The flow keeps the gradient incompressible.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_dQ
proofs.doc: **Layer 2 is driven by layer 3**: 3·dQ/dt = 9R (so dQ/dt = 3R).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_dR
proofs.doc: **Layer 3 is driven by layer 2 squared**: 3·dR/dt = −2Q² (so dR/dt = −⅔Q²).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_conserved
proofs.doc: **The discriminant is conserved**: along restricted Euler, d/dt (27R² + 4Q³) = 54R·R' + 12Q²·Q' = 0. 27R² + 4Q³ is minus the discriminant of the cube polynomial λ³ + Qλ − R; its zero set is the Vieillefosse tail.
proofs.statement: 54 * X.det * dDet X (reStep X) + 12 * X.e2^2 * dE2 X (reStep X) = 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det2_step
proofs.doc: The 2D step: det(I + hX) = 1 + h·P + h²·Q, the square (1, 2, 1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_cube_2d
proofs.doc: In 2D an incompressible gradient has no third invariant: tr(X³) = 0.
proofs.statement: ((⟨a, b, c, -a⟩ : M2 R).mul ((⟨a, b, c, -a⟩ : M2 R).mul ⟨a, b, c, -a⟩)).tr = 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re2_frozen
proofs.doc: **2D restricted Euler is frozen**: −2A² + tr(A²)·I = 0 for every traceless 2×2 gradient, so the self-advection is cancelled exactly by the pressure.
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.shift_is_corner
proofs.doc: The shift is the corner: S₁Δ₂v = Δ₂v + Δ₁Δ₂v (shift = 1 + Δ).
proofs.statement: d2 v (i + 1) j = d2 v i j + d1 (d2 v) i j

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.minor_is_divergence
proofs.doc: **The corner-kept minor is an exact discrete divergence:** minor = Δ₁(u·Δ₂v) − Δ₂(u·Δ₁v).
proofs.statement: minor u v i j = d1 (fun i j => u i j * d2 v i j) i j - d2 (fun i j => u i j * d1 v i j) i j

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_sub
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun k => f k - g k) n = sumTo f n - sumTo g n

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_telescope
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun k => G (k + 1) - G k) n = G n - G 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_congr
proofs.statement: sumTo f n = sumTo g n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.box_minor_zero
proofs.doc: **The minor sums to zero over a periodic box**: the grid version of "∫ (layer 2 of ∇u) = 0" for a 2D map of the torus.
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun i => sumTo (fun j => minor u v i j) n) n = 0

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tsum_comm
proofs.statement: tsum d S T = tsum d T S

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tsum_assoc
proofs.statement: tsum d (tsum d S T) U = tsum d S (tsum d T U)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tsum_zeroT
proofs.doc: [0] is the identity of tangle addition.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.closeD_tsum
proofs.doc: The lift law is connected sum: closing a sum gives the product of the closures.
proofs.statement: closeD d (tsum d S T) = closeD d S * closeD d T

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tsum_lift
proofs.doc: The homogeneous form of the dial: the [∞]-part of a sum, times d, plus its [0]-part, is the product (f₁ + d g₁)(f₂ + d g₂): the weighted lift 1 + d·x with x = g/f, cleared of fractions.
proofs.statement: (tsum d S T).1 + d * (tsum d S T).2 = (S.1 + d * S.2) * (T.1 + d * T.2)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.closeD_multAdd
proofs.doc: The "mult-add value" P − 1 of a closed diagram turns connected sum into ✳ exactly. (A relabelling: it is the lift of P(K # L) = P(K)·P(L).)
proofs.statement: closeD d (tsum d S T) - 1 = (closeD d S - 1) ✳ (closeD d T - 1)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.poly_multAdd
proofs.doc: The same for any multiplicative knot polynomial (Jones, Alexander, HOMFLY).

proofs.name: KnotTheory.closeD_wall
proofs.doc: The wall: a tangle whose closure has bracket 0 absorbs everything added to it.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tsum_infT
proofs.doc: The second wall, x = ∞: adding [∞] leaves only [∞], carrying the closure ⟨D(S)⟩.
proofs.statement: tsum d S infT = (0, closeD d S)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.vsum_eq_swap
proofs.doc: Stacking is adding, turned a quarter: vsum = swap ∘ tsum ∘ swap.
proofs.statement: vsum d S T = swapT (tsum d (swapT S) (swapT T))

proofs.name: KnotTheory.closeN_vsum
proofs.doc: So the numerator closure is the lift for stacking.
proofs.statement: closeN d (vsum d S T) = closeN d S * closeN d T

proofs.name: KnotTheory.stack_zero_zero
proofs.doc: A loop on its own: [0] stacked on [0] is d·[0].

proofs.name: KnotTheory.weight_is_q_minus_one
proofs.doc: In y = A²·x the dial weight d becomes d·A⁻² = q − 1.
proofs.statement: loopv A Ai * (Ai * Ai) = tq Ai - 1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.y_scale
proofs.doc: Rescaling by A² turns the d-dial into the (q − 1)-dial.
proofs.statement: A * A * wAdd (loopv A Ai) x y = wAdd (tq Ai - 1) (A * A * x) (A * A * y)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.twist_formula
proofs.doc: n twists: [n] = Aⁿ·[0] + Aⁿ·A⁻²·[n]_q·[∞].
proofs.statement: twist A Ai n = (A ^ n, A ^ n * (Ai * Ai) * QDial.qnum (tq Ai) n)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.kink
proofs.doc: One crossing closed up is a kink: ⟨D(X)⟩ = −A⁻³.
proofs.statement: closeD (loopv A Ai) (A, Ai) = -(Ai * Ai * Ai)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.twist_closeD
proofs.doc: Closing [n] gives n kinks: (−A⁻³)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: closeD (loopv A Ai) (twist A Ai n) = (-(Ai * Ai * Ai)) ^ n

proofs.name: KnotTheory.walls_merge
proofs.doc: The twist matrix [[A, 0], [A⁻¹, −A⁻³]] has two eigenvalues, A and −A⁻³ (the two walls); they coincide exactly when A⁴ = −1.
proofs.statement: A = -(Ai * Ai * Ai) ↔ A * A * A * A = -1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.loop_zero
proofs.doc: Where the walls merge the loop value is 0 ...

proofs.name: KnotTheory.q_one
proofs.doc: ... and the tangle q is 1 (the counting point of the dial).

proofs.name: KnotTheory.mirror_q
proofs.doc: Mirror image A ↦ A⁻¹ sends q to 1/q: q(A)·q(A⁻¹) = 1.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.potts_Q
proofs.doc: The Potts number of the loop: Q = d² = t + 2 + t⁻¹ with t = A⁻⁴.
proofs.statement: loopv A Ai * loopv A Ai = Ai * Ai * Ai * Ai + 2 + A * A * A * A

proofs.name: KnotTheory.qnum_mul
proofs.doc: [pq]_t = [p]_t·[q]_(t^p) (the q-number behind Δ(T(p,q)) = [q]_(t^p)/[q]_t).
proofs.statement: QDial.qnum t (p * n) = QDial.qnum t p * QDial.qnum (t ^ p) n

proofs.name: KnotTheory.ratio_dial
proofs.doc: In x = g/f, adding tangles is the weighted mult-add with weight d.
proofs.statement: (tsum d S T).2 / (tsum d S T).1 = wAdd d (S.2 / S.1) (T.2 / T.1)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.lift_is_closing
proofs.doc: The lift 1 + d·x is the closure, divided by the [0]-coefficient.
proofs.statement: 1 + d * (T.2 / T.1) = closeD d T / T.1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.stack_dial
proofs.doc: Stacking is the same dial in z = f/g.
proofs.statement: (vsum d S T).1 / (vsum d S T).2 = wAdd d (S.1 / S.2) (T.1 / T.2)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.twist_step_y
proofs.doc: One crossing added: y ↦ q·y + 1, with y = A²·g/f.
proofs.statement: A * A * (tsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).2 / (tsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).1 = tq Ai * (A * A * S.2 / S.1) + 1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.stack_step_y
proofs.doc: One crossing stacked: 1/y ↦ q⁻¹·(1/y) + 1 (the same step at 1/q, seen through 1/y).
proofs.statement: (vsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).1 / (A * A * (vsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).2) = tq A * (S.1 / (A * A * S.2)) + 1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.step_about_wall
proofs.doc: The q-step is a rotation (|q| = 1) or scaling about its finite wall c = 1/(1 − q).

proofs.name: KnotTheory.twists_on_circle
proofs.doc: So the twists sit on a circle around the wall: [n]_q = c − qⁿ·c.
proofs.statement: QDial.qnum q n = 1 / (1 - q) - q ^ n * (1 / (1 - q))

proofs.name: KnotTheory.twists_close
proofs.doc: At a root of unity qᵐ = 1 the polygon closes: m twists return y to 0.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.conway_twist
proofs.doc: Conway's fraction F = A²·g/f at A⁴ = −1: a crossing adds 1.
proofs.statement: A * A * (tsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).2 / (tsum (loopv A Ai) S (A, Ai)).1 = A * A * S.2 / S.1 + 1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.conway_add
proofs.doc: Conway's fraction is additive under tangle sum (the dial at weight d = 0).
proofs.statement: A * A * (tsum (loopv A Ai) S T).2 / (tsum (loopv A Ai) S T).1 = A * A * S.2 / S.1 + A * A * T.2 / T.1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.conway_stack
proofs.doc: ... and 1/F is additive under stacking.
proofs.statement: (vsum (loopv A Ai) S T).1 / (A * A * (vsum (loopv A Ai) S T).2) = S.1 / (A * A * S.2) + T.1 / (A * A * T.2)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.rational_fractions
proofs.doc: The seven rational knots of the page: 3_1, 4_1, 5_1, 5_2, 6_1, 6_2, 6_3.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.hstep_det
proofs.doc: Both steps keep the determinant p·s − q·r of any two fractions (they are in SL(2, ℤ)).
proofs.statement: (hstep a P).1 * (hstep a Q).2 - (hstep a P).2 * (hstep a Q).1 = P.1 * Q.2 - P.2 * Q.1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.vstep_det
proofs.statement: (vstep a P).1 * (vstep a Q).2 - (vstep a P).2 * (vstep a Q).1 = P.1 * Q.2 - P.2 * Q.1

proofs.name: KnotTheory.hstep_inv
proofs.doc: Twist forward, back: the steps are invertible.

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tangle_trefoil
proofs.doc: Three crossings side by side, closed on top: the right-handed trefoil, the mirror of the left trefoil of QAcross.Knots (bracket A⁻⁷ − A⁻³ − A⁵).
proofs.statement: lcloseN (lbuild [true, true, true]) = mirrorLP (normLP (-9, bracketP 3 6 trefoilL))

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tangle_figEight
proofs.doc: h v h h closed on top (fraction 5/2) is the figure-eight of QAcross.Knots.
proofs.statement: lcloseN (lbuild [true, true, false, true]) = normLP (-12, bracketP 4 8 figEight)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tangle_figEight_D
proofs.doc: h h v v closed at the sides (fraction 2/5) is the figure-eight again.
proofs.statement: lcloseD (lbuild [false, false, true, true]) = normLP (-12, bracketP 4 8 figEight)

proofs.name: KnotTheory.tangle_cinquefoil
proofs.doc: Five crossings closed on top: the cinquefoil (mirror of QAcross.Knots' 5₁).
proofs.statement: lcloseN (lbuild [true, true, true, true, true]) = mirrorLP (normLP (-15, bracketP 5 10 cinquefoilL))

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.num_comm
proofs.doc: commutativity, numerator and denominator separately
proofs.statement: num p a b = num p b a

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.den_comm
proofs.statement: den q a b = den q b a

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.num_zero
proofs.doc: identity: F(a, 0) = a / 1

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.assoc_num
proofs.doc: Associativity, projective form. Composing (a ⊕ b) ⊕ c with fractions N/D gives numerator N + c·D + p·N·c and denominator D − q·N·c; the other bracketing is symmetric. The two numerators are equal and the two denominators are equal, as polynomials.
proofs.statement: num p a b + c * den q a b + p * num p a b * c = a * den q b c + num p b c + p * a * num p b c

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.assoc_den
proofs.statement: den q a b - q * num p a b * c = den q b c - q * a * num p b c

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.inverse_num
proofs.doc: inverse: F(a, −a/(1 + p a)) = 0, cross-multiplied: the numerator vanishes

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_lift
proofs.doc: the lift, cross-multiplied: (D − u N)(1 − v a)(1 − v b) = (D − v N)(1 − u a)(1 − u b)
proofs.statement: (den (u * v) a b - u * num (-(u + v)) a b) * ((1 - v * a) * (1 - v * b)) = (den (u * v) a b - v * num (-(u + v)) a b) * ((1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b))

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_factor_u
proofs.doc: the lift actually factors: D − u N = (1 − u a)(1 − u b), and the same with v
proofs.statement: den (u * v) a b - u * num (-(u + v)) a b = (1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_factor_v
proofs.statement: den (u * v) a b - v * num (-(u + v)) a b = (1 - v * a) * (1 - v * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.multadd_point
proofs.doc: mult-add is the point u = −1, v = 0: walls at −1 and at infinity
proofs.statement: num (-((-1) + 0)) a b = multAdd a b ∧ den ((-1) * 0) a b = 1

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.velocity_point
proofs.doc: velocity addition is u = 1, v = −1: walls at +1 and −1 (the speed of light)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.discriminant
proofs.doc: the parabola: the discriminant of the walls is (u − v)²

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parabola_additive
proofs.doc: the parabola itself (a double wall, u = v): the lens N(x) = x/(1 − u x) turns the law into addition. Cross-multiplied: N·(1 − u a)(1 − u b) = (a(1 − u b) + b(1 − u a))·(D − u N), with D − u N = (1 − u a)(1 − u b).

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parabola_den
proofs.statement: den (u * u) a b - u * num (-(u + u)) a b = (1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.units_num
proofs.doc: rescaling by λ moves a point along a parabola through the origin: (p, q) ↦ (λ p, λ² q)
proofs.statement: num p (lam * a) (lam * b) = lam * num (lam * p) a b

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.units_den
proofs.statement: den q (lam * a) (lam * b) = den (lam * lam * q) a b

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.dial_is_multadd
proofs.doc: the dial: k·(a ⊕ₖ b) = (k a) ⊕ (k b); every k ≠ 0 on the straight line is mult-add in other units
proofs.statement: k * wAdd k a b = multAdd (k * a) (k * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.kdv_phase_shift
proofs.doc: the KdV soliton corner: A(f − 1) with f − 1 = e₁ + e₂ + A e₁e₂ is plain mult-add of A e₁ and A e₂ (each wave moved by its phase shift log A)
proofs.statement: A * wAdd A e1 e2 = multAdd (A * e1) (A * e2)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.rung_equivalent
proofs.doc: so the unit-free shape p²/(p² − 4q) of rung s is s: (4s)² = s·(16 s)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parity_reaches_floor
proofs.doc: at L = 2 (parity) the floor is reached exactly at full error: eigenvalue −1

proofs.name: LeeYang.Mat2.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LeeYang.edge_gas
proofs.doc: One edge of the dial gas: the two-site lattice gas with pair weight k is the lift of the weighted mult-add of the two fugacities.
proofs.statement: 1 + wAdd k x y = 1 + x + y + k * x * y

proofs.name: LeeYang.edge_gas_free
proofs.doc: At k = 1 (q = 2) the two sites are independent: the gas factors.

proofs.name: LeeYang.edge_gas_hardcore
proofs.doc: At k = 0 (q = 1) the two sites exclude each other: hard core.

proofs.name: LeeYang.ringT_tr
proofs.doc: Its trace is the weighted lift of z.

proofs.name: LeeYang.cayley_hamilton
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton for 2×2 matrices: x² = tr(x)·x − det(x)·I.
proofs.statement: mul x x = ⟨tr x * x.a - det x, tr x * x.b, tr x * x.c, tr x * x.d - det x⟩

proofs.name: LeeYang.odd_pow_of_tr_zero
proofs.doc: With trace 0, every odd power is a multiple of x: x^(2m+1) = (−det x)^m · x.
proofs.statement: pow x (2 * m + 1) = smul ((-det x) ^ m) x

proofs.name: LeeYang.tr_odd_pow_zero
proofs.doc: Odd powers of a traceless 2×2 matrix are traceless.

proofs.name: LeeYang.odd_ring_vanishes_on_wall
proofs.doc: **The wall theorem for rings.** The dial gas on a ring of 2m + 1 sites, tr(Tⁿ), vanishes whenever 1 + k·z = 0, that is at z = −1/k, for every weight k.

proofs.name: LeeYang.even_pow_of_tr_zero
proofs.doc: Even powers of a traceless 2×2 matrix are scalar: x^(2m) = (−det x)^m · I.
proofs.statement: pow x (2 * m) = smul ((-det x) ^ m) one

proofs.name: LeeYang.even_ring_on_wall
proofs.doc: On the wall an even ring is 2·(z(1 − k))^m, not zero (unless k = 1).
proofs.statement: tr (pow (ringT k z) (2 * m)) = 2 * (z * (1 - k)) ^ m

proofs.name: LeeYang.triangle_count
proofs.doc: The transfer matrix counts correctly: the 3-ring (triangle) is 1 + 3z + 3k·z² + k³·z³ (each pair of occupied sites shares an edge).
proofs.statement: tr (pow (ringT k z) 3) = 1 + 3 * z + 3 * k * z ^ 2 + k ^ 3 * z ^ 3

proofs.name: LeeYang.square_count
proofs.doc: The 4-ring: 1 + 4z + (2 + 4k)z² + 4k²z³ + k⁴z⁴.

proofs.name: LeeYang.pentagon_count
proofs.doc: The 5-ring: 1 + 5z + (5 + 5k)z² + (5k + 5k²)z³ + 5k³z⁴ + k⁵z⁵.

proofs.name: LeeYang.triangle_factor
proofs.doc: The triangle splits off the wall: (1 + kz) times a quadratic.

proofs.name: LeeYang.triangle_disc
proofs.doc: The quadratic's discriminant: (3 − k)² − 4k² = 3(1 − k)(3 + k). It is ≤ 0 for k ≥ 1 (the two other zeros are a conjugate pair with product 1/k², on the circle |z| = 1/k: Lee–Yang), and > 0 for −3 < k < 1 (real zeros).

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_disc
proofs.doc: The ring's eigenvalue discriminant: (1 + kz)² − 4z(k − 1) = k²z² + (4 − 2k)z + 1. Its zeros are the ends of the zero arc (Yang–Lee edges). At k = 1 it is (1 + z)².

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_zero_family
proofs.doc: The ring's zero family. A ring of n sites vanishes exactly when the two eigenvalues have ratio e^{iφ} with φ = π(2j+1)/n, which is (1 + kz)² = c·z(k − 1) with c = 4cos²(φ/2) in [0, 4]. Each c gives a quadratic in z:

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_family_wall
proofs.doc: c = 0 is the wall, doubled: (1 + kz)².

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_family_edge
proofs.doc: c = 4 is the edge of the zero arc (the eigenvalue discriminant).

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_family_zeta
proofs.doc: In ζ = k·z the family reads k·(ζ² + 1) + (2k − c(k − 1))·ζ = 0 after multiplying by k: so ζ + 1/ζ = c(1 − 1/k) − 2 runs from −2 (the wall, c = 0) to 2 − 4/k (c = 4).

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_edges_vieta
proofs.doc: The two edge points z₁, z₂ of the zero arc satisfy k²·z₁z₂ = 1 (Vieta), so in ζ = k·z they are a reciprocal pair, symmetric under ζ ↦ 1/ζ (the up–down flip of the spins).

proofs.name: LeeYang.ising_ring_transfer
proofs.doc: For Q = 2 (Ising) the formula is the trace of the transfer matrix [[1+v, 1], [1, 1+v]].
proofs.statement: tr (pow (⟨1 + v, 1, 1, 1 + v⟩ : Mat2 R) n) = pottsRing 2 v n

proofs.name: LeeYang.pottsRing_lift
proofs.doc: **The Potts ring is the weighted lift of tⁿ.** With t = v/(Q + v) and k = Q − 1: Z = (Q + v)ⁿ·(1 + k·tⁿ).
proofs.statement: pottsRing Q v n = (Q + v) ^ n * (1 + (Q - 1) * t ^ n)

proofs.name: LeeYang.two_rings
proofs.doc: Two separate rings together: their weights multiply, which in the lift is the weighted mult-add of the two tⁿ, at the dial k = Q − 1.

proofs.name: LeeYang.cycle_chromatic
proofs.doc: Proper colourings: v = −1. The chromatic polynomial of the n-cycle.

proofs.name: LeeYang.colourings_on_wall
proofs.doc: Colourings sit on the wall: v = −1 gives t·(Q + v) = v with t = −1/(Q − 1), i.e. 1 + k·t = 0 for k = Q − 1. (Stated without division: (Q − 1)·t = −1 and t(Q − 1) = −1.)

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_zero_at_q0
proofs.doc: q = 0 (the "or" point, k = −1) is a zero of every ring.

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_zero_at_q1
proofs.doc: q = 1 (plain addition, k = 0) is a zero of every ring with at least one site.

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_zero_at_q2_odd
proofs.doc: q = 2 (mult-add, k = 1) is a zero exactly for odd rings.

proofs.name: LeeYang.ring_at_parity
proofs.doc: q = −1 (parity, k = −2): the ring gives (−1)ⁿ(2ⁿ − 2), the signed number of acyclic orientations of the cycle.

proofs.name: LeeYang.two_pow_ge_four
proofs.doc: The parity point is never a zero of a ring with two or more sites (over Int).

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.small_of_mul
proofs.doc: If a·b = c with c ≠ 0, then |a| ≤ |c|.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha5_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 5: k = golden ratio, k² = k + 1, has no integer solution.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha7_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 7: k = 1 + 2cos(2π/7) is a root of k³ − 2k² − k + 1, which has no integer root.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha8_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 8: k = 1 + √2, k² = 2k + 1, has no integer solution.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha9_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 9: k = 1 + 2cos(2π/9) is a root of k³ − 3k² + 3, which has no integer root.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha10_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 10: k = 1 + golden ratio, k² = 3k − 1, has no integer solution.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.beraha12_not_int
proofs.doc: n = 12: k = 1 + √3, k² = 2k + 2, has no integer solution.

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.wAdd_units
proofs.doc: Units: rescaling the variable by λ turns weight λ·k into weight k.
proofs.statement: lam * wAdd (lam * k) a b = wAdd k (lam * a) (lam * b)

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.leverage_is_compounding
proofs.doc: 2× leverage: weight 2 on unlevered returns is plain mult-add on levered returns.
proofs.statement: 2 * wAdd 2 a b = wAdd 1 (2 * a) (2 * b)

proofs.name: LeeYangCluster.units_bend
proofs.doc: The same move off the axis: the q-coordinate scales by λ², so k²/q is what stays.
proofs.statement: 1 - (lam * lam * q) * a * b = 1 - q * (lam * a) * (lam * b)

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.step_disc
proofs.doc: The step's discriminant: trace² − 4·det = x²·(k² − 4q), the same sign for every step size.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.step_gap
proofs.doc: One step moves a by x·(1 + k·a + q·a²), over the denominator 1 − q·a·x.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.wall_square
proofs.doc: Completing the square: the step's size is a square plus the distance to the border.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.walls_factor
proofs.doc: Two walls: when k² − 4q = m², the step size factors through the two walls, where it is 0.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.border_orbit
proofs.doc: The border (k = 2u, q = u²): n steps of x from 0 land at n·x / (1 − (n − 1)·u·x). Stated for a general t in place of n, cross-multiplied: the step takes the t-th point to the (t+1)-th. The denominator is linear in t: it passes infinity once, then fills toward the double wall −1/u like 1/t, forever.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.sq_nonneg'
proofs.doc: A square is never negative.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.slowest_step
proofs.doc: On the turning side the slowest step is bounded below by the distance to the border: 4q·(1 + k·a + q·a²) ≥ 4q − k² for every a.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.turning_never_stalls
proofs.doc: On the turning side the step never stalls: if q > 0 and 4q > k², the step size is positive.

proofs.name: LeeYangSpill.tan_square
proofs.doc: Tangent addition (k = 0, q = 1) with step 1: a ↦ (a + 1)/(1 − a). Its matrix [[1,1],[−1,1]] squared is [[0,2],[−2,0]] and to the fourth is −4·I, a scalar: every orbit spills through infinity and returns to its start in exactly four steps (tan(θ + π/4)).

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.ext'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.lift
proofs.statement: add one (madd x y) = mul (add one x) (add one y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.wlift
proofs.statement: add one (smul k (wmadd k x y)) = mul (add one (smul k x)) (add one (smul k y))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.madd_assoc
proofs.statement: madd (madd x y) z = madd x (madd y z)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.wmadd_zero_weight
proofs.doc: At weight 0 the corner is gone: plain matrix addition.
proofs.statement: wmadd 0 x y = add x y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.det_one_add_smul
proofs.doc: det(I + kA) = 1 + k·tr A + k²·det A.
proofs.statement: det (add one (smul k x)) = 1 + k * tr x + k * k * det x

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.det_mul
proofs.statement: det (mul x y) = det x * det y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.tr_add
proofs.statement: tr (add x y) = tr x + tr y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.Dk_hom
proofs.doc: The dial homomorphism, for every weight k at once (any commutative ring).
proofs.statement: Dk k (wmadd k x y) = wAdd k (Dk k x) (Dk k y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.shifted_det_hom
proofs.doc: k = 1: the shifted determinant det(I + A) − 1 turns matrix ⊞ into scalar ⊞.
proofs.statement: det (add one (madd x y)) - 1 = multAdd (det (add one x) - 1) (det (add one y) - 1)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.coupling_sets_weight
proofs.doc: det(I + M) − 1 = m₁₁ ⊞_w m₂₂ whenever m₁₂·m₂₁ = (1 − w)·m₁₁·m₂₂.
proofs.statement: det (add one m) - 1 = wAdd w m.a m.d

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.diagonal_is_multAdd
proofs.doc: No coupling (diagonal): mult-add, weight 1.
proofs.statement: det (add one ⟨p, 0, 0, q⟩) - 1 = multAdd p q

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rank_one_is_add
proofs.doc: Rank one (m₁₂m₂₁ = m₁₁m₂₂, determinant 0): plain addition, weight 0.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.madd_not_comm
proofs.doc: Two by two, a matrix never commutes for free: order matters for matrix ⊞.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.orth_lift
proofs.statement: mul (transpose (add one (smul k x))) (add one (smul k x)) = add one (smul k (wmadd k (transpose x) x))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rotation_condition
proofs.doc: For X = [[x, −y], [y, x]], Xᵀ ⊞ₖ X is (2x + k(x² + y²))·I.
proofs.statement: wmadd k (transpose ⟨x, -y, y, x⟩) ⟨x, -y, y, x⟩ = ⟨2 * x + k * (x * x + y * y), 0, 0, 2 * x + k * (x * x + y * y)⟩

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rotation_condition_flat
proofs.doc: k = 0 drops the corner: the condition becomes Xᵀ + X = 0 (skew, the Lie algebra).
proofs.statement: wmadd 0 (transpose x) x = add (transpose x) x
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.lift
proofs.statement: add one (madd x y) = mul (add one x) (add one y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.wlift
proofs.statement: add one (smul k (wmadd k x y)) = mul (add one (smul k x)) (add one (smul k y))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.madd_assoc
proofs.statement: madd (madd x y) z = madd x (madd y z)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.det_one_add_smul
proofs.doc: The mult-add cube of a matrix: det(I + kA) = 1 + k·e₁ + k²·e₂ + k³·e₃.
proofs.statement: det (add one (smul k x)) = 1 + k * tr x + k * k * e2 x + k * k * k * det x

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.det_one_add
proofs.doc: k = 1: det(I + A) = 1 + e₁ + e₂ + e₃.
proofs.statement: det (add one x) = 1 + tr x + e2 x + det x

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.det_mul
proofs.statement: det (mul x y) = det x * det y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.box_cube
proofs.doc: The box picture: stretching the unit cube to (1 + a)(1 + b)(1 + c) adds 3 slabs, 3 beams and 1 corner block: 1, 3, 3, 1.
proofs.statement: det (add one ⟨a, 0, 0, 0, b, 0, 0, 0, c⟩) = 1 + (a + b + c) + (a * b + a * c + b * c) + a * b * c

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.triangular_eigen
proofs.doc: For a triangular matrix (eigenvalues on the diagonal) the shifted determinant is the mult-add of the eigenvalues, as the trace is their sum.
proofs.statement: det (add one x) - 1 = foldMA [x.a11, x.a22, x.a33]

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.tr_add
proofs.statement: tr (add x y) = tr x + tr y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.orth_lift
proofs.statement: mul (transpose (add one (smul k x))) (add one (smul k x)) = add one (smul k (wmadd k (transpose x) x))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M3.Dk_hom
proofs.doc: The 3×3 dial homomorphism for every weight k: k = 0 is trace additivity, k ≠ 0 is det(I + kA) multiplicative.
proofs.statement: M3.Dk k (M3.wmadd k x y) = wAdd k (M3.Dk k x) (M3.Dk k y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.madd_inverse
proofs.doc: Off the wall (det(I + A) ≠ 0) every matrix has a mult-add inverse: (I + A)⁻¹ − I.
proofs.statement: madd x (sub (inv (add one x)) one) = zero

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.msub_undo_W
proofs.statement: madd (mul (sub x (sub w one)) (inv w)) (sub w one) = x

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.msub_undo
proofs.doc: ⊟ undoes ⊞: (X ⊟ A) ⊞ A = X, off the wall.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.cayley_eq
proofs.doc: The Cayley transform of a skew matrix is the rational rotation [[p, q], [−q, p]] with p = (1 − s²)/(1 + s²), q = 2s/(1 + s²).

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.cayley_is_msub
proofs.doc: The Cayley transform is mult-add subtraction of S from its transpose: I + (Sᵀ ⊟ S).
proofs.statement: cayley s = add one (msubM (transpose (skew s)) (skew s))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.cayley_on_circle
proofs.doc: The Cayley point lies on the unit circle (the matrix is a rotation).

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.cayley_on_wall_circle
proofs.doc: The same point, shifted by −1, satisfies the k = 1 rotation condition 2x + x² + y² = 0: it lies on the circle centred at the wall −1.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.rotation_circle
proofs.doc: The weighted rotation condition is a circle through 0 centred at the weighted wall −1/k.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.kdv_two_soliton
proofs.doc: The KdV two-soliton: with the Cauchy-type coupling m² = 4k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)²·E₁E₂, det(I + M) is Hirota's τ = 1 + E₁ + E₂ + ((k₁ − k₂)/(k₁ + k₂))²·E₁E₂.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.fl_sadd
proofs.statement: fl1 m (sadd u1 v1) (sadd u2 v2) = sadd (fl1 m u1 u2) (fl1 m v1 v2) ∧ fl2 m (sadd u1 v1) (sadd u2 v2) = sadd (fl2 m u1 u2) (fl2 m v1 v2)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.fl_scale
proofs.statement: fl1 m (multAdd c v1) (multAdd c v2) = multAdd c (fl1 m v1 v2) ∧ fl2 m (multAdd c v1) (multAdd c v2) = multAdd c (fl2 m v1 v2)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.multAdd_is_zoom
proofs.doc: Mult-adding a is zooming by 1 + a about the wall −1.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.mono_hom
proofs.doc: Monomial maps are the linear maps of rate space: they turn ⊞ into ⊞.
proofs.statement: mono p q (multAdd x1 y1) (multAdd x2 y2) = multAdd (mono p q x1 x2) (mono p q y1 y2)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.mono_compose
proofs.doc: Composing monomial maps multiplies exponent matrices (first row shown; the second row is the same statement with the other row of exponents).

proofs.name: LogicSets.dial_table
proofs.doc: The dial's table on 0 and 1, for every weight k. Only the corner moves: 1 ⊞ₖ 1 = 2 + k.
proofs.statement: wAdd k (0:R) 0 = 0 ∧ wAdd k (0:R) 1 = 1 ∧ wAdd k (1:R) 0 = 1 ∧ wAdd k (1:R) 1 = 2 + k

proofs.name: LogicSets.idem_defect
proofs.doc: **The idempotent defect.** For a² = a and b² = b, (a ⊞ₖ b)² − (a ⊞ₖ b) = (k + 1)(k + 2)·ab.
proofs.statement: wAdd k a b * wAdd k a b - wAdd k a b = (k + 1) * (k + 2) * (a * b)

proofs.name: LogicSets.or_keeps_idem
proofs.doc: At k = −1 (OR) idempotents stay idempotent.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a b * wAdd (-1) a b = wAdd (-1) a b

proofs.name: LogicSets.xor_keeps_idem
proofs.doc: At k = −2 (XOR) idempotents stay idempotent.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-2) a b * wAdd (-2) a b = wAdd (-2) a b

proofs.name: LogicSets.and_keeps_idem
proofs.doc: AND (the product, the corner cell) keeps idempotents for free.

proofs.name: LogicSets.dist_defect
proofs.doc: The distributivity defect: a(b ⊞ₖ c) − (ab ⊞ₖ ac) = k·abc(1 − a).
proofs.statement: a * wAdd k b c - wAdd k (a * b) (a * c) = k * a * b * c * (1 - a)

proofs.name: LogicSets.dist_on_idem
proofs.doc: On an idempotent, AND distributes over every dial value (so over OR and over XOR).
proofs.statement: a * wAdd k b c = wAdd k (a * b) (a * c)

proofs.name: LogicSets.absorb_defect
proofs.doc: The absorption defect: a ⊞₋₁ (ab) = a + ab(1 − a).
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a (a * b) = a + a * b * (1 - a)

proofs.name: LogicSets.absorb_on_idem
proofs.doc: Absorption, both ways, on idempotents: a ∨ (a ∧ b) = a and a ∧ (a ∨ b) = a.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a (a * b) = a ∧ a * wAdd (-1) a b = a

proofs.name: LogicSets.or_self
proofs.doc: OR is idempotent exactly on idempotents: a ⊞₋₁ a − a = a − a².
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a a - a = a - a * a

proofs.name: LogicSets.xor_self
proofs.doc: XOR of a thing with itself: a ⊞₋₂ a = 2(a − a²), zero on idempotents (self-inverse).

proofs.name: LogicSets.or_from_xor_and
proofs.doc: OR is XOR corrected by AND: a ∨ b = (a ⊕ b) ⊕ (a ∧ b) on idempotents.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a b = wAdd (-2) (wAdd (-2) a b) (a * b)

proofs.name: LogicSets.xor_from_or_and
proofs.doc: XOR from OR and AND: a ⊕ b = (a ∨ b)·(1 − ab) on idempotents.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-2) a b = wAdd (-1) a b * (1 - a * b)

proofs.name: LogicSets.or_wall
proofs.doc: OR's wall is "true": 1 absorbs everything under ⊞₋₁.

proofs.name: LogicSets.order_iff
proofs.doc: The order of the Boolean lattice, read on the dial: on idempotents a ⊞₋₁ b = b exactly when a·b = a.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) a b - b = a - a * b

proofs.name: LogicSets.bits_closed_iff
proofs.doc: On the integers: 1 ⊞ₖ 1 is a truth value exactly at k = −1 and k = −2.

proofs.name: LogicSets.fold_or_trues
proofs.doc: n trues folded with OR give 1: [n]_q at q = 0.

proofs.name: LogicSets.fold_xor_trues
proofs.doc: n trues folded with XOR give n mod 2: [n]_q at q = −1.

proofs.name: LogicSets.one_time_pad
proofs.doc: XOR's wall sits at 1/2: a fair key bit hides any message bit (Shannon's one-time pad). This is the library's `wAdd_wall` at k = −2, read as a truth value.

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamS_is_lens
proofs.doc: Every Hamacher t-conorm is a landscape law, at p = γ − 2, q = 1 − γ.
proofs.statement: hamS γ a b = lens (γ - 2) (1 - γ) a b

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamacher_line
proofs.doc: And they all sit on the line p + q = −1.

proofs.name: LogicSets.ham_one
proofs.doc: γ = 1 is the probabilistic sum, the dial at k = −1 (no bend).
proofs.statement: hamS 1 a b = wAdd (-1) a b

proofs.name: LogicSets.ham_two
proofs.doc: γ = 2 is the Einstein sum (a + b)/(1 + ab): relativity's point (0, −1).
proofs.statement: hamS 2 a b = lens 0 (-1) a b

proofs.name: LogicSets.ham_zero_cusp
proofs.doc: γ = 0 sits at (−2, 1), on the border parabola p² = 4q (a double wall).

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamS_miss
proofs.doc: The miss of a Hamacher t-conorm does not depend on γ: 1 − S_γ(a, b) = (1 − a)(1 − b)/(1 + (γ − 1)ab).

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamS_odds
proofs.doc: **Hamacher is the dial on odds.** odds(S_γ(a, b)) = odds a ⊞_γ odds b.
proofs.statement: odds (hamS γ a b) = wAdd γ (odds a) (odds b)

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamT_mirror
proofs.doc: De Morgan: Hamacher's t-norm is the mirror of its t-conorm, T(a, b) = 1 − S(1 − a, 1 − b).
proofs.statement: hamT γ a b = 1 - hamS γ (1 - a) (1 - b)

proofs.name: LogicSets.hamS_bits
proofs.doc: On truth values every Hamacher t-conorm with γ ≠ 0 is OR.
proofs.statement: hamS γ 0 0 = 0 ∧ hamS γ 0 1 = 1 ∧ hamS γ 1 0 = 1 ∧ hamS γ 1 1 = 1

proofs.name: LogicSets.fexp_one_inj
proofs.doc: The fused exponent at base 1 is 2^(n+1) − 1, so it tells exponents apart.
proofs.statement: fexp 1 m = fexp 1 n ↔ m = n

proofs.name: LogicSets.multAdd_definable
proofs.doc: Mult-add is definable from the fused exponent alone: b ⊞ c = d exactly when (a ⊛ b) ⊛ c = a ⊛ d for every a (the tower law).
proofs.statement: b ✳ c = d ↔ ∀ a, fexp (fexp a b) c = fexp a d
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LogicSets.sadd_definable
proofs.doc: Shifted add (rung 0) is definable from the fused exponent and mult-add: b + c + 1 = d exactly when (a ⊛ b) ⊞ (a ⊛ c) = a ⊛ d for every a.
proofs.statement: sadd b c = d ↔ ∀ a, (fexp a b) ✳ (fexp a c) = fexp a d
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LogicSets.zero_definable
proofs.doc: Zero is definable from the fused exponent: the only right identity.
proofs.statement: (∀ a, fexp a y = a) ↔ y = 0
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: LogicSets.succ_and_add
proofs.doc: With 0 in hand the successor is shifted add with 0, and plain + is shifted add, shifted back.
proofs.statement: sadd x 0 = x + 1 ∧ (x + y = z ↔ sadd x y = z + 1)

proofs.name: LogicSets.lift_iso
proofs.doc: Mult-add alone is multiplication in disguise: the lift x ↦ x + 1 carries (Nat, ⊞, 0) onto the positive numbers under ×, one-to-one.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_append
proofs.doc: Disjoint union: μ(A ∪ B) = μ(A) ✳ₖ μ(B).
proofs.statement: lam k (A ++ B) = wAdd k (lam k A) (lam k B)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_lift
proofs.doc: The lift: 1 + λ·μ(A) = ∏ (1 + λ·gᵢ).
proofs.statement: 1 + k * lam k l = prodL (l.map (fun g => 1 + k * g))

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_scale
proofs.doc: λ·μ is plain mult-add of the scaled densities λ·gᵢ.
proofs.statement: k * lam k l = foldMA (l.map (fun g => k * g))

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_corners
proofs.doc: Möbius masses are cube corners: 1 + λμ(A) = Σ over sub-lists S of ∏_{i∈S} λgᵢ.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * lam k l = sumL ((groups (l.map (fun g => k * g))).map prodL)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_three
proofs.doc: The three-atom expansion: layer 1, layer 2 weighted λ, layer 3 weighted λ².
proofs.statement: lam k [a, b, c] = (a + b + c) + k * (a * b + a * c + b * c) + k * k * (a * b * c)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_additive
proofs.doc: λ = 0 is an ordinary additive measure.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_neg_one
proofs.doc: λ = −1: μ(A) = 1 − ∏(1 − gᵢ), the chance at least one atom fires.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_comm_two
proofs.doc: Order of the atoms never matters.
proofs.statement: lam k (A ++ B) = lam k (B ++ A)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.norm_two
proofs.doc: Two atoms: λ = (1 − g₁ − g₂)/(g₁g₂) solves (1 + λg₁)(1 + λg₂) = 1 + λ.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.norm_two_root
proofs.doc: Any nonzero root of the two-atom normalization is that one.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.norm_two_sign
proofs.doc: Two atoms with positive densities: λ > 0 exactly when g₁ + g₂ < 1.
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_incl_excl
proofs.doc: Inclusion–exclusion is multiplication: with atoms x (only A), y (only B), z (both), (1 + λμ(A∪B))(1 + λμ(A∩B)) = (1 + λμ(A))(1 + λμ(B)).
proofs.statement: (1 + k * lam k (X ++ Y ++ Z)) * (1 + k * lam k Z) = (1 + k * lam k (X ++ Z)) * (1 + k * lam k (Y ++ Z))

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.dual_weight
proofs.doc: Duality: if the whole space a, b, c is normalized, the dual measure μ*(S) = 1 − μ(complement) obeys the dial with weight multAddInv λ.
proofs.statement: 1 - c = wAdd (multAddInv k) (1 - wAdd k b c) (1 - wAdd k a c)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.dual_involution
proofs.doc: The dual of the dual weight is the weight again.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.dual_q
proofs.doc: In q = 1 + λ terms the dual is the reciprocal: q* = 1/q.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.lam_equal_atoms
proofs.doc: m equal atoms of size g have measure g·[m]_q with q = 1 + λg.
proofs.statement: lam k (List.replicate m g) = g * qnum (1 + k * g) m

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.wall_blocks
proofs.doc: Below the wall stays below the wall: positive lifts multiply to a positive lift.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.wall_list
proofs.doc: For any list of atoms below the wall, the measure stays below the wall.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.no_norm_past_wall
proofs.doc: So when the wall sits in (0, 1] (k ≤ −1), no such set has measure 1: a normalized λ-measure needs λ > −1.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.sure_atom
proofs.doc: At k = −1 the only way to reach 1 is a sure atom: the product of misses vanishes.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.prodL_eq_zero
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.sure_atom_exists
proofs.doc: k = −1, measure 1 ⇒ some atom has density exactly 1.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.odds_lift
proofs.doc: The lift of the odds is 1/(1 − p).

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.odds_or
proofs.doc: Odds of an independent "or" mult-add: odds(p ✳₋₁ q) = odds p ✳ odds q.
proofs.statement: odds (wAdd (-1) p q) = odds p ✳ odds q

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.against_and
proofs.doc: Odds against an independent "and" mult-add.
proofs.statement: against (p * q) = against p ✳ against q

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.odds_or_three
proofs.doc: Three independent events: the odds of "any" is the three-way mult-add.
proofs.statement: odds (wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) p q) r) = odds p ✳ odds q ✳ odds r

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.Ex_append
proofs.statement: Ex (l ++ m) f = Ex l f + Ex m f

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.Ex_row
proofs.statement: Ex (vs.map (fun bv => ((a, bv.1), w * bv.2))) F = w * Ex vs (fun b => F (a, b))

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.Ex_prod
proofs.doc: Independent product: E[f(X)·g(Y)] = E f(X) · E g(Y).
proofs.statement: Ex (prodD ws vs) (fun ab => f ab.1 * g ab.2) = Ex ws f * Ex vs g

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.indep_dial
proofs.doc: The engine: for independent X and Y (total mass 1 each), E[X ✳ₖ Y] = E X ✳ₖ E Y.
proofs.statement: Ex (prodD ws vs) (fun ab => wAdd k (X ab.1) (Y ab.2)) = wAdd k (Ex ws X) (Ex vs Y)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.dial_gap_cov
proofs.doc: For any joint law (dependent or not), the gap is k times the covariance: the corner's excess.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => wAdd k (X a) (Y a)) - wAdd k (Ex ws X) (Ex ws Y) = k * (Ex ws (fun a => X a * Y a) - Ex ws X * Ex ws Y)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.martingale_step
proofs.doc: Multiplicative martingale step: independent mean-zero returns keep mean zero.
proofs.statement: Ex (prodD ws vs) (fun ab => X ab.1 ✳ Y ab.2) = 0

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.yor
proofs.doc: Yor's formula step by step: ℰ(x) ✳ ℰ(y) = ℰ(x ✳ y) increment-wise, where Δx ✳ Δy = Δx + Δy + ΔxΔy carries the bracket [X, Y].
proofs.statement: sexp xs ✳ sexp ys = sexp (List.zipWith multAdd xs ys)

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.yor_step
proofs.doc: One step: the increment of X + Y + [X, Y] is exactly Δx ✳ Δy.

proofs.name: MeasureProbability.sexp_inverse
proofs.doc: The self-bracket: one step of ℰ(x) against its own mult-add inverse is flat.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.mpow_one_nat
proofs.doc: Mult-adding 1 to itself n times counts the nonempty corners of the n-cube: 1^(⊞n) + 1 = 2ⁿ.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.box_doubles
proofs.doc: Doubling the side of an n-dimensional box of side 2ʲ multiplies its cells by 2ⁿ.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.annulus_cells
proofs.doc: **The dyadic annulus is a mult-add power.** The new cells added when a box of side 2ʲ doubles number 2^(nj) · 1^(⊞n): the old box times the n-fold mult-add of 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.annulus_graded
proofs.doc: **The annulus is graded by the cube's layers.** 2ⁿ − 1 = Σ_{k=1..n} C(n,k): the new cells of a doubled box split by how many of the n coordinates landed in the upper half (k = 1 strips, k = 2 corners, …, k = n the far corner).
proofs.statement: (2 : Int) ^ n - 1 = bsum (fun k => (layer n (k + 1) : Int) * 1 ^ (k + 1)) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.onRay_refl
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.onRay_trans
proofs.doc: Lying on one ray is transitive (away from the pivot dimension n = −2), so the rays split the plane: sliding the dimension and sliding the dissipation are one dial.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.lions_on_2d_ray
proofs.doc: Lions' 3D threshold α = 5/4 is on the same ray as 2D Navier–Stokes (α = 1): both are critical.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.ns3d_on_ray_of_2d_four_fifths
proofs.doc: 3D Navier–Stokes (α = 1) is on the same ray as 2D flow with dissipation power α = 4/5. (2D is smooth there anyway, for a reason scaling cannot see: §5.)

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.ns3d_supercritical
proofs.doc: 3D Navier–Stokes is off the critical ray: the scaling gap is a quarter power.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.fan_pivot
proofs.doc: The three known thresholds are rays: critical α = (n+2)/4, the dyadic regularity line α = (n+2)/5 (Barbato–Morandin–Romito) and the dyadic blow-up line α = (n+2)/6 (Cheskidov). In twentieths: 5(n+2), 4(n+2), (10/3)(n+2); all three vanish at the pivot n = −2.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.ns3d_on_bmr_line
proofs.doc: 3D Navier–Stokes lies exactly on the dyadic regularity line A = 4(n+2).

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.gain_is_model
proofs.doc: The gain is aⱼ times the model's nonlinear term.

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.energy_telescopes
proofs.doc: **Energy only moves.** Summed over shells 0..N, the nonlinear gains telescope to minus the flux out of the top shell.
proofs.statement: ∀ N, ssum (gain c a) (N + 1) = -(flux c a N)

proofs.name: MultAdd.NSContinuum.planar_stretching_zero
proofs.statement: stretch G (fun k => if k = 2 then w else 0) i = 0

proofs.name: FusedRungs.shell_energy
proofs.statement: c0 s0 s1 s2 l + c1 s0 s1 s2 l - c2 s0 s1 s2 l = 0

proofs.name: FusedRungs.shell_helicity
proofs.doc: Helicity is conserved for every sign corner and every shell ratio l, as a polynomial identity (it does not even need s² = 1).
proofs.statement: s0 * c0 s0 s1 s2 l + s1 * l * c1 s0 s1 s2 l - s2 * l ^ 2 * c2 s0 s1 s2 l = 0

proofs.name: FusedRungs.homochiral_layers
proofs.doc: The homochiral corners (+++) and (---) are exactly layers 0 and 3.

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.mul_rule
proofs.doc: the multiplication really is "u² = k u − q": expand (a + b u)(c + d u) and replace u²
proofs.statement: (a + b * u) * (c + d * u) = mre q a b c d + mu k a b c d * u
