proofs.name: SimpleLaws.mul_comm_re
proofs.statement: mre q a b c d = mre q c d a b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.mul_comm_u
proofs.statement: mu k a b c d = mu k c d a b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.mul_assoc_re
proofs.doc: associativity, real part and u-part
proofs.statement: mre q (mre q a b c d) (mu k a b c d) e f = mre q a b (mre q c d e f) (mu k c d e f)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.mul_assoc_u
proofs.statement: mu k (mre q a b c d) (mu k a b c d) e f = mu k a b (mre q c d e f) (mu k c d e f)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.tilted_re
proofs.doc: (1 + x u)(1 + y u): its real part is the landscape denominator
proofs.statement: mre q 1 x 1 y = LandscapeMap.den q x y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.tilted_u
proofs.doc: ... and its u-part is the landscape numerator, the weighted mult-add of x and y
proofs.statement: mu k 1 x 1 y = LandscapeMap.num k x y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.multadd_point_u
proofs.doc: at mult-add's own point (k, q) = (1, 0) the unit is idempotent (u² = u) and the u-part is plain mult-add, with real part 1: nothing to divide by
proofs.statement: mu 1 1 x 1 y = multAdd x y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.complex_point
proofs.doc: the complex corner (0, 1), u = i: slopes add like tangents, (x + y)/(1 − x y)
proofs.statement: mu 0 1 x 1 y = x + y ∧ mre 1 1 x 1 y = 1 - x * y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.split_point
proofs.doc: the split corner (0, −1), u² = 1: velocity addition, (x + y)/(1 + x y)
proofs.statement: mu 0 1 x 1 y = x + y ∧ mre (-1) 1 x 1 y = 1 + x * y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.dual_point
proofs.doc: the dual corner (0, 0), u² = 0: Galileo's velocity addition, plain x + y over 1
proofs.statement: mu 0 1 x 1 y = x + y ∧ mre 0 1 x 1 y = 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_mul
proofs.doc: the norm multiplies (the generalized Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity)
proofs.statement: norm k q (mre q a b c d) (mu k a b c d) = norm k q a b * norm k q c d

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_conj
proofs.doc: the norm is the number times its conjugate: with ū = k − u, (a + b u)(a + b ū) = N
proofs.statement: (a + b * u) * (a + b * (k - u)) = norm k q a b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.four_norm
proofs.doc: 4·N splits as a square plus (4q − k²)·b²: the sign of 4q − k² picks the country
proofs.statement: 4 * norm k q a b = (2 * a + k * b) * (2 * a + k * b) + (4 * q - k * k) * (b * b)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.sq_nonneg
proofs.doc: a square is never negative (core Lean has no lemma by this name, so we prove it)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_nonneg_turning
proofs.doc: turning country: when 4q ≥ k² the norm is never negative (a true length)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_border
proofs.doc: border: when k² = 4q the norm is one square, (2a + k b)²/4 (Galileo: lengths only one way)
proofs.statement: 4 * norm k q a b = (2 * a + k * b) * (2 * a + k * b)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_walls
proofs.doc: two walls: write k = −(r + s), q = r s; the norm splits into two light-cone factors
proofs.statement: norm (-(r + s)) (r * s) a b = (a - r * b) * (a - s * b)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_complex
proofs.doc: Pythagoras at the complex corner: a² + b²
proofs.statement: norm 0 1 a b = a * a + b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_split
proofs.doc: the spacetime interval at the split corner: a² − b²
proofs.statement: norm 0 (-1) a b = a * a - b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_dual
proofs.doc: Galileo at the dual corner: only a² survives

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_multadd
proofs.doc: at (1, 0) the norm is a·(a + b): in the coordinates X = a, Y = a + b it is X·Y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_multadd_tilted
proofs.doc: the tilted one 1 + x u at mult-add's point has norm 1·(1 + x): its lift

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.norm_multadd_lift
proofs.doc: the product of two tilted ones has norm (1 + x)(1 + y) = 1 + (x ⊞ y)
proofs.statement: norm 1 0 (mre 0 1 x 1 y) (mu 1 1 x 1 y) = 1 + multAdd x y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.unit_circle_is_hyperbola
proofs.doc: the unit circle N = 1 at mult-add's point is the curve x ⊞ y = 0, i.e. (1 + x)(1 + y) = 1: a hyperbola whose asymptotes are the walls x = −1 and y = −1

proofs.name: Numerical.relerr_mul
proofs.doc: Multiply two perturbed values: the relative errors mult-add.

proofs.name: Numerical.relerr_mul3
proofs.doc: Three perturbed factors: the errors fold.

proofs.name: Numerical.theta_is_fold
proofs.doc: Higham's θₙ: the product of the factors (1 + δᵢ), minus 1, is the mult-add fold.

proofs.name: Numerical.chain_eq
proofs.statement: chain ds p = p * (1 + foldMA ds)

proofs.name: Numerical.multAdd_sensitivity
proofs.doc: Perturbing a value moves a ✳ b by exactly h·(1 + b): the sensitivity is the other lift.

proofs.name: Numerical.newton_residual
proofs.doc: The residual squares (with a sign): the corner e·e is all that is left.
proofs.statement: u ✳ newton u v = -((u ✳ v) * (u ✳ v))

proofs.name: Numerical.newton_iter_residual
proofs.doc: After n steps the residual is −(−e₀)^(2ⁿ): quadratic convergence, digits double.
proofs.statement: ∀ (n : Nat) (v : R), u ✳ newtonIter u n v = -(pw (-(u ✳ v)) (2 ^ n))

proofs.name: Numerical.newton_fixed
proofs.doc: At the exact inverse the residual is 0 and Newton stands still.

proofs.name: Numerical.gold_eq
proofs.statement: ∀ n, gold e n = -(pw e (2 ^ n))

proofs.name: Numerical.gold_lift
proofs.statement: 1 + gold e n = 1 - pw e (2 ^ n)

proofs.name: Numerical.hornerMA_eq
proofs.statement: hornerMA acc bs = acc ✳ foldMA bs

proofs.name: Numerical.horner_cube
proofs.doc: Starting from 0, the n Horner steps give the whole cube: every corner product once.

proofs.name: Numerical.mpow_horner
proofs.doc: Mult-adding the same b n times is Horner on the polynomial b(1 + y + … + yⁿ⁻¹), y = 1 + b.
proofs.statement: ∀ n, mpow b n = horner (1 + b) (List.replicate n b)

proofs.name: Numerical.mpow_double
proofs.doc: Powers by squaring: a^(✳2n) = a^(✳n) ✳ a^(✳n).
proofs.statement: mpow a (2 * n) = mpow a n ✳ mpow a n

proofs.name: Numerical.relerr_div
proofs.doc: Divide two perturbed values: the relative errors mult-subtract (Fisher's rule).
proofs.statement: (x * (1 + d₁)) / (y * (1 + d₂)) = (x / y) * (1 + msub d₁ d₂)

proofs.name: Numerical.lift_amplifier
proofs.doc: The way back from the lift: a relative rounding η of 1 + a becomes η·(1 + a)/a in a.

proofs.name: Numerical.inverse_sensitivity
proofs.doc: The inverse's exact sensitivity: only 1 + u near 0 (the wall) makes it large.
proofs.statement: multAddInv (u + h) - multAddInv u = -h / ((1 + u) * (1 + u + h))

proofs.name: Numerical.inverse_lift
proofs.doc: The fused inverse undoes the lift's reciprocal: 1 + inv u = 1/(1 + u).

proofs.name: Numerical.sterbenz_window_pos
proofs.doc: Sterbenz's window, part 1: for 0 ≤ a ≤ 1 (lift in [1, 2]) the inverse b lies in [−2a, −a/2], so a + b is computed exactly in floating point.

proofs.name: Numerical.sterbenz_window_neg
proofs.doc: Sterbenz's window, part 2: for −1/2 ≤ a ≤ 0 (lift in [1/2, 1]) the inverse b lies in [−a/2, −2a].

proofs.name: Numerical.multAdd_bound
proofs.doc: |a| ≤ u and |t| ≤ M give |a ✳ t| ≤ u ✳ M (the corner of the bounds bounds the corner).
proofs.statement: -(u ✳ M) ≤ a ✳ t ∧ a ✳ t ≤ u ✳ M

proofs.name: Numerical.theta_bound
proofs.doc: Higham's Lemma 3.1 in mult-add form: n step errors of size at most u fold to at most (1 + u)ⁿ − 1 = u^(✳n).
proofs.statement: ∀ (ds : List Rat), (∀ d ∈ ds, -u ≤ d ∧ d ≤ u) → -(mpow u ds.length) ≤ foldMA ds ∧ foldMA ds ≤ mpow u ds.length

proofs.name: Numerical.gamma_lift
proofs.doc: (1 + u)ⁿ(1 − nu) ≤ 1 for u ≥ 0: the γₙ bound without division.

proofs.name: Numerical.gamma_bound
proofs.doc: γₙ: u^(✳n)·(1 − nu) ≤ nu, i.e. (1 + u)ⁿ − 1 ≤ nu/(1 − nu) whenever nu < 1.
proofs.statement: mpow u n * (1 - n * u) ≤ n * u

proofs.name: Numerical.bernoulli
proofs.doc: Bernoulli: compounding never loses to simple interest, a^(✳n) ≥ n·a for a ≥ −1.
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Nat, (n : Rat) * a ≤ mpow a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.recip_diff
proofs.doc: The clock of the Riccati climb: reciprocals of the lift.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.ric_lift
proofs.doc: Under the lift it is a reciprocal: 1 + y = 1/(1 − t). The time left, 1 − t, is the clock.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.ric_step
proofs.doc: **The exact difference law.** y(t+h) − y(t) = h·(1+y(t))(1+y(t+h)): the trapezoid-free discrete form of y' = (1+y)², with no error term.
proofs.statement: ric (t + h) - ric t = h * (1 + ric t) * (1 + ric (t + h))

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.ric_step_multAdd
proofs.doc: The same law in mult-add: the step is h times the lift of y(t) ⊞ y(t+h).
proofs.statement: ric (t + h) - ric t = h * (1 + multAdd (ric t) (ric (t + h)))

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.riccati_clock_step
proofs.doc: Read in the clock coordinate, the climb is uniform: one step of the law lowers 1/(1+y) by exactly h.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.steps_add
proofs.statement: steps h (m + n) = steps h m + steps h n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.riccati_clock
proofs.doc: **The discrete Riccati climb runs on a straight clock.** As long as the lift stays off the wall, 1/(1+yₙ) = 1/(1+y₀) − n·h.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.riccati_hits_wall
proofs.doc: **Blow-up.** If the clock starts at m·h, the climb cannot take m steps with finite values: at step m the clock reads 0, and no finite y has 1/(1+y) = 0. (Continuous form: the blow-up time is ∫₀^∞ ds/(1+s)² = 1.)

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.mirror_step
proofs.doc: **The mirror.** Through the mult-add inverse v = −u/(1+u), a Riccati step is a step of exactly −h: the climb to infinity is a walk at constant speed into the wall −1. Blow-up at infinity and leaving the wall are one question, swapped by the mult-add inverse.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.mirror_lift
proofs.doc: The mirrored walk reaches the wall exactly when the climb blows up: 1 + (−u/(1+u)) = 1/(1+u).

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rung1_lift
proofs.doc: **The rung-1 climb never reaches the wall.** If yₙ₊₁ = yₙ ⊞ h then 1 + yₙ = (1 + y₀)(1 + h)ⁿ: the clock log₁₊ y advances by log(1+h) per step forever (continuous form: ∫ ds/(1+s) = log(1+s) → ∞).

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rung1_never_wall
proofs.doc: On the rationals the rung-1 climb stays on the safe side of the wall forever.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.steps_quarter
proofs.doc: With h = 1/4 the Riccati clock started at 1 reads 0 after 4 steps: the climb from y₀ = 0 blows up at step 4 = 1/h.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.ric_near_one
proofs.doc: The continuous climb passes every height before t = 1: y(1 − 1/(M+2)) = M + 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.time_left_pos
proofs.doc: … and that time is still before 1: the time left 1/(M+2) is positive.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.root_sq
proofs.statement: root c n ^ 2 = fan c n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fan_step
proofs.doc: **Every fan member solves the trapezoid scheme of x' = 2√x.**
proofs.statement: fan c (n + 1) = fan c n + root c n + root c (n + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fan_zero
proofs.doc: Every fan member starts at 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fan_distinct
proofs.doc: **Different start times give different solutions**, so the scheme has infinitely many solutions from x(0) = 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.lipschitz_unique
proofs.doc: **Lipschitz means unique.** The trapezoid scheme of x' = x, x(n+1) − x(n) = (h/2)(x(n) + x(n+1)), started at 0 stays at 0 (for h ≠ 2).

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fsum_append
proofs.statement: ∀ n, fsum a s (m + n) = fsum a s m + fsum a (s + m) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fsum_mono
proofs.statement: ∀ len, (∀ i, i < len → a (s + i) ≤ b (s + i)) → fsum a s len ≤ fsum b s len

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.const_block
proofs.doc: A constant over a block of length 2ʲ sums to 2ʲ·c.
proofs.statement: ∀ s, fsum (fun _ => c) s (2 ^ j) = (2 : Rat) ^ j * c

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.block_start
proofs.doc: **The blocks are the mult-add lattice.** The j-th block starts at 2ʲ = 1 + 1^(⊞j), the lift of the j-fold mult-add of 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.blk_le
proofs.statement: blk a j ≤ (2 : Rat) ^ j * a (2 ^ j)

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.le_blk
proofs.statement: (2 : Rat) ^ j * a (2 ^ (j + 1)) ≤ blk a j

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.dsum_succ
proofs.statement: dsum a (n + 1) = dsum a n + blk a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.dsum_le_csum
proofs.doc: **Upper squeeze.** a(1) + … + a(2ⁿ − 1) ≤ Σ_{j<n} 2ʲ·a(2ʲ).
proofs.statement: ∀ n, dsum a n ≤ csum a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.csum_le_dsum
proofs.statement: ∀ n, csum a (n + 1) ≤ a 1 + 2 * dsum a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.condensation
proofs.doc: **The test is the same one rung down.** For shrinking nonnegative terms, the dyadic partial sums are bounded iff the condensed sums are.
proofs.statement: (∃ B, ∀ n, csum a n ≤ B) ↔ (∃ B, ∀ n, dsum a n ≤ B)

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.fsum_le_dsum
proofs.doc: Every partial sum a(1) + … + a(N) sits under a dyadic one, so the dyadic sums decide boundedness of all partial sums.
proofs.statement: fsum a 1 N ≤ dsum a N

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.nr_add
proofs.statement: ∀ n, nr (m + n) = nr m + nr n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.csum_harm
proofs.doc: One rung down, the harmonic terms become all ones: 2ʲ · (1/2ʲ) = 1.
proofs.statement: ∀ n, csum harm n = nr n

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.harmonic_grows
proofs.doc: **Rung 0 passes.** 1 + 1/2 + … + 1/(2ⁿ − 1) ≥ n/2: the clock never stops.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.csum_isq
proofs.doc: One rung down, the inverse squares become a geometric series: Σ_{j<n} 2ʲ/4ʲ = 2 − 2/2ⁿ.
proofs.statement: ∀ n, csum isq n = 2 - 2 * (1 / (2 : Rat) ^ n)

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.inverse_squares_bounded
proofs.doc: **One power past rung 0 fails the test (the sum converges).** 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + … + 1/(2ⁿ − 1)² ≤ 2 for every n.

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rot_speed
proofs.doc: Both have speed r³ (speed² = r⁶): the size alone fails the Osgood test.
proofs.statement: rot1 x y ^ 2 + rot2 x y ^ 2 = (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) ^ 3

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rad_speed
proofs.statement: rad1 x y ^ 2 + rad2 x y ^ 2 = (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) ^ 3

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rot_perp
proofs.doc: **The rotation pushes sideways:** x·F = 0, so d/dt |x|² = 2x·F = 0 and the size never changes, though the speed fails the Osgood test.
proofs.statement: x * rot1 x y + y * rot2 x y = 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.OsgoodInverse.rad_out
proofs.doc: **The radial field pushes straight out:** x·F = r⁴, so ρ = r² obeys ρ' = 2ρ², the Riccati law of §1, and blows up at time 1/(2ρ₀).
proofs.statement: x * rad1 x y + y * rad2 x y = (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) ^ 2

proofs.name: Patterns.step_num
proofs.doc: The step's top entry is the law's numerator: x + a·y + k·x·a (for y = 1, wAdd k x a).
proofs.statement: (step k q a (x, y)).1 = x + a * y + k * x * a

proofs.name: Patterns.step_den
proofs.doc: The step's bottom entry is the law's denominator: y − q·x·a (for y = 1, 1 − q·x·a).
proofs.statement: (step k q a (x, y)).2 = y - q * x * a

proofs.name: Patterns.step_is_law
proofs.doc: With y = 1 the step is exactly the law: numerator wAdd k x a, denominator 1 − q·x·a.
proofs.statement: step k q a (x, 1) = (wAdd k x a, 1 - q * x * a)

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_succ_succ
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (n + 2) = P * lucas P Q (n + 1) - Q * lucas P Q n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Patterns.iter_lucas
proofs.doc: The heart of it: n + 1 copies of a, in any law of the map, are (a·U(n+1), U(n+1) − Q·U n) with P = 2 + k·a and Q = 1 + k·a + q·a².
proofs.statement: iter k q a (n + 1) = (a * lucas (2 + k * a) (1 + k * a + q * a * a) (n + 1), lucas (2 + k * a) (1 + k * a + q * a * a) (n + 1) - (1 + k * a + q * a * a) * lucas (2 + k * a) (1 + k * a + q * a * a) n)

proofs.name: Patterns.step_trace
proofs.doc: The trace of the step is P = 2 + k·a.

proofs.name: Patterns.step_det
proofs.doc: The determinant of the step is Q = 1 + k·a + q·a²: the law's wall polynomial.

proofs.name: Patterns.wall_absorbs
proofs.doc: A wall is where the determinant vanishes: adding a wall value w sends every pair onto the wall (top = w · bottom), whatever it started as. This is absorption.
proofs.statement: (step k q w (x, y)).1 = w * (step k q w (x, y)).2

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_add_pair
proofs.doc: Associativity of the law, read on the counting sequence, is Lucas's addition rule: U(m+n+1) = U(m+1)·U(n+1) − Q·U m·U n. Proved for the pair (n, n+1) together.
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (m + n + 1) = lucas P Q (m + 1) * lucas P Q (n + 1) - Q * lucas P Q m * lucas P Q n ∧ lucas P Q (m + n + 2) = lucas P Q (m + 1) * lucas P Q (n + 2) - Q * lucas P Q m * lucas P Q (n + 1)

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_add
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (m + n + 1) = lucas P Q (m + 1) * lucas P Q (n + 1) - Q * lucas P Q m * lucas P Q n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Patterns.cassini
proofs.doc: Cassini's identity is the determinant of n steps: U(n+1)² − U n·U(n+2) = Qⁿ.
proofs.statement: lucas P Q (n + 1) * lucas P Q (n + 1) - lucas P Q n * lucas P Q (n + 2) = Q ^ n

proofs.name: Patterns.cycle_of_lucas_zero
proofs.doc: If U(n+1) = 0 then n + 1 copies of a land back on 0: a cycle.

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_five
proofs.doc: The fifth term: U 5 = (P² − Q)² − Q·P².
proofs.statement: lucas P Q 5 = (P * P - Q) * (P * P - Q) - Q * (P * P)

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_five_golden
proofs.doc: With Q = 1 (a step of determinant 1, a pure turn), the five-cycle condition factors into the two golden quadratics: U 5 = (P² − P − 1)(P² + P − 1).
proofs.statement: lucas P 1 5 = (P * P - P - 1) * (P * P + P - 1)

proofs.name: Patterns.multadd_den_one
proofs.doc: Mult-add (k, q) = (1, 0): the denominator is always 1, U(n+1) − (1 + a)·U n = 1.

proofs.name: Patterns.multadd_iter
proofs.doc: Mult-add's counting pair is ((1 + a)^(n+1) − 1, 1), via the Lucas formula.

proofs.name: Patterns.golden_step
proofs.doc: The Fibonacci law (k, q) = (−1, −1): adding 1 is the Fibonacci step (x, y) ↦ (y, x + y).

proofs.name: Patterns.ladder_is_step
proofs.doc: The resistor ladder of the simple-laws page is one step of the mirror law (1, −1).

proofs.name: Patterns.mirror_num
proofs.doc: Mirror: flipping the sign of every value takes the law at (k, q) to the law at (−k, q).

proofs.name: Patterns.golden_walls
proofs.doc: The golden walls: the Fibonacci law's wall polynomial is 1 − a − a², whose roots are 1/φ and −φ (stated as: w is a wall exactly when w² + w = 1).

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_fib_pair
proofs.doc: The Lucas sequence with P = 1, Q = −1 is Fibonacci.
proofs.statement: lucas (1 : Int) (-1) n = SimpleLaws.fib n ∧ lucas (1 : Int) (-1) (n + 1) = SimpleLaws.fib (n + 1)

proofs.name: Patterns.lucas_fib
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Patterns.golden_law_fib
proofs.doc: In the law a ⊕ b = (a + b − ab)/(1 + ab), adding 1 to itself n + 1 times gives F(n+1)/F(n+2): 1, 1/2, 2/3, 3/5, 5/8, …, marching into the golden wall 1/φ.

proofs.name: Patterns.golden_cassini
proofs.doc: Cassini for the golden law: F(n+1)² − F n·F(n+2) = (−1)ⁿ, the determinant (−1) per step.
proofs.statement: SimpleLaws.fib (n + 1) * SimpleLaws.fib (n + 1) - SimpleLaws.fib n * SimpleLaws.fib (n + 2) = (-1 : Int) ^ n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Patterns.disc_square_or_ge_five
proofs.doc: The smallest irrational walls. For whole-number k and q the wall discriminant k² − 4q is either a perfect square or at least 5. So the first integer law whose walls are irrational has discriminant 5: the golden walls, at (k, q) = (±1, −1).
proofs.statement: ∃ s : Int, k * k - 4 * q = s * s

proofs.name: Patterns.no_integer_five_cycle
proofs.doc: No whole-number turn has period 5. With determinant 1 and a whole-number trace P, the fifth Lucas term P⁴ − 3P² + 1 is odd, so never 0. A five-cycle needs a golden trace.

proofs.name: Patterns.mfib_lift_pair
proofs.doc: Flatten it and the exponents are Fibonacci numbers: 1 + x(n+1) = (1 + x0)^F(n) · (1 + x1)^F(n+1).
proofs.statement: 1 + mfib x0 x1 (n + 1) = (1 + x0) ^ nfib n * (1 + x1) ^ nfib (n + 1) ∧ 1 + mfib x0 x1 (n + 2) = (1 + x0) ^ nfib (n + 1) * (1 + x1) ^ nfib (n + 2)

proofs.name: Patterns.mfib_lift
proofs.statement: 1 + mfib x0 x1 (n + 1) = (1 + x0) ^ nfib n * (1 + x1) ^ nfib (n + 1)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: Patterns.mfib_one_one
proofs.doc: From 1, 1: the mult-add Fibonacci numbers are 2^F(n) − 1 (1, 1, 3, 7, 31, 255, 8191, …), stated as 1 + x(n+1) = (1 + 1)^F(n+2) in any number system.

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.gma_lift
proofs.statement: G.add G.one (gma a b) = G.mul (G.add G.one a) (G.add G.one b)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.gma_comm
proofs.statement: gma a b = gma b a

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.gma_assoc
proofs.statement: gma (gma a b) c = gma a (gma b c)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.mul_assoc'
proofs.statement: G.mul (G.mul a b) c = G.mul a (G.mul b c)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.gpow_lift
proofs.doc: the lift of a mult-add power is an ordinary power: 1 + a^(⊞n) = (1 + a)ⁿ
proofs.statement: G.add G.one (gpow a n) = G.pow (G.add G.one a) n

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.norm_mul
proofs.doc: lengths multiply (Brahmagupta–Fibonacci)
proofs.statement: G.norm (G.mul a b) = G.norm a * G.norm b

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.circle_closed
proofs.doc: the circle |1 + a| = 1 (centre: the wall −1, radius 1) is closed under mult-add
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.circle_real_points
proofs.doc: On the real line (Rat), the circle (1 + x)² = 1 is exactly the two points 0 and −2.

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.multAdd_self_zero
proofs.doc: in mult-add units: x ⊞ x = 0 (a half turn twice is a full turn) exactly at 0 and −2

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.lens
proofs.doc: THE LENS. Slope addition is exactly Gaussian multiplication.
proofs.statement: toG (tl x y) = G.mul (toG x) (toG y)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.lens_conj
proofs.doc: and the conjugates multiply the same way, so the lift W/W̄ of a sum is the product of the lifts: 1 + a(x ⊕ y) = (1 + a(x))·(1 + a(y)), i.e. a(x ⊕ y) = a(x) ⊞ a(y).
proofs.statement: G.conj (toG (tl x y)) = G.mul (G.conj (toG x)) (G.conj (toG y))

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.lens_on_circle
proofs.doc: every real slope lands on the circle: W and W̄ have the same length, so |W/W̄| = 1

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.lens_zero
proofs.doc: slope 0 lands on the identity: W = W̄, lift 1, a = 0
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.lens_infinity
proofs.doc: slope ∞ lands on the parity point: W = −W̄, lift −1, a = −2

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.slope_one_twice
proofs.doc: the same in slopes: 1 ⊕ 1 = 2/0 = ∞, and four steps of slope 1 come back to slope 0

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.parity_twice
proofs.doc: the parity point is its own way back: (−2) ⊞ (−2) = 0

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.machin
proofs.doc: Machin (1706): four steps of i/5, one step back of i/239

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.euler
proofs.doc: Euler: one step of i/2, one of i/3

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.hermann
proofs.doc: Hermann: two steps of i/2, one back of i/7

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.hutton
proofs.doc: Hutton: two steps of i/3, one of i/7

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.machin_slopes
proofs.doc: Machin again, in the turning law itself: 1/5 ⊕ 1/5 ⊕ 1/5 ⊕ 1/5 ⊕ (−1/239) = 1

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.cross_10
proofs.doc: 32 steps of i/10 pass −2; 31 do not

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.cross_100
proofs.doc: 315 steps of i/100

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.cross_1000
proofs.doc: 3142 steps of i/1000

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.div_le_div_of
proofs.doc: a'/d ≤ a/b when 0 < b ≤ d and 0 ≤ a' ≤ a

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.term_shrink
proofs.doc: the terms shrink for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.greg_two
proofs.statement: greg x (2 * m + 2) = greg x (2 * m) + gt x (2 * m) - gt x (2 * m + 1)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.greg_even_up
proofs.doc: even partial sums climb
proofs.statement: greg x (2 * m) ≤ greg x (2 * m + 2)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.greg_odd_above
proofs.doc: each odd partial sum sits above the even one before it
proofs.statement: greg x (2 * m) ≤ greg x (2 * m + 1)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.greg_odd_down
proofs.doc: odd partial sums fall
proofs.statement: greg x (2 * m + 3) ≤ greg x (2 * m + 1)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.greg_even_le_odd
proofs.doc: so [even sum, odd sum] is a nested interval: every even sum sits below every odd sum
proofs.statement: greg x (2 * m) ≤ greg x (2 * n + 1)

proofs.name: PiMultAdd.machin_nested
proofs.doc: the Machin intervals nest: the lower end climbs and the upper end falls with N
proofs.statement: machinLo N ≤ machinLo (N + 1) ∧ machinHi (N + 1) ≤ machinHi N

proofs.name: PowersetDials.sumL_map_append
proofs.statement: sumL ((l ++ m).map f) = sumL (l.map f) + sumL (m.map f)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.sumL_map_mul
proofs.statement: sumL (l.map (fun a => k * f a)) = k * sumL (l.map f)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.sumL_vecs_succ
proofs.statement: sumL ((vecs (n + 1)).map F) = sumL ((vecs n).map (fun a => F (false :: a))) + sumL ((vecs n).map (fun a => F (true :: a)))

proofs.name: PowersetDials.sumL_map_add
proofs.statement: sumL (l.map (fun a => f a + g a)) = sumL (l.map f) + sumL (l.map g)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.total_W
proofs.doc: **The count.** The dialled subsets of an n-element set add up to ∏(1 + tᵢ).
proofs.statement: sumL ((vecs ts.length).map (W ts)) = prodL (ts.map (fun t => 1 + t))

proofs.name: PowersetDials.total_W_chain
proofs.doc: The count is the mult-add chain plus one: ∏(1 + tᵢ) = 1 + (t₁ ✳ … ✳ tₙ).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.total_uniform
proofs.doc: All dials equal: (1 + t)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: prodL ((List.replicate n t).map (fun x => 1 + x)) = (1 + t) ^ n

proofs.name: PowersetDials.W_ones
proofs.doc: All dials 1: every subset weighs 1, and there are 2ⁿ of them.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.total_empty
proofs.doc: All dials 0: only the empty set survives, total 1.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.total_split
proofs.doc: Dials that are only 0 or 1 give 2^(number of ones): the classical split P(S) = P(A) × P(S∖A), the corners of the box of halves.
proofs.statement: prodL ((bs.map (fun b => if b then (1 : Nat) else 0)).map (fun t => 1 + t)) = 2 ^ (bs.filter (fun b => b)).length

proofs.name: PowersetDials.cell_merge
proofs.doc: **One element merged.** The four ways (in/out, in/out) that land on "out" weigh 1; the three that land on "in" weigh t + s + ts = t ✳ s. Read as coarse-graining: a block of two elements, present when either is, carries the dial t ✳ s.
proofs.statement: ((if (false || false) = z then cell t false * cell s false else 0) + (if (false || true) = z then cell t false * cell s true else 0)) + ((if (true || false) = z then cell t true * cell s false else 0) + (if (true || true) = z then cell t true * cell s true else 0)) = cell (t ✳ s) z

proofs.name: PowersetDials.summand_split
proofs.statement: (if orV (x :: a) (y :: b) = z :: c then W (t :: ts) (x :: a) * W (s :: ss) (y :: b) else 0) = (if (x || y) = z then cell t x * cell s y else 0) * (if orV a b = c then W ts a * W ss b else 0)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.inner_sum
proofs.statement: sumL ((vecs (n + 1)).map fun b => if orV (x :: a) b = z :: c then W (t :: ts) (x :: a) * W (s :: ss) b else 0) = (if (x || false) = z then cell t x * cell s false else 0) * sumL ((vecs n).map fun b => if orV a b = c then W ts a * W ss b else 0) + (if (x || true) = z then cell t x * cell s true else 0) * sumL ((vecs n).map fun b => if orV a b = c then W ts a * W ss b else 0)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.conv_W
proofs.doc: **Merging dialled power sets multiplies nothing new in: the dials mult-add.** Union-convolving the family with dials ts and the family with dials ss gives the family with dials tᵢ ✳ sᵢ.
proofs.statement: conv n ts ss c = W (List.zipWith multAdd ts ss) c

proofs.name: PowersetDials.zipWith_zero
proofs.doc: Dial 0 is the unit of merging: the family {∅}.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.zipWith_replicate
proofs.doc: Merging a constant family with itself mult-adds the dial with itself.
proofs.statement: List.zipWith multAdd (List.replicate n t) (List.replicate n t) = List.replicate n (t ✳ t)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.half_of_merge
proofs.doc: Merging commutes with halving: if r halves t and r' halves t', then r ✳ r' halves t ✳ t'. (On the line u = log(1 + t), merging is addition and halving is u ↦ u/2.)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.mth_root_of_full
proofs.doc: m copies merged: the m-fold mult-add power of the dial. An m-th root of the full power set is a dial with t^(✳m) = 1, that is (1 + t)^m = 2.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PowersetDials.half_dial
proofs.doc: **The half dial.** If r·r = 2, then h = r − 1 (that is √2 − 1) has h ✳ h = 1.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.W_replicate_one
proofs.doc: W with every dial 1 weighs every subset 1.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.half_squared_family
proofs.doc: **The half power set, squared, is the power set.** With every dial √2 − 1, the family merged with itself weighs every subset exactly 1: it is P(S).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.partner_spec
proofs.doc: Partners mult-add to 1: (1 + t)(1 + partner t) = 2.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.partner_partner
proofs.doc: Partnering is an involution.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.partner_zero
proofs.doc: The corners swap: dial 0 (leave the element out) pairs with dial 1 (all of it).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.partner_fixed_iff
proofs.doc: The fixed points of partnering are exactly the half dials.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.half_prob_union
proofs.doc: In probabilities (p = t/(1 + t)), the union half is p = 1 − r/2 = 1 − 1/√2: two independent copies, joined, give a fair coin, 1/2.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.cell_compl
proofs.doc: Complement of one element: in becomes out. Weight t on "in" read from the other side is t times weight 1/t on "out".
proofs.statement: cell t (!b) = t * cell t⁻¹ b

proofs.name: PowersetDials.W_compl
proofs.doc: **Complement inverts every dial.** The family with dials t, read through A ↦ S ∖ A, is (∏ t) times the family with dials 1/t.
proofs.statement: W ts (c.map (fun b => !b)) = prodL ts * W (ts.map (fun t => t⁻¹)) c

proofs.name: PowersetDials.compl_swaps_merge
proofs.doc: Complement swaps the two mergers: reciprocal dials mult-add under intersection exactly as dials mult-add under union. (1 + 1/t)(1 + 1/s) is the lift of t·s/(1 + t + s), the intersection's dial.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.halves_reciprocal
proofs.doc: The intersection half is the reciprocal of the union half: √2 + 1 = 1/(√2 − 1).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.halves_mirror
proofs.doc: In probabilities the two halves are 1 − r/2 and r/2: mirror images about 1/2.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.half_prob_inter
proofs.doc: The intersection half: two independent copies, intersected, give 1/2.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.no_half_both_ways
proofs.doc: **No single probability is a half both ways.** Joining two copies gives 1/2 and intersecting two copies gives 1/2 cannot both hold.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.compl_fixed_dial
proofs.doc: **The only dial complement leaves alone is 1** (the full power set).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.no_iterate_half
proofs.doc: **No dial construction is a half step of the power set by iteration.** The empty set has exactly one subset (itself), weight 1, so any size rule f coming from dials has f 0 = 1. Then f (f n) = 2ⁿ fails at once: f 1 = f (f 0) = 1, so f (f 1) = 1, not 2. No monotonicity is assumed.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.no_iterate_half_rat
proofs.doc: The same over the rationals (real-valued masses): f 0 = 1 forces f 1 = 1.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.euler_squarefree
proofs.doc: **Primes → squarefree numbers.** One prime's dial x = p^(−s) contributes the factor 1 + x; times 1 − x it is 1 − x², the same factor at 2s. Over all primes this is ∏(1 + p^(−s)) = ζ(s)/ζ(2s).

proofs.name: PowersetDials.fermi_dirac
proofs.doc: **Naturals as merged squarefree layers (Fermi–Dirac).** The exponent of a prime written in binary: (1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)⋯(1 + x^(2^(k−1))) times (1 − x) is 1 − x^(2^k). So ζ(s) is the merge of the squarefree power sets at dials p^(−s), p^(−2s), p^(−4s), …
proofs.statement: (1 - x) * prodL ((List.range k).map (fun j => 1 + x ^ (2 ^ j))) = 1 - x ^ (2 ^ k)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.rational_factor
proofs.doc: **Rationals: the exponent of a prime runs over all of ℤ.** Weighing exponent e by x^|e|, the first 2m + 1 exponents sum to 1 + 2(x + ⋯ + x^m), and times (1 − x) that is 1 + x − 2x^(m+1). The full factor is (1 + x)/(1 − x): the squarefree factor merged with the naturals' factor, so ∏ = ζ(s)²/ζ(2s).
proofs.statement: (1 - x) * (1 + 2 * sumL ((List.range m).map (fun k => x ^ (k + 1)))) = 1 + x - 2 * x ^ (m + 1)

proofs.name: PowersetDials.integers_square
proofs.doc: **Integers: ℕ is an exact half of ℤ∖{0}.** Pair n with −n, both carrying the same dial: the total is the square of the naturals' total, so the naturals (a corner half) and the centre half have exactly the same total.
proofs.statement: prodL (ts.map (fun t => (1 + t) * (1 + t))) = prodL (ts.map (fun t => 1 + t)) * prodL (ts.map (fun t => 1 + t))

proofs.name: PowersetDials.tiny_half
proofs.doc: **Tiny dials linearise.** Halving a small dial x by plain participation (x/2) misses the union half only at second order: (x/2) ✳ (x/2) = x + x²/4. Where the dials that matter are tiny (large primes, Poisson points on the line), the naive half and the merging half agree.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.participation_fixed
proofs.doc: Participation complement c ↦ 1 − c fixes exactly c = 1/2.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.halves_merge_to_whole
proofs.doc: Exponents of merged pieces add, and complement of participation sends α to 1 − α; the two halves α = 1/2 and 1 − α merge to the whole.

proofs.name: PowersetDials.squarefree_from_subsets
proofs.doc: The 32 subsets of the first five primes give 32 different squarefree numbers.

proofs.name: PvsNP.sAdd_lift
proofs.doc: The shift carries ⊕ to +.

proofs.name: PvsNP.multAdd_sAdd_distrib
proofs.doc: On the shifted ruler, ⊞ distributes over ⊕ (the semiring law, moved by x ↦ 1 + x).
proofs.statement: multAdd a (sAdd b c) = sAdd (multAdd a b) (multAdd a c)

proofs.name: PvsNP.evalS_lift
proofs.doc: Transport: a ⊕/⊞ circuit is a +/× circuit of the same wiring, seen through x ↦ 1 + x.
proofs.statement: 1 + evalS env C = eval (fun i => 1 + env i) (mapC (fun c => 1 + c) C)

proofs.name: PvsNP.eval_from_shift
proofs.doc: And back: every +/× circuit is a ⊕/⊞ circuit of the same wiring and size.
proofs.statement: eval env C = 1 + evalS (fun i => env i - 1) (mapC (fun c => c - 1) C)

proofs.name: PvsNP.shifted_identities
proofs.doc: The identities of the shifted semiring: −1 for ⊕ and 0 for ⊞; −1 absorbs under ⊞.
proofs.statement: sAdd a (-1) = a ∧ multAdd a 0 = a ∧ multAdd a (-1) = -1

proofs.name: PvsNP.witness_fold
proofs.doc: The dial folded over witnesses is the q-integer of the witness count, q = k + 1.

proofs.name: PvsNP.modp_period
proofs.doc: The ModₚP family: if qᵖ = 1, the count only matters mod p (through the lift).
proofs.statement: (q - 1) * QDial.qnum q (m + p) = (q - 1) * QDial.qnum q m

proofs.name: PvsNP.np_point_forgets
proofs.doc: q = 0 forgets: one witness and five witnesses give the same answer.

proofs.name: PvsNP.qnum_two_strictMono
proofs.doc: q = 2 keeps the whole count: different counts give different answers.
proofs.statement: QDial.qnum (2 : Int) m < QDial.qnum (2 : Int) n

proofs.name: PvsNP.gf2_multAdd_is_or
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PvsNP.gf2_shift_is_not
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PvsNP.gf2_lift_de_morgan
proofs.doc: The lift 1 + (a ⊞ b) = (1 + a)(1 + b) over GF(2) is De Morgan: ¬(a ∨ b) = ¬a ∧ ¬b.
proofs.statement: xor true (gf2MultAdd a b) = (xor true a && xor true b)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: PvsNP.foldMA_ones
proofs.doc: n gates, 2ⁿ − 1 monomials: 1 + (1 ⊞ 1 ⊞ … ⊞ 1) = 2ⁿ.

proofs.name: PvsNP.minplus_distrib
proofs.statement: a + min b c = min (a + b) (a + c)

proofs.name: PvsNP.minplus_assoc
proofs.statement: min (min a b) c = min a (min b c)

proofs.name: QKnots.kink_bracket
proofs.doc: ⟨kink⟩ = −A³ (stored times A³ as −A⁶).

proofs.name: QKnots.unknot_f
proofs.doc: The writhe correction removes the kink: the unknot's invariant is 1.

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoilL_bracket
proofs.doc: ⟨left trefoil⟩ = A⁷ − A³ − A⁻⁵ (stored times A⁹).

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoilL_f
proofs.doc: Left trefoil: f = A⁴ + A¹² − A¹⁶, so V(t) = t⁻¹ + t⁻³ − t⁻⁴.

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoilR_f
proofs.doc: Right trefoil: f = −A⁻¹⁶ + A⁻¹² + A⁻⁴, so V(t) = t + t³ − t⁴.

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoil_mirror
proofs.doc: The two trefoils are mirror images of each other ...

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoil_chiral
proofs.doc: ... and the invariant tells them apart: the trefoil is chiral.

proofs.name: QKnots.figEight_f
proofs.doc: Figure-eight: f = A⁻⁸ − A⁻⁴ + 1 − A⁴ + A⁸, so V(t) = t² − t + 1 − t⁻¹ + t⁻².

proofs.name: QKnots.figEight_amphichiral
proofs.doc: The figure-eight equals its own mirror image (it is amphichiral), unlike the trefoil.

proofs.name: QKnots.hopf_f
proofs.doc: Hopf link: f = −A⁻¹⁰ − A⁻², so V(t) = −t^(1/2) − t^(5/2).

proofs.name: QKnots.cinquefoilL_f
proofs.doc: Cinquefoil: V(t) = t⁻² + t⁻⁴ − t⁻⁵ + t⁻⁶ − t⁻⁷.

proofs.name: QKnots.jones_at_one
proofs.doc: At t = 1 (the counting point, k = 0) the Jones polynomial only counts components: 1 for every knot, −2 for the two-component Hopf link.
proofs.statement: evalOne (kauffmanF 3 6 trefoilL (-3)) = 1 ∧ evalOne (kauffmanF 3 6 trefoilR 3) = 1 ∧ evalOne (kauffmanF 4 8 figEight 0) = 1 ∧ evalOne (kauffmanF 5 10 cinquefoilL (-5)) = 1 ∧ evalOne (kauffmanF 2 4 hopf 2) = -2

proofs.name: QKnots.jones_at_neg_one
proofs.doc: At t = −1 (the parity point, k = −2) the Jones polynomial gives ± the knot's determinant: 3 for the trefoil (its three 3-colorings beyond the trivial), 5 for the figure-eight and for the cinquefoil.
proofs.statement: evalTneg (kauffmanF 3 6 trefoilL (-3)) = -3 ∧ evalTneg (kauffmanF 3 6 trefoilR 3) = -3 ∧ evalTneg (kauffmanF 4 8 figEight 0) = 5 ∧ evalTneg (kauffmanF 5 10 cinquefoilL (-5)) = 5

proofs.name: QKnots.trefoilL_cube
proofs.doc: The trefoil's eight states as (number of B-smoothings, loops). The B-count runs over the layers of the 3-cube (1, 3, 3, 1).

proofs.name: QKnots.state_layers
proofs.doc: The states with k B-smoothings are counted by the cube's layers (Pascal), up to 5 crossings.
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Fin 6, ∀ k : Fin 6, ((allStates n.val).filter (fun s => numB s == k.val)).length = MultAdd.Cube.layer n.val k.val

proofs.name: QKnots.loop_value_q
proofs.doc: The loop value is minus a q-integer: d = −A⁻²·[2] with [2] = 1 + A⁴ = QDial.qnum (A⁴) 2.
proofs.statement: -(A * A) - Ai * Ai = -(Ai * Ai) * QDial.qnum (A * A * A * A) 2

proofs.name: QKnots.reidemeister_one
proofs.doc: Reidemeister I: a kink multiplies the bracket by A·d + A⁻¹ = −A³.
proofs.statement: A * (-(A * A) - Ai * Ai) + Ai = -(A * A * A)

proofs.name: QKnots.reidemeister_two
proofs.doc: Reidemeister II: in the bracket of two crossings, the cup-cap term has coefficient A² + A·A⁻¹·d + A⁻² = 0, and the parallel term has coefficient A·A⁻¹ = 1.
proofs.statement: A * A + A * Ai * (-(A * A) - Ai * Ai) + Ai * Ai = 0

proofs.name: QKnots.writhe_cancels
proofs.doc: The writhe factor undoes the kink: (−A³)·(−A⁻³) = 1.

proofs.name: QPartitions.pentagonal_30
proofs.doc: Euler's pentagonal theorem, checked mod q³⁰.

proofs.name: QPartitions.euler_is_multAdd_30
proofs.doc: 1 + (−q ⊞ −q² ⊞ …) is Euler's product (the list lift foldMA_lift, seen on series).

proofs.name: QPartitions.euler_inverse_30
proofs.doc: Euler's product times the partition series is 1 (mod q³⁰): the two are inverse.

proofs.name: QPartitions.ramanujan_5
proofs.doc: Ramanujan: p(5n+4) ≡ 0 mod 5, for p(4), p(9), …, p(49).

proofs.name: QPartitions.ramanujan_7
proofs.doc: Ramanujan: p(7n+5) ≡ 0 mod 7, for p(5), p(12), …, p(47).

proofs.name: QPartitions.no_ramanujan_13
proofs.doc: The congruences are special to 5, 7, 11: for the prime 13 the same pattern p(13n+r) ≡ 0 already fails for every residue r by n ≤ 2 (13n + r ≤ 38).
proofs.statement: ∀ r : Fin 13, ∃ n : Fin 3, partList.getD (13 * n.val + r.val) 0 % 13 ≠ 0

proofs.name: QPartitions.triple_product_30
proofs.doc: The product side equals θ, mod q³⁰. (θ is the function the Tate gluing makes periodic.)

proofs.name: QPartitions.jacobi_four_squares_30
proofs.doc: θ⁴ counts the ways to write n as a sum of four squares (signs and order counted); Jacobi's theorem says that count is 8 × (sum of divisors not divisible by 4). Checked mod q³⁰.

proofs.name: QPartitions.four_squares_primes
proofs.doc: So for a prime p, r₄(p) = 8(p + 1): the prime's only divisors are 1 and p.

proofs.name: QPartitions.lagrange_below_30
proofs.doc: Every n < 30 is a sum of four squares (Lagrange's theorem, checked in this range).

proofs.name: QCounting.peval_padd
proofs.statement: ∀ p q : Poly, peval x (padd p q) = peval x p + peval x q

proofs.name: QCounting.peval_pzeros
proofs.statement: ∀ (k : Nat) (p : Poly), peval x (pzeros k p) = pw x k * peval x p

proofs.name: QCounting.gauss_at_one
proofs.doc: At q = 1 the Gaussian binomial is the binomial coefficient: the layer of the mult-add cube. (Every n and k, not a finite check.)
proofs.statement: ∀ n k : Nat, peval 1 (gauss n k) = (MultAdd.Cube.layer n k : Int)

proofs.name: QCounting.gauss_4_2
proofs.doc: The four points of the dial on [4, 2]_q = 1 + q + 2q² + q³ + q⁴: q = 1 counts 6 = C(4,2); q = 2 counts the 35 planes in a 4-dimensional space over the two-element field; q = 0 gives 1; q = −1 gives 2 = C(2,1) (Pascal folded in half).

proofs.name: QCounting.gauss_at_neg_one
proofs.doc: At q = −1, [n, k] is C(⌊n/2⌋, ⌊k/2⌋), or 0 when n is even and k odd. Checked n ≤ 8.
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Fin 9, ∀ k : Fin 9, k.val ≤ n.val → peval (-1) (gauss n.val k.val) = (if n.val % 2 == 0 && k.val % 2 == 1 then 0 else (MultAdd.Cube.layer (n.val / 2) (k.val / 2) : Int))

proofs.name: QCounting.q_binomial_theorem
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Fin 7, (qbinLHS n.val).map trim = (qbinRHS n.val).map trim

proofs.name: QCounting.uq_sl2_commutator
proofs.doc: On the irreducible representation of dimension n + 1, with basis v₀ … vₙ, E and F move between neighbours with factors [k]_q and [n − k]_q (symmetric q-integers [m] = (qᵐ − q⁻ᵐ)/(q − q⁻¹)), and K acts by q^(n − 2k). The relation [E, F] = (K − K⁻¹)/(q − q⁻¹) on v_k is [k+1][n−k] − [k][n−k+1] = [n − 2k]. Clearing the denominators (q − q⁻¹)² and writing x = qᵏ, y = q^(n−k) (xi, yi, qi their inverses), it is this ring identity, so the relation holds on every irreducible representation.
proofs.statement: (q * x - qi * xi) * (y - yi) - (x - xi) * (q * y - qi * yi) = (q - qi) * (xi * y - x * yi)

proofs.name: QCounting.uq_sl2_weight
proofs.doc: K E K⁻¹ = q² E: E moves v_k to v_{k−1}, whose weight q^(n−2k+2) is q² times v_k's.

proofs.name: QCounting.sl2_classical
proofs.doc: The classical limit q → 1: [E, F] = H, i.e. (a + 1)·b − a·(b + 1) = b − a.

proofs.name: QCounting.quantum_dim_is_loop
proofs.doc: The quantum dimension of the 2-dimensional representation is [2] = q + q⁻¹; with q = A² it is minus the knot loop value d = −A² − A⁻².
proofs.statement: A * A + Ai * Ai = -(-(A * A) - Ai * Ai)

proofs.name: QCounting.ising_eigen
proofs.doc: The two eigen-directions: a + b = (1 + u)ⁿ and a − b = (1 − u)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: (ising u n).1 + (ising u n).2 = pw (1 + u) n ∧ (ising u n).1 - (ising u n).2 = pw (1 - u) n

proofs.name: QCounting.ising_trace
proofs.doc: The partition function of n spins on a ring (up to the factor e^(nβJ)) is the trace: Z = (1 + u)ⁿ + (1 − u)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: 2 * (ising u n).1 = pw (1 + u) n + pw (1 - u) n

proofs.name: QCounting.ising_multAdd
proofs.doc: ... and in mult-add terms: Z = 2 + u^(⊞n) + (−u)^(⊞n). Only the even layers of the cube survive (a ring has an even number of domain walls).
proofs.statement: 2 * (ising u n).1 = 2 + mpow u n + mpow (-u) n

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_succ
proofs.statement: qnum q (n + 1) = 1 + q * qnum q n
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_eq_wpow
proofs.doc: The q-integer is the weighted mult-add power of 1 with weight k = q − 1.

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_lift
proofs.doc: The lift: 1 + (q − 1)·[n]_q = qⁿ. (So q-counting is mult-add counting through x ↦ 1 + x.)

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_add
proofs.doc: q-integers add by the weighted mult-add, weight q − 1: [m+n] = [m] ⊞ₖ [n].
proofs.statement: qnum q (m + n) = wAdd (q - 1) (qnum q m) (qnum q n)

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_add_std
proofs.doc: The standard form of the same rule: [m+n] = [m] + qᵐ·[n].
proofs.statement: qnum q (m + n) = qnum q m + q ^ m * qnum q n

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_mpow
proofs.doc: (q − 1)·[n]_q is the mult-add power (q − 1)^(⊞n).

proofs.name: QDial.tate_glue_step
proofs.doc: One Tate step: multiplying the lift 1 + a by q is a mult-add step by q − 1.

proofs.name: QDial.tate_glue_n
proofs.doc: n Tate steps: (1 + a)·qⁿ = 1 + (a ⊞ (q − 1)·[n]_q). Going n times round the torus's q-direction is one mult-add step whose length is (q − 1) times the q-integer [n]_q.
proofs.statement: (1 + a) * q ^ n = 1 + multAdd a ((q - 1) * qnum q n)

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_at_one
proofs.doc: q = 1, k = 0: the q-integer is plain counting.

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_at_two
proofs.doc: q = 2, k = 1: [n]₂ = 2ⁿ − 1, the mult-add power of 1 (and the number of nonzero vectors in an n-dimensional space over the two-element field).

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_at_zero
proofs.doc: q = 0, k = −1: every nonempty count collapses to 1 (the failure union 1 ⊞₋₁ 1 = 1).

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_at_neg_one
proofs.doc: q = −1, k = −2: parity.

proofs.name: QDial.parity_xor
proofs.doc: The parity law is ⊞ at k = −2: on {0, 1} it is "exclusive or". Same truth table as StatFused.xor_table, which is over Rat; this one is over Int.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-2 : Int) 0 0 = 0 ∧ wAdd (-2 : Int) 0 1 = 1 ∧ wAdd (-2 : Int) 1 0 = 1 ∧ wAdd (-2 : Int) 1 1 = 0

proofs.name: QDial.failure_or
proofs.doc: The failure union at k = −1 on {0, 1} is "or". Same truth table as StatFused.or_table, which is over Rat; this one is over Int.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1 : Int) 0 0 = 0 ∧ wAdd (-1 : Int) 0 1 = 1 ∧ wAdd (-1 : Int) 1 0 = 1 ∧ wAdd (-1 : Int) 1 1 = 1

proofs.name: QDial.qnum_three_at_dial
proofs.doc: Small values: [3]_q at the four dial points (counting 3, volume 7, union 1, parity 1).
proofs.statement: qnum (1 : Int) 3 = 3 ∧ qnum (2 : Int) 3 = 7 ∧ qnum (0 : Int) 3 = 1 ∧ qnum (-1 : Int) 3 = 1

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.call_rule_gap
proofs.doc: The rule from the call, p + q − pq, is the k = −1 rule. It is right for amplitude damping. For bit-flips it is off by exactly p·q.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) p q - wAdd (-2) p q = p * q

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.stacked_bit_flips
proofs.doc: n stacked bit-flips: the chance of an odd number of flips P satisfies 1 − 2P = (1 − 2p)ⁿ.

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.faces
proofs.doc: The four faces of the tetrahedron are the four chances (times 4). So "inside the tetrahedron" is exactly "all chances are nonnegative".
proofs.statement: 1 + p.lx + p.ly + p.lz = 4 * p.i ∧ 1 + p.lx - p.ly - p.lz = 4 * p.x ∧ 1 - p.lx + p.ly - p.lz = 4 * p.y ∧ 1 - p.lx - p.ly + p.lz = 4 * p.z

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.odd3_polar
proofs.doc: Phase-flips go straight through the bit-flip code: an odd number of them is a logical phase-flip, so the polarization is cubed.

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.f_fixed
proofs.doc: The vote only has fixed points at −1, 0 and 1 (the clean corner, the wall, the mirror).

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.f_helps
proofs.doc: Between the wall and the clean corner the vote always helps.

proofs.name: QuantumNoise.undetected_two_ways
proofs.doc: The chance a 3-repetition code misses an error (all three flip), computed two ways: on the code's own cube, and from the dual code's layers in the polarization 1 − 2p.

proofs.name: Relativity.dop_lift
proofs.doc: Its lift is the Doppler factor squared (Bondi's k²).

proofs.name: Relativity.dop_vel
proofs.doc: **Velocity addition is mult-add in disguise**: d(u ⊕ v) = d(u) ⊞ d(v).
proofs.statement: dop (vel u v) = multAdd (dop u) (dop v)

proofs.name: Relativity.dop_back
proofs.doc: The way back: u = d/(2 + d).

proofs.name: Relativity.velC_units
proofs.statement: velC c u v / c = vel (u / c) (v / c)

proofs.name: Relativity.dop_wall
proofs.doc: d carries the light wall −1 onto mult-add's wall −1.

proofs.name: Relativity.gap_to_light
proofs.doc: How far below light: 1 − u ⊕ v = (1 − u)(1 − v)/(1 + uv).

proofs.name: Relativity.under_light
proofs.doc: Two speeds under light, both forward, add to a speed under light.

proofs.name: kicks_plus
proofs.doc: The lift of n kicks splits: D + N = (1 + u)ⁿ and D − N = (1 − u)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: kD n u + kN n u = (1 + u) ^ n

proofs.name: kicks_minus
proofs.statement: kD n u - kN n u = (1 - u) ^ n

proofs.name: kick_step
proofs.doc: One more kick in the numerator/denominator form is velocity addition.
proofs.statement: vel (kN n u / kD n u) u = kN (n + 1) u / kD (n + 1) u

proofs.name: kicks_lift
proofs.doc: **n kicks lift to the mult-add power**: (D + N)/(D − N) = ((1 + u)/(1 − u))ⁿ.
proofs.statement: (kD n u + kN n u) * (1 - u) ^ n = (kD n u - kN n u) * (1 + u) ^ n

proofs.name: boost_mul
proofs.doc: Boosts multiply as speeds velocity-add: B(u)B(v) = (1 + uv)·B(u ⊕ v).
proofs.statement: B2.mul (boost u) (boost v) = ⟨1 + u * v, u + v, u + v, 1 + u * v⟩
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: boost_mul_vel
proofs.statement: (1 + u * v) * vel u v = u + v
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: squeeze_plus
proofs.doc: On the light-cone axes P = T + X, M = T − X a boost is a squeeze.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: squeeze_minus
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: squeeze_ratio
proofs.doc: The squeeze ratio is the lift 1 + d.

proofs.name: hyperbola
proofs.doc: The hyperbola: T'² − X'² = (1 − u²)(T² − X²), and T² − X² = P·M.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: hyperbola_cone
proofs.statement: T * T - X * X = (T + X) * (T - X)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: cone_fixed
proofs.doc: The light cone is fixed: a ray with T = X (or T = −X) stays one.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: cone_fixed'
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: landscape_point
proofs.doc: The landscape law (a + b + k·ab)/(1 − q·ab) at k = 0, q = −1/c² is velocity addition.

proofs.name: landscape_walls
proofs.doc: Its walls 1 + k·a + q·a² = (1 − a/c)(1 + a/c): the light cone.

proofs.name: corner_tax
proofs.doc: The corner tax: w = u ⊕ v satisfies w = u + v − u·v·w.
proofs.statement: vel u v = u + v - u * v * vel u v
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: rung_natural_k
proofs.doc: Rung s's third-layer dot is (s, s(s − 1)/4). In units λ the dot moves to (λk, λ²q). With s = t² and λ = 2/t it lands at (2t, t² − 1).

proofs.name: rung_parabola
proofs.doc: That curve is the border parabola moved down by 1: q = k²/4 − 1.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: rung_walls
proofs.doc: Its walls factor: 1 + 2t·a + (t² − 1)a² = (1 + (1 + t)a)(1 − (1 − t)a).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: rung_zero_is_velocity
proofs.doc: t = 0: walls ±1, velocity addition.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: rung_one_is_multadd
proofs.doc: t = 1: one wall at −1/2, the other at infinity: mult-add at weight 2.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: rung_raw_walls
proofs.doc: In raw units rung s = t² has walls −2/(t(1 + t)) and 2/(t(1 − t)): a speed limit near 2/√s as s → 0, light speed growing to infinity at plain addition.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.path_obeys
proofs.doc: a path of three pairs obeys the rule for all weights

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.star_obeys
proofs.doc: a star obeys the rule for all weights

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.triangle_obeys
proofs.doc: a triangle with a lone fourth wave obeys the rule

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.paw_obeys
proofs.doc: a triangle with a pendant wave obeys the rule for all weights

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.cycle_rule
proofs.doc: the 4-cycle 0–1–2–3–0 with diagonals 1: the rule is the product of (w − 1)² over its pairs

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.diamond_rule
proofs.doc: the 4-cycle with one diagonal, one weight k

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.cycle_two_breaks
proofs.doc: the cycle breaks the rule when its weights avoid 1: an example with weight 2

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.uniform_rule
proofs.doc: every pair of four waves at weight k

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.uniform_three_breaks
proofs.doc: so k = 3 (or any k other than 0, 1, −2) is not carried by four point-waves

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.uniform_minus_two_obeys
proofs.doc: … and k = −2 is

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.third_wave
proofs.doc: with waves (0, ∞) and (1, 1/k), a third wave (t, t/k) has weight k to both exactly when t is a root of t² − (k + 1)t + 1 (numerator of the cross ratio minus k)

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.fourth_wave_forces
proofs.doc: four waves need the pair of roots to be the cube roots of unity (t² + t + 1 = 0); against the quadratic that leaves (k + 2)·t = 0, so k = −2

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.omega_cube_root
proofs.doc: ω² really is −1 − ω in this arithmetic: ω·ω + ω + 1 = 0

proofs.name: RuleBreakers.tetrahedral_waves
proofs.doc: the waves (1, −1/2), (ω, −ω/2), (ω², −ω²/2): every pair has weight −2 (denominators nonzero), and each has weight a/b = −2 to the wave (0, ∞)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.thermostat_residue
proofs.doc: The thermostat: undoing +d by -d leaves the corner square -d².

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.panel_grid
proofs.doc: A panel of two: area = own corners + cross corners.
proofs.statement: (e₁ + e₂) * (i₁ + i₂) = (e₁ * i₁ + e₂ * i₂) + (e₁ * i₂ + e₂ * i₁)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.balance
proofs.doc: Balance: moving d away from the even split loses exactly d².
proofs.statement: (s + d) * (s - d) = s * s - d * d

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.fused_price_step
proofs.doc: Fused voice price: total voice V costs V² - 1, so the next unit of voice costs 2V + 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.fused_price_expand
proofs.doc: Plain and fused prices for k extra votes differ by the 2k strips.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.boundary
proofs.statement: foldMA (S ++ T) = foldMA S + foldMA T + foldMA S * foldMA T

proofs.name: MultAdd.Rulecraft.recovery
proofs.doc: Losing n parts of n+1 needs a gain of n: 90% lost (n = 9) needs +900%.

proofs.name: RungShape.twist_rung1
proofs.doc: Mixed second difference of mult-add = h·k, the area of the corner rectangle. (Rung 0 has twist 0: a flat plane. Rung 1 has twist 1: the saddle.)
proofs.statement: multAdd (a + h) (b + k) - multAdd (a + h) b - multAdd a (b + k) + multAdd a b = h * k

proofs.name: RungShape.twist_dial
proofs.doc: The corner dial a + b + t·ab has twist t (the corner weight).
proofs.statement: wAdd t (a + h) (b + k) - wAdd t (a + h) b - wAdd t a (b + k) + wAdd t a b = t * (h * k)

proofs.name: RungShape.ruled_rung1
proofs.doc: Rung 1's graph is ruled: along any fixed a it is a straight line in b.
proofs.statement: multAdd a b = a + (1 + a) * b

proofs.name: RungShape.ruled_rung1'
proofs.doc: ... and along any fixed b it is a straight line in a (doubly ruled saddle).
proofs.statement: multAdd a b = b + (1 + b) * a

proofs.name: RungShape.axis_rung1
proofs.doc: Flat along the axes: rung 1 adds nothing on the a-axis (the identity line).

proofs.name: RungShape.flow_zero
proofs.doc: Whole rung height 0 is the identity of the near-identity flow.

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_rung0
proofs.doc: Rung 0 slice: a + b = c is the straight line b = c − a.

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_rung1
proofs.doc: Rung 1 slice: a ⊞ b = c is the hyperbola b = (c − a)/(1 + a).

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_dial
proofs.doc: Corner-dial slice: a ⊞ₜ b = c is b = (c − a)/(1 + t·a).
proofs.statement: wAdd t a ((c - a) / (1 + t * a)) = c

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_edges
proofs.doc: Every slice passes through (c, 0) and (0, c): the sheet's two fixed edges.
proofs.statement: multAdd c 0 = c ∧ multAdd 0 c = c

proofs.name: RungShape.flow_closed
proofs.doc: The near-identity flow in closed form: φ_t(x) = 2x/(2 − t x) satisfies its defining relation.

proofs.name: RungShape.addPow_eq
proofs.doc: Rung 0, count d: the line d·a.

proofs.name: RungShape.cube_count
proofs.doc: Rung 1, count d, edge 1: the d-cube's corners, 2^d (so the mult-add power is 2^d − 1).
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_iff_line
proofs.doc: A point is on the sheet (rung value c) exactly when its lens image is on the straight line u + v = ψ c.
proofs.statement: lensOp φ ψ a b = c ↔ ψ a + ψ b = ψ c
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape
it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_diagonal
proofs.doc: The diagonal point of the sheet: a ⊕ a = c exactly when ψ a + ψ a = ψ c (so a is the flow carrying half of ψ c back out).
proofs.statement: lensOp φ ψ a a = c ↔ ψ a + ψ a = ψ c
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape
it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: RungShape.sheet_rung1_lens
proofs.doc: Rung 1 with no logarithms: its lens is x ↦ 1 + x into multiplication, and the slice a ⊞ b = c is the "straight line" (1 + a)(1 + b) = 1 + c of that lens.
proofs.statement: multAdd a b = c ↔ (1 + a) * (1 + b) = 1 + c

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.tau4_free
proofs.doc: every pair weight 1: four separate mult-adds

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.tau4_splits
proofs.doc: a fourth wave with weight 1 to the others splits off as its own mult-add factor

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.tau4_exclusion
proofs.doc: weight 0 between waves 1 and 2: no term has both of them on

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.kp_dispersion
proofs.doc: every pair of points p, q gives a wave: (p − q, p² − q², p³ − q³) solves the dispersion
proofs.statement: kpP (p - q) (p * p - q * q) (p * p * p - q * q * q) = 0

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.kp_pair_weight
proofs.doc: Hirota's two-wave condition: P(k₁ + k₂)·A + P(k₁ − k₂) = 0, with A the cross ratio (written with denominators cleared)

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.kdv_cross_ratio
proofs.doc: the KdV case q = −p: the cross ratio becomes ((p₁ − p₂)/(p₁ + p₂))²

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.cross_ratio_minus_one
proofs.doc: numerator minus denominator of the cross ratio: A − 1 carries (a_i − b_i)(a_j − b_j)
proofs.statement: (ai - aj) * (bi - bj) - (ai - bj) * (bi - aj) = (ai - bi) * (aj - bj)

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.free_iff_trivial
proofs.doc: the pair weight is 1 exactly when one of the two waves is trivial
proofs.statement: (ai - aj) * (bi - bj) = (ai - bj) * (bi - aj) ↔ ai = bi ∨ aj = bj

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.resonance_iff
proofs.doc: the pair weight is 0 exactly when the waves share a point (resonance)
proofs.statement: (ai - aj) * (bi - bj) = 0 ↔ ai = aj ∨ bi = bj

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.cross_ratio_affine
proofs.doc: an affine change p ↦ λp + μ scales numerator and denominator by λ² alike
proofs.statement: ((l * ai + m) - (l * aj + m)) * ((l * bi + m) - (l * bj + m)) = l * l * ((ai - aj) * (bi - bj)) ∧ ((l * ai + m) - (l * bj + m)) * ((l * bi + m) - (l * aj + m)) = l * l * ((ai - bj) * (bi - aj))

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.cross_ratio_inversion
proofs.doc: p ↦ 1/p keeps the cross ratio (cross-multiplied, with p ↦ 1/p written as p ↦ P/p on the common denominator P = a_i b_i a_j b_j)
proofs.statement: ((aj - ai) * (bj - bi)) * ((ai - bj) * (bi - aj)) = ((ai - aj) * (bi - bj)) * ((bj - ai) * (aj - bi))

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.excess_points
proofs.doc: pair weights minus the numbers 2g points carry, doubled

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.excess_curves
proofs.doc: Riemann's period numbers minus curves, doubled: the same excess

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.excess_agree
proofs.doc: the two counts agree for every number of waves

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.excess_kdv
proofs.doc: the symmetric KdV waves: g − 1 numbers, excess (g − 1)(g − 2)/2

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.excess_from_four
proofs.doc: the excess is zero up to three waves and positive from four

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.kdv_excess_from_three
proofs.doc: for KdV it is positive already from three waves

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.config_one_rule
proofs.doc: … and they obey the rule

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.rule4_all_two
proofs.doc: the rule is a real constraint: an array of all 2s breaks it, so no four waves on a line have every pair weight 2

proofs.name: SeveralWaves.rule4_second_value
proofs.doc: five weights fix the sixth up to two values: with the first five of configuration one, both 5/2 (the actual weight) and 92/77 satisfy the rule

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.star_def
proofs.statement: a ✳ b = a + b + a * b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.weight_is_units
proofs.doc: Zooming the inputs by λ and the weight by 1/λ gives the same law: the weight is units.
proofs.statement: l * wAdd (l * k) a b = wAdd k (l * a) (l * b)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.qcount_is_weight
proofs.doc: The q of the q-integers (and of the Potts colours) is the weight plus one.
proofs.statement: wAdd (q - 1) a b = a + b + q * a * b - a * b

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.path3_sum
proofs.doc: The list of all eight occupation patterns adds up to the closed form.
proofs.statement: path3 k z = 1 + z + z + z + (z * z * k) + (z * z * k) + (z * z) + (z * z * z * k * k)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.graph_weight_survives
proofs.doc: On the graph the weight survives: if a rescaling of the sites (z ↦ λz) and of the whole sum (by m) turns the coefficients for weight k into those for weight k', then k = k'.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ruler_num
proofs.doc: Cross-multiplied numerator of F_{p,q}(N a, N b) with N(x) = x/(1+cx): it is the numerator of F_{p+2c, ·}(a, b).
proofs.statement: a * (1 + c * b) + b * (1 + c * a) + p * a * b = wAdd (p + 2 * c) a b

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ruler_den
proofs.doc: Cross-multiplied denominator: (1+ca)(1+cb) − q·ab is the denominator of N applied to F_{p+2c, q+pc+c²}(a, b). Together with ruler_num: N⁻¹(F_{p,q}(N a, N b)) = F_{p+2c, q+pc+c²}(a,b).
proofs.statement: (1 + c * a) * (1 + c * b) - q * a * b = (1 - (q + p * c + c * c) * a * b) + c * wAdd (p + 2 * c) a b

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ruler_keeps_disc
proofs.doc: The ruler keeps the discriminant: (p+2c)² − 4(q+pc+c²) = p² − 4q. The ruler's orbits are the parabolas q = (p² − D)/4, one for each D.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.zoom_disc
proofs.doc: Units zoom the discriminant: (λp)² − 4(λ²q) = λ²(p² − 4q). Only its sign is free of units.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ladder_forces_c3
proofs.doc: The ladder at fourth order forces c₃ of any rung with c₂ = s/2.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ladder_forces_c4
proofs.doc: The ladder at fifth order then forces c₄.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.ladder_jets_commute
proofs.doc: ...and the forced jets do satisfy the ladder (so the rung exists to this order).

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.rung_rate_inverts
proofs.doc: The rung-s law is plain addition in the ruler ℓ = E^{−s}, whose jets are the forced ones at −s: ℓ₂ = −s/2, ℓ₃ = s(3s+1)/12, ℓ₄ = −s(2s+1)(3s+1)/48. Its rate R = 1/ℓ′ has coefficients r₁ = s, r₂ = s(s−1)/4, r₃ = −s(s−1)/12: these satisfy ℓ′·R = 1 through a³.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.lens_jets_at_minus
proofs.doc: The jets of E^{−s} are the forced jets with s replaced by −s.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.rung_disc_is_height
proofs.doc: Through third order the rung's discriminant is its height: r₁² − 4r₂ = s. So rung s looks, to third order, like the law with one period 2πi/√s (rung 1: 2πi, mult-add; rung 0: no period; rung −1: real period 2π, a circle).

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.rung_leaves_plane
proofs.doc: Every point of the landscape plane has rate 1 + p a + q a² exactly, so r₃ = 0 there; the rung's r₃ = −s(s−1)/12 differs from 0 at s = 2, s = −1 and s = 1/2.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.rung_crossings
proofs.doc: The rung crosses the plane at rungs 0 and 1 (r₃ = 0 there), crossing, not touching: dr₃/ds = −(2s−1)/12 is +1/12 at s = 0 and −1/12 at s = 1.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.glue_commutes
proofs.doc: Gluing a ↦ a ✳ (q − 1) commutes with the law, for every q.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.glue_twice
proofs.doc: Two gluings are one gluing by the product: the gluings form the group q^ℤ (in mult-add form).

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.glue_descends
proofs.doc: The law descends to the quotient: glued inputs give a glued output, whatever the gluings. So the torus ℂ*/q^ℤ carries mult-add for every nome, and the nome is invisible near 0.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.cusp_psi3
proofs.doc: Cusp y² = x³ (addition): ψ₃ = 3x⁴, whose only root is the cusp itself: no point other than the start comes back in three steps.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.node_psi3
proofs.doc: Node y² + xy = x³ (mult-add): ψ₃ = x³(3x + 1). Besides the node (x = 0) the root x = −1/3.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.node_three_points
proofs.doc: At x = −1/3 the node's equation y² + xy − x³ = 0 reads y² − y/3 + 1/27 = 0, whose discriminant 1/9 − 4/27 = −1/27 is not 0: two points. With the start, three: mult-add's three cube roots of 1. (The Tate torus has nine: see checks.py, 5a.)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.pair_weight_survives
proofs.doc: No separate rescaling of the waves changes the pair weight: if τ_A(λ₁w₁, λ₂w₂) = τ_{A'}(w₁, w₂) for all w₁, w₂, then λ₁ = λ₂ = 1 and A = A'. (A single law's weight is units; a pair weight is not.)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.periods_outnumber_curves
proofs.doc: Period matrices for g waves have g(g+1)/2 entries; curves of genus g have 3g − 3 moduli. The first exceeds the second exactly from g = 4 on (checked for 2 ≤ g < 40): Schottky's problem.

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.pseries_two
proofs.statement: wpow k x 2 = 2 * x + k * x * x

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.pseries_three
proofs.statement: wpow k x 3 = 3 * x + 3 * k * x * x + k * k * x * x * x

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.pseries_five
proofs.statement: wpow k x 5 = 5 * x + 10 * k * x * x + 10 * k * k * x * x * x + 5 * k * k * k * x * x * x * x + k * k * k * k * x * x * x * x * x

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.additive_at_two
proofs.doc: p ∣ k: the p-fold power is p times a whole number (the law is additive at p).
proofs.statement: wpow (2 * m) x 2 = 2 * (x + m * x * x)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.additive_at_three
proofs.statement: wpow (3 * m) x 3 = 3 * (x + 3 * m * x * x + 3 * m * m * x * x * x)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.mult_at_three
proofs.doc: p ∤ k: the p-fold power is k^{p−1}x^p plus p times a whole number, and k^{p−1} is 1 more than a multiple of p (shown for p = 3; the law is multiplicative at p, height 1).
proofs.statement: wpow k x 3 - k * k * x * x * x = 3 * (x + k * x * x)

proofs.name: ShapeDirections.mult_at_two
proofs.statement: wpow k x 2 - k * x * x = 2 * x

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.weight_is_twist
proofs.doc: **A size weight is a twist.** Weighing two dials by w and mult-adding is the twisted mult-add at k = w, scaled by w.
proofs.statement: multAdd (w * t) (w * s) = w * wAdd w t s

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.weighted_merge_gap
proofs.doc: **Weighing does not commute with merging.** Union of the weighted dials vs the weighted union dial: the gap is t·s·w·(w − 1).
proofs.statement: multAdd (t * w) (s * w) = multAdd t s * w + t * s * w * (w - 1)

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.sharp_weight_commutes
proofs.doc: **Only a sharp count commutes.** If w·w = w (w is 0 or 1 in a domain), weighing and merging commute.
proofs.statement: multAdd (t * w) (s * w) = multAdd t s * w

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.weight_one
proofs.doc: Weight 1 is the plain count.

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.twisted_half
proofs.doc: **The half under a twist.** If (1 + k·h)² = 1 + k then k·(h ✳ₖ h) = k.
proofs.statement: k * wAdd k h h = k

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.stacked_dials
proofs.doc: Dial 1/2 under weight w is the dial w/2: the uniform dial and the weight multiply.

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.distinct_times_doubled
proofs.doc: Subsets times multisets-at-doubled-size: element by element, ∏(1 + x) · ∏(1 − x²)⁻¹… in the finite form ∏(1 + x) · ∏(1 − x) = ∏(1 − x²).
proofs.statement: prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + x)) * prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 - x)) = prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 - x * x))

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.S2_eq_S
proofs.statement: S2 f N = S f (2 * N)

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.alt_eq_sum_sub_evens
proofs.doc: **The finite η–ζ law.** Alternating sum = plain sum − 2 × even terms.
proofs.statement: A f N = S2 f N - 2 * E f N

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.evens_scale
proofs.doc: If doubling scales a weight by c, the even terms are c times the first half.
proofs.statement: E f N = c * S f N

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.alt_doubling
proofs.doc: **Doubling law (η = (1 − 2c)·ζ in finite form).** With c = 2^(−s): the "at most once" share is the whole minus twice c times the first half.
proofs.statement: A f N = S f (2 * N) - 2 * c * S f N

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.at_most_m
proofs.doc: **At most m copies.** (1 − x)(1 + x + … + x^m) = 1 − x^(m+1); m = 1 is mult-add's "at most once", m → ∞ is full repetition.

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.at_most_one
proofs.doc: m = 1 is the mult-add factor.

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.prod_plus_even_odd
proofs.statement: prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + x)) = ev l + od l

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.prod_minus_even_odd
proofs.statement: prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 - x)) = ev l - od l

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.even_half
proofs.doc: **Class group of order 2.** The principal part (even number of non-principal primes) is half of ∏(1 + x) + ∏(1 − x): the sign dial is the missing piece.
proofs.statement: prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 + x)) + prodL (l.map (fun x => 1 - x)) = 2 * ev l

proofs.name: SizeDialResidual.two_sign_dials_example
proofs.doc: Two non-principal primes make a principal product (the xy term), one alone does not.

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau2_is_wAdd
proofs.statement: tau2 A a b = 1 + wAdd A a b

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau2_free
proofs.doc: weight 1: no interaction, the tau function is the plain mult-add lift (1+a)(1+b)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau2_merge
proofs.doc: weight 0: equal speeds, the two exponentials just add (rung 0)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau2_scaled
proofs.doc: for two solitons the law is rung 1 in a rescaled coordinate: A·(τ − 1) = (A a) ⊞ (A b)
proofs.statement: A * (tau2 A a b - 1) = multAdd (A * a) (A * b)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau2_excess
proofs.doc: read in the 1+x picture, the weight is mult-add plus an excess (A − 1) per pair
proofs.statement: tau2 A a b = 1 + multAdd a b + (A - 1) * a * b

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau3_splits
proofs.doc: a soliton that interacts with nobody (weights 1) factors off
proofs.statement: tau3 A12 1 1 a b c = tau2 A12 a b * (1 + c)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tau3_equal_corner
proofs.doc: equal weights k: the triple corner is k³ (three pairs)
proofs.statement: tau3 k k k a b c = 1 + a + b + c + k * (a * b + a * c + b * c) + (k * k * k) * (a * b * c)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.wAdd_three_corner
proofs.doc: weighted mult-add of three has triple corner k², not k³: it is mult-add rescaled, while solitons weight every pair
proofs.statement: wAdd k (wAdd k a b) c = a + b + c + k * (a * b + a * c + b * c) + (k * k) * (a * b * c)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.soliton_vs_wAdd_corner
proofs.doc: the two agree exactly when k³ = k², i.e. k = 0 or k = 1 (rung 0 or rung 1)
proofs.statement: k * k * k = k * k ↔ k = 0 ∨ k = 1

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.three_body_roads
proofs.doc: three bodies: 2·(soliton corner − rung corner) = s(2s−1)(s−1): the roads meet at s = 0, ½, 1

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.rung_three_body
proofs.doc: the rung flow's three-body term: triple corner minus (pair)², times 2, is s(s−1)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.rung_three_body_zero
proofs.doc: on whole numbers the rung flow has no three-body term only at rungs 0 and 1

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.four_body_roads
proofs.doc: four bodies: 2·(soliton corner A⁶ − rung corner) factors as s(s−1)·(quartic)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.four_body_half
proofs.doc: the quartic is not zero at s = ½ (16 × its value there, written with S = 2s = 1, is −2): so the three-body meeting at s = ½ does not survive to four bodies

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.tri_zero_iff
proofs.doc: the lattice weight q^(n(n−1)/2) is free of q only for n = 0 and n = 1

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.face_iff
proofs.doc: two waves: the exponent n₁(n₁−1) + n₂(n₂−1) vanishes exactly on the unit square {0,1}², the corners of the mult-add cube

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.theta2_face
proofs.doc: at q₁ = q₂ = 0 the theta series is the weighted mult-add cube 1 + (w₁ ⊞_A w₂)
proofs.statement: theta2 0 0 A w1 w2 = 1 + wAdd A w1 w2

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.theta2_free_face
proofs.doc: with A = 1 the two-wave theta splits into two one-wave pieces (no interaction)

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.glue_is_multAdd
proofs.doc: multiplying by q in the w picture is mult-add by q − 1 in the 1+x picture

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.orbit_product
proofs.doc: a truncated theta product: (1+w)(1+wq)(1+vq), v standing for 1/w, is 1 + the mult-add of three points of w's q-orbit
proofs.statement: (1 + w) * (1 + w * q) * (1 + v * q) = 1 + multAdd w (multAdd (w * q) (v * q))

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.orbit_product_q0
proofs.doc: and at q = 0 only the soliton factor 1 + w is left

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.kdv_weight_below_one
proofs.doc: for positive wave numbers, (k₁ − k₂)² < (k₁ + k₂)²: the weight A is below 1

proofs.name: SolitonsRungs.kdv_weight_zero
proofs.doc: the weight is 0 exactly when the speeds match

proofs.name: StatFused.or_table
proofs.doc: Truth tables.

proofs.name: StatFused.sq_diff_is_xor
proofs.doc: The squared difference of two indicators is their XOR (k = −2).

proofs.name: StatFused.de_morgan
proofs.doc: De Morgan: "not (A or B)" = "not A and not B"; complement x ↦ 1 − x turns ⊞₋₁ into ×.

proofs.name: StatFused.de_morgan_and
proofs.doc: The complement conjugates OR into AND: 1 − ((1−x) ⊞₋₁ (1−y)) = x·y.

proofs.name: StatFused.xor_complement
proofs.doc: XOR is self-dual under complement of both inputs.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-2) (1 - x) (1 - y) = wAdd (-2) x y

proofs.name: StatFused.union_misses
proofs.doc: Nothing happens: 1 − union = product of the misses.

proofs.name: StatFused.union_neg_foldMA
proofs.doc: The k = −1 fold is mult-add read on the negatives.

proofs.name: StatFused.inclusion_exclusion
proofs.doc: **Inclusion–exclusion for n events**: 1 − P(union) is the sum over every corner g of the n-cube of the signed product Π_{i∈g}(−xᵢ).

proofs.name: StatFused.incl_excl_two
proofs.statement: unionL [p, q] = p + q - p * q

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_add
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => f a + g a) = Ex ws f + Ex ws g

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_sub
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => f a - g a) = Ex ws f - Ex ws g

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_smul
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => c * f a) = c * Ex ws f

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_const
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun _ => c) = c * Ex ws (fun _ => 1)

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_congr
proofs.statement: Ex ws f = Ex ws g
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: StatFused.Ex_sumL
proofs.doc: Linearity over a finite list of functions.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => sumL (gs.map (fun g => F g a))) = sumL (gs.map (fun g => Ex ws (F g)))

proofs.name: StatFused.union_general
proofs.doc: Union of two events, dependent or not: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => wAdd (-1) (A a) (B a)) = Ex ws A + Ex ws B - Ex ws (fun a => A a * B a)

proofs.name: StatFused.union_lift
proofs.doc: **Dependence is the weight.** If the overlap is `lift` times what independence predicts, P(A ∩ B) = lift·P(A)·P(B), then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) ⊞ₖ P(B) with k = −lift.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => wAdd (-1) (A a) (B a)) = wAdd (-lift) (Ex ws A) (Ex ws B)

proofs.name: StatFused.union_disjoint
proofs.doc: Disjoint events (lift 0): k = 0, plain addition, Kolmogorov's axiom.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => wAdd (-1) (A a) (B a)) = wAdd 0 (Ex ws A) (Ex ws B)

proofs.name: StatFused.xor_lift
proofs.doc: Exclusive or with dependence: k = −2·lift.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => wAdd (-2) (A a) (B a)) = wAdd (-2 * lift) (Ex ws A) (Ex ws B)

proofs.name: StatFused.cov_is_corner_excess
proofs.doc: Covariance of two indicators is the corner's excess over the independent corner.
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => A a * B a) - Ex ws A * Ex ws B = (lift - 1) * Ex ws A * Ex ws B

proofs.name: StatFused.prodL_neg_sgn
proofs.statement: prodL (g.map (fun x => -x)) = sgn g * prodL g

proofs.name: StatFused.union_corners
proofs.statement: 1 - unionL l = sumL ((groups l).map (fun g => sgn g * prodL g))

proofs.name: StatFused.inclusion_exclusion_general
proofs.doc: **Inclusion–exclusion, n events, any dependence.** With total weight 1, P(no event happens) = Σ over every corner g of the cube of (−1)^|g|·P(all of g).
proofs.statement: Ex ws (fun a => 1 - unionL (As.map (fun A => A a))) = sumL ((groups As).map (fun g => sgn g * Ex ws (allOf g)))

proofs.name: StatFused.gen_append
proofs.statement: gen (d ++ e) t = gen d t + gen e t

proofs.name: StatFused.gen_nshift
proofs.statement: gen (nshift x w e) t = w * pw t x * gen e t

proofs.name: StatFused.gen_conv
proofs.doc: Generating functions multiply under independent sums: the volume reading (1+a)(1+b).
proofs.statement: gen (nconv d e) t = gen d t * gen e t

proofs.name: StatFused.kmoment_law
proofs.doc: **The dial.** If a and b are the k-moments of X and Y, read through 1 + k·a = G(1 + k), then the k-moment of X + Y is a ⊞ₖ b.
