proofs.statement: 1 + k * wAdd k a b = gen (nconv d e) (1 + k)

proofs.name: StatFused.bern_kmoment
proofs.doc: A coin's k-moment is p at every k: one number, every weight.

proofs.name: StatFused.heads_kmoment
proofs.statement: gen (heads ps) (1 + k) = 1 + k * foldW k ps

proofs.name: StatFused.heads_none
proofs.doc: t = 0 (k = −1): G(0) = P(no heads) = Π(1 − pᵢ), the union rule's survival.

proofs.name: StatFused.heads_parity
proofs.doc: t = −1 (k = −2): G(−1) = P(even) − P(odd) = 1 − 2·(p₁ ⊞₋₂ p₂ ⊞₋₂ …): piling-up for unequal coins.

proofs.name: StatFused.pw_neg_one_parity
proofs.statement: pw (-1 : Rat) x = (if x % 2 = 0 then 1 else -1)

proofs.name: StatFused.gen_neg_one
proofs.statement: gen d (-1) = pEven d - pOdd d

proofs.name: StatFused.binom_kmoment
proofs.statement: gen (binom p n) (1 + k) = 1 + k * wpow k p n

proofs.name: StatFused.gen_is_lit_corners
proofs.statement: gen d (1 + k) = litCorners d k

proofs.name: StatFused.bp_zero_col
proofs.statement: bp p q n 0 = pw q n

proofs.name: StatFused.bp_above
proofs.statement: ∀ n j, n < j → bp p q n j = 0

proofs.name: StatFused.bp_layers
proofs.doc: **Binomial = Pascal layers**: P(j heads of n) = C(n, j)·pʲ·qⁿ⁻ʲ.
proofs.statement: ∀ n j, j ≤ n → bp p q n j = (Cube.layer n j : Rat) * pw p j * pw q (n - j)

proofs.name: StatFused.mass_append
proofs.statement: mass (d ++ e) = mass d + mass e

proofs.name: StatFused.m1_append
proofs.statement: m1 (d ++ e) = m1 d + m1 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m2_append
proofs.statement: m2 (d ++ e) = m2 d + m2 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m3_append
proofs.statement: m3 (d ++ e) = m3 d + m3 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m4_append
proofs.statement: m4 (d ++ e) = m4 d + m4 e

proofs.name: StatFused.mass_shift
proofs.statement: mass (shift x w e) = w * mass e

proofs.name: StatFused.m1_shift
proofs.statement: m1 (shift x w e) = w * (x * mass e + m1 e)

proofs.name: StatFused.m2_shift
proofs.statement: m2 (shift x w e) = w * (x * x * mass e + 2 * x * m1 e + m2 e)

proofs.name: StatFused.m3_shift
proofs.statement: m3 (shift x w e) = w * (x*x*x * mass e + 3 * (x*x) * m1 e + 3 * x * m2 e + m3 e)

proofs.name: StatFused.m4_shift
proofs.statement: m4 (shift x w e) = w * (x*x*x*x * mass e + 4 * (x*x*x) * m1 e + 6 * (x*x) * m2 e + 4 * x * m3 e + m4 e)

proofs.name: StatFused.mass_conv
proofs.doc: Total weight multiplies: the grid of outcomes.
proofs.statement: mass (conv d e) = mass d * mass e

proofs.name: StatFused.m1_conv
proofs.doc: Moments of a sum: the Pascal rows 1·1, 1·2·1, 1·3·3·1, 1·4·6·4·1.
proofs.statement: m1 (conv d e) = m1 d * mass e + mass d * m1 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m2_conv
proofs.statement: m2 (conv d e) = m2 d * mass e + 2 * m1 d * m1 e + mass d * m2 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m3_conv
proofs.statement: m3 (conv d e) = m3 d * mass e + 3 * m2 d * m1 e + 3 * m1 d * m2 e + mass d * m3 e

proofs.name: StatFused.m4_conv
proofs.statement: m4 (conv d e) = m4 d * mass e + 4 * m3 d * m1 e + 6 * m2 d * m2 e + 4 * m1 d * m3 e + mass d * m4 e

proofs.name: StatFused.mean_add
proofs.statement: m1 (conv d e) = m1 d + m1 e

proofs.name: StatFused.var_add
proofs.statement: k2 (conv d e) = k2 d + k2 e

proofs.name: StatFused.k3_add
proofs.statement: k3 (conv d e) = k3 d + k3 e

proofs.name: StatFused.k4_add
proofs.statement: k4 (conv d e) = k4 d + k4 e

proofs.name: StatFused.convPow_mean
proofs.statement: m1 (convPow d n) = n * m1 d

proofs.name: StatFused.convPow_k2
proofs.statement: k2 (convPow d n) = n * k2 d

proofs.name: StatFused.convPow_k3
proofs.statement: k3 (convPow d n) = n * k3 d

proofs.name: StatFused.convPow_k4
proofs.statement: k4 (convPow d n) = n * k4 d

proofs.name: StatFused.scale_m
proofs.statement: mass (scale c d) = mass d ∧ m1 (scale c d) = c * m1 d ∧ m2 (scale c d) = c*c * m2 d ∧ m3 (scale c d) = c*c*c * m3 d ∧ m4 (scale c d) = c*c*c*c * m4 d

proofs.name: StatFused.scale_k
proofs.doc: Cumulant r scales as cʳ: the reason the shape terms die after standardizing.
proofs.statement: k2 (scale c d) = c^2 * k2 d ∧ k3 (scale c d) = c^3 * k3 d ∧ k4 (scale c d) = c^4 * k4 d

proofs.name: StatFused.clt_skew
proofs.doc: **CLT, the exact part.** For a sum of n independent copies the shape numbers fall as 1/n: skewness²(Sₙ) = skewness²(X)/n and kurtosis(Sₙ) = kurtosis(X)/n. Only the mean and variance survive, which is the normal law.
proofs.statement: skewSq (convPow d n) * n = skewSq d

proofs.name: StatFused.clt_kurt
proofs.statement: kurt (convPow d n) * n = kurt d

proofs.name: StatFused.bern_stats
proofs.statement: mass (bern p) = 1 ∧ m1 (bern p) = p ∧ k2 (bern p) = p * (1 - p) ∧ k3 (bern p) = p * (1 - p) * (1 - 2 * p) ∧ k4 (bern p) = p * (1 - p) * (1 - 6 * p + 6 * p * p)

proofs.name: StatFused.bern_var_parity
proofs.doc: A coin's variance is half its self-parity: Var = ½·(p ⊞₋₂ p), the chance two copies differ, halved.

proofs.name: StatFused.binom_mean_var
proofs.doc: Binomial mean np and variance np(1 − p), from additivity alone.
proofs.statement: m1 (convPow (bern p) n) = n * p ∧ k2 (convPow (bern p) n) = n * (p * (1 - p))
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: StatFused.fair_coin_kurt
proofs.doc: Fair coins: skewness 0 and kurtosis −2/n, falling to the normal's 0.

proofs.name: StatFused.bayes_odds
proofs.doc: Bayes' rule in odds form: posterior odds = prior odds × likelihood ratio.
proofs.statement: odds (p * lH / (p * lH + (1 - p) * lN)) = odds p * (lH / lN)

proofs.name: StatFused.evidence_multAdd
proofs.doc: Two independent pieces of evidence: o·L₁·L₂ − 1 = (o − 1) ⊞ (L₁ − 1) ⊞ (L₂ − 1).

proofs.name: StatFused.repeated_evidence
proofs.doc: The same evidence n times: o·Lⁿ − 1 = (o − 1) ⊞ (L − 1)^(⊞n), the climb (rung 2).

proofs.name: StatFused.complement_is_inverse
proofs.doc: The complement is the way back: odds(1 − p) − 1 is the mult-add inverse of odds(p) − 1.

proofs.name: StatFused.pool_velocity
proofs.doc: In the coordinate ρ = 2p − 1 pooling is velocity addition, the lens law at landscape point (0, −1), walls at ±1 (certainty).

proofs.name: StatFused.pool_odds
proofs.doc: Pooling multiplies odds: the same law in the odds coordinate.
proofs.statement: odds (pool p q) = odds p * odds q

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_union_is_lens
proofs.doc: **Union under AMH dependence is a lens law** at k = −(1 + θ), q = θ: "neither happens" follows the AMH copula, so "at least one happens" is (p + q − (1 + θ)pq)/(1 − θpq).
proofs.statement: 1 - amh θ (1 - p) (1 - q) = lens (-(1 + θ)) θ p q

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_walls
proofs.doc: Its walls: 1 + k·x + q·x² = (1 − x)(1 − θx). One wall sits at certainty, x = 1; the other at 1/θ.

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_lens_multiplies
proofs.doc: The lens M(x) = (1 − x)/(1 − θx) turns the law into multiplication, so it is associative: two independent-looking "survivals" multiply in this coordinate.

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_independent
proofs.doc: θ = 0: independence, the union rule a ⊞₋₁ b.
proofs.statement: lens (-(1 + 0)) 0 a b = wAdd (-1) a b

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_velocity
proofs.doc: θ = −1: walls at ±1, velocity addition, the same law as pooling opinions.

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_cusp
proofs.doc: θ = 1: a double wall at certainty, the border parabola k² = 4q (the cusp).

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_line
proofs.doc: Every θ lands on the line k + q = −1 of the landscape plane.

proofs.name: StatFused.certainty_absorbs_iff
proofs.doc: **Why the line.** An "or" law must let certainty swallow everything: a ⊙ 1 = 1. A lens law does that exactly when k + q = −1, i.e. when it has a wall at 1.
proofs.statement: lens k q a 1 = 1 ↔ k + q = -1

proofs.name: StatFused.amh_zero
proofs.doc: The AMH copula at θ = 0 is independence: P(both) = uv.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.sumL_map_mul
proofs.statement: sumL (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * sumL ys

proofs.name: ThermoFused.outer_sum
proofs.doc: A grid's total is its edges multiplied.
proofs.statement: sumL (outer xs ys) = sumL xs * sumL ys

proofs.name: ThermoFused.partition_square
proofs.doc: Independent systems: Z_AB = Z_A · Z_B, so Z − 1 composes by mult-add.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.partition_multiplies
proofs.doc: The joint partition function of two systems is the product of theirs (the weights of joint states are products of weights).
proofs.statement: sumL (outer wA wB) = sumL wA * sumL wB

proofs.name: ThermoFused.partition_excess
proofs.doc: Put each ground state first with weight 1 (energies measured from it). Then the joint partition function is 1 + (zA ⊞ zB), where z is the sum of the excited weights: zA is "A excited, B in its ground state", zB the reverse, and the corner zA·zB is "both excited".
proofs.statement: sumL (outer (1 :: xs) (1 :: ys)) = 1 + multAdd (sumL xs) (sumL ys)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.free_energy_adds
proofs.doc: Free energy (and any log) is the linear coordinate: it adds.
proofs.statement: L (1 + multAdd zA zB) = L (1 + zA) + L (1 + zB)
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ThermoFused.third_law_identity
proofs.doc: As T → 0 every excess goes to 0, the identity, and the identity composes to the identity: a composite's entropy also goes to 0.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.residual_degeneracy
proofs.doc: Residual entropy: ground-state degeneracies compose by mult-add of g − 1.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ThermoFused.pauling_ice
proofs.doc: Pauling's ice: W = (3/2)^N, so W − 1 is the mult-add power (1/2)^(⊞N).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.landauer_states
proofs.doc: Landauer: n bits have 2^n states, 2^n − 1 = 1^(⊞n).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.cooling_step_pos
proofs.doc: One cooling step that keeps T above 0 (ratio 1 + a > 0), followed by another, still keeps T above 0.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: ThermoFused.unattainable
proofs.doc: Unattainability: any finite list of cooling steps, each short of the wall, stays short of it. T = 0 is the wall −1, and mult-add only reaches the wall if some step is already on it.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.equipartition
proofs.doc: Equipartition: n quadratic degrees of freedom are n half-steps of T. If s·s = T/T₀ then 1 + (s − 1)^(⊞2m) = (T/T₀)^m.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fermion_lift
proofs.doc: Fermion grand partition function: each mode empty or full (Pauli), so Ξ = Π(1 + zᵢ) = 1 + (z₁ ⊞ … ⊞ zₙ).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fermion_cube
proofs.doc: …and that is the sum over every corner of the cube: every many-fermion state is one corner (one subset of occupied modes).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.boson_mode
proofs.doc: A boson mode: Ξ_B = 1/(1 − z) = 1 + multAddInv(−z). The excess z/(1 − z) is the way back from a negative fermion.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.boson_fermion_dual
proofs.doc: Boson–fermion duality, one mode: Ξ_B(z) · Ξ_F(−z) = 1.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fermi_velocity_num
proofs.doc: Fermi function: with Boltzmann odds E = e^x the occupation is 1/(1 + E) and t = 1 − 2n = (E − 1)/(E + 1). Adding energies multiplies odds, and then t composes by velocity addition: numerator…

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fermi_velocity_den
proofs.doc: …and denominator: (t₁ + t₂)/(1 + t₁t₂) = (E₁E₂ − 1)/(E₁E₂ + 1).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.vel_wall_pos
proofs.doc: The two walls ±1 (n = 0 and n = 1, i.e. T = 0⁺ and T = 0⁻) absorb.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.vel_identity
proofs.doc: Infinite temperature (t = 0, n = 1/2) is the identity, not a wall.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.engine_cascade
proofs.doc: Two engines in series, the second running on the first's waste heat: total work / heat in = η₁ ⊞₋₁ η₂ (the failure-union rule).
proofs.statement: e1 * Qh + e2 * (Qh - e1 * Qh) = wAdd (-1) e1 e2 * Qh

proofs.name: ThermoFused.carnot_series
proofs.doc: Carnot: η(Th,Tc) = η(Th,Tm) ⊞₋₁ η(Tm,Tc); the lift 1 − η is Tc/Th.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.perfect_stage
proofs.doc: The k = −1 wall is the perfect engine: one perfect stage makes all perfect.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fridge_cascade
proofs.doc: Two fridges in cascade (the second pumps the first's rejected heat): work per unit of cold heat u = W/Qc composes by plain mult-add.
proofs.statement: u1 * Qc + u2 * (Qc + u1 * Qc) = multAdd u1 u2 * Qc

proofs.name: ThermoFused.reverse_is_inverse
proofs.doc: Running an engine backwards is the mult-add inverse: u = η/(1 − η) = multAddInv(−η).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.fridge_lift
proofs.doc: …so 1 + u is the reciprocal of the engine's lift 1 − η.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.carnot_fridge
proofs.doc: Carnot fridge: 1 + u = Th/Tc.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.curzon_ahlborn_half
proofs.doc: Curzon–Ahlborn (efficiency at maximum power): with s·s = Tc/Th, η_CA = 1 − s and η_C = 1 − s·s. Two CA steps make one Carnot step: η_C = η_CA ⊞₋₁ η_CA. CA is the half-step of the k = −1 climb.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.ratio_series
proofs.doc: CA engines in series also compose by ⊞₋₁ (and so do Otto cycles, whose 1 − η = r^(1−γ) multiplies with the compression ratios).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.second_law_composes
proofs.doc: The second law composes: stages below their Carnot bounds (1 − ηᵢ ≥ rᵢ, rᵢ = T_out/T_in ≥ 0) make a cascade below the overall bound 1 − r₁r₂.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.map_mul_map
proofs.statement: (ys.map (fun y => x * y)).map f = (ys.map f).map (fun y => f x * y)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.outer_map
proofs.statement: (outer xs ys).map f = outer (xs.map f) (ys.map f)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.power_sum_multiplies
proofs.doc: Power sums of independent sources multiply (f = x ↦ x^q is multiplicative).
proofs.statement: sumL ((outer xs ys).map f) = sumL (xs.map f) * sumL (ys.map f)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.tsallis_composes
proofs.doc: Tsallis pseudo-additivity: if 1 + k·S is the power sum for A, for B and for the pair (whose power sum is the product), then S_AB = S_A ⊞ₖ S_B.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.qlog_qsum
proofs.doc: The q-logarithm ln_q u = (u^k − 1)/k obeys ln_q(uv) = ln_q u ⊞ₖ ln_q v.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.renyi_adds
proofs.doc: Rényi entropy log(1 + k·S)/k adds: the log of the lift.
proofs.statement: L (1 + k * wAdd k SA SB) = L (1 + k * SA) + L (1 + k * SB)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.decimation_num
proofs.doc: Summing out the middle spin of two bonds (X = e^{2K}): the "agree" weight minus the "disagree" weight is (X₁ − 1)(X₂ − 1)…

proofs.name: ThermoFused.decimation_den
proofs.doc: …and their sum is (X₁ + 1)(X₂ + 1), so tanh K' = tanh K₁ · tanh K₂.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.ising_series
proofs.doc: In the chance p that two linked spins disagree (tanh K = 1 − 2p), bonds in series compose at k = −2, the parity weight (Matsui's piling-up rule).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.lens_num
proofs.doc: The lens turns velocity addition (bonds in parallel) into multiplication (bonds in series): polynomial form.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.lens_vel
proofs.statement: lens (vel u v) = lens u * lens v

proofs.name: ThermoFused.lens_involution
proofs.doc: Kramers–Wannier duality t ↦ e^{−2K} = M(tanh K) is an involution.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.lens_fixed_point
proofs.doc: The self-dual point (2D Ising critical point, tanh K_c = √2 − 1) is the fixed point of the lens: any t with t² + 2t − 1 = 0.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.doppler_is_lens
proofs.doc: A Doppler factor D² = (1 + β)/(1 − β) is the reciprocal of the lens, so temperature ratios of boosted blackbody light multiply as boosts add.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.stokes_wall
proofs.doc: A perfect mirror (R = 1) is the wall.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.stokes_num
proofs.doc: The lens N(R) = R/(1 − R) = 1/ε − 1: polynomial pieces…

proofs.name: ThermoFused.stokes_additive
proofs.doc: …so N turns the law into plain addition (addition in disguise).
proofs.statement: stokes a b / (1 - stokes a b) = a / (1 - a) + b / (1 - b)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.stokes_double_wall
proofs.doc: The rate 1 + k·x + q·x² at (k, q) = (−2, 1) is (1 − x)²: one double wall.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.shields
proofs.doc: n identical plates: Rₙ = nR/(1 + (n − 1)R) has N(Rₙ) = n·N(R), so n radiation shields cut the heat by 1/(n + 1), not exponentially.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.bond_infinite_T
proofs.doc: At infinite temperature (a = 1) a bond's Lee–Yang square is the plain mult-add square.
proofs.statement: 1 + 1 * x + 1 * y + x * y = 1 + multAdd x y

proofs.name: ThermoFused.bond_zero_T
proofs.doc: At zero temperature (a = 0) only the diagonal corners survive.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.two_spin_no_real_zero
proofs.doc: Two spins, ferromagnetic (0 ≤ a < 1): Z = 1 + 2az + z² has no real zero.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.chain3_multAdd
proofs.statement: chain3 a b z = 1 + multAdd a b * z + multAdd a b * (z * z) + z * z * z

proofs.name: ThermoFused.chain3_factor
proofs.doc: It factors as (1 + z)(1 + (m − 1)z + z²) with m = a ⊞ b.

proofs.name: ThermoFused.chain3_ferro_bound
proofs.doc: Ferromagnetic bonds (0 ≤ a, b ≤ 1) give 0 ≤ a ⊞ b ≤ 3, so the quadratic's discriminant (m − 1)² − 4 = (m − 3)(m + 1) ≤ 0: its zeros lie on the unit circle (the turning country), as Lee–Yang says.
proofs.statement: 0 ≤ multAdd a b ∧ multAdd a b ≤ 3

proofs.name: ThermoFused.wick_num
proofs.doc: With i·i = −1, the law at (k, q) read in units i·a is the law at (i·k, −q): numerator…
proofs.statement: i * a + i * b + k * (i * a) * (i * b) = i * (a + b + (i * k) * a * b)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.wick_den
proofs.doc: …and denominator. On the k = 0 axis thermal tanh addition (two walls) becomes quantum tan addition (a turn).

proofs.name: ThermoFused.jarzynski_composes
proofs.doc: Jarzynski: for independent processes the averages ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ multiply (weights times probabilities form a grid), so ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ − 1 mult-adds.
proofs.statement: sumL (outer xs ys) - 1 = multAdd (sumL xs - 1) (sumL ys - 1)

proofs.name: ThermoFused.hess
proofs.doc: Hess's law: coupled reactions multiply equilibrium constants.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.prime_dvd_middle
proofs.doc: **The middle of the prime cube.** For a prime p, every middle layer of the p-cube has a multiple of p corners.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.MEq.refl
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.MEq.symm
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.MEq.trans
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.MEq.zero_of_dvd
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.divmod_of_eq
proofs.doc: Reading n in base p: n = p·q + r with r < p pins down q and r.
proofs.statement: (p * q + r) / p = q ∧ (p * q + r) % p = r

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.blockCount_eq
proofs.statement: blockCount p (p * a + b) (p * c + d) = layer a c * layer b d

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.layer_zero_left
proofs.statement: layer 0 k = if k = 0 then 1 else 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.lucas_step
proofs.doc: **Lucas, one step.** C(n,k) ≡ C(n div p, k div p) · C(n mod p, k mod p).
proofs.statement: ∀ n k, MEq p (layer n k) (blockCount p n k)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.lucas
proofs.doc: **Lucas's theorem.** For n, k with at most f base-p digits, C(n,k) ≡ product over digits of C(nᵢ, kᵢ) (mod p).
proofs.statement: ∀ f n k, n < p ^ f → k < p ^ f → MEq p (layer n k) (digitProd p f n k)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.exists_prime_factor
proofs.statement: ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.aks_middle
proofs.doc: **The AKS identity on the cube.** For n ≥ 2: every middle layer of the n-cube has a multiple of n corners exactly when n is prime. (Equivalently (1 + x)ⁿ ≡ 1 + xⁿ mod n: the mult-add n-th power equals the plain n-th power, which is the identity behind the AKS test.)
proofs.statement: (∀ k, 0 < k → k < n → n ∣ layer n k) ↔ IsPrime n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_add
proofs.statement: ∀ m, bsum (fun k => f k + g k) m = bsum f m + bsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_mul
proofs.statement: ∀ m, bsum (fun k => c * f k) m = c * bsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_shift
proofs.statement: ∀ m, bsum f (m + 1) = f 0 + bsum (fun k => f (k + 1)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_congr
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → f k = g k) → bsum f m = bsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_dvd
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → d ∣ f k) → d ∣ bsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.binomial
proofs.doc: **The cube's corner count.** (1 + x)ⁿ = Σₖ C(n,k) xᵏ: a box of side 1 + x cut at 1 on every axis falls into the n-cube's corner pieces.
proofs.statement: ∀ n x, (1 + x) ^ n = cubeSum n x

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.frobenius
proofs.doc: **Mult-add powers are plain powers mod p.** (1 + x)ᵖ ≡ 1 + xᵖ: in the p-cube only the two end corners survive mod p.
proofs.statement: MEq p ((1 + x) ^ p) (1 + x ^ p)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.fermat
proofs.doc: **Fermat's little theorem.** aᵖ ≡ a (mod p) for every natural number a. Each step a → a + 1 adds one mult-add unit, and frobenius says the p-th power passes straight through it mod p.
proofs.statement: ∀ a : Nat, MEq p ((a : Int) ^ p) a

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.oneMod_oddPow
proofs.doc: Raising to an odd power keeps the level (for j ≥ 1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.oneMod_sq
proofs.doc: Squaring raises the level by one (for j ≥ 2).

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.three_pow_two_pow
proofs.doc: 3^(2^k) is one more than 2^(k+2) times an odd number, for k ≥ 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.two_adic_split
proofs.doc: Every positive n is 2^k times an odd number.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.level_three_pow
proofs.doc: The level of 3^n: 1 if n is odd, k + 2 if n = 2^k · odd with k ≥ 1.
proofs.statement: OneMod (if k = 0 then 1 else k + 2) (3 ^ (2 ^ k * (2 * t + 1)))

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.le_of_dvd_two_pow_odd
proofs.doc: If 2^n divides 2^e times an odd number, then n ≤ e.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.pow_ge
proofs.doc: 2^k ≥ k + 3 once k ≥ 3.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.only_one_two_four
proofs.doc: **Part 1.** 2^n | 3^n − 1 forces n = 1, 2 or 4 (for n ≥ 1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.one_two_four_work
proofs.doc: And the three survivors really work.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.commute_equation
proofs.doc: ψ² ψ³ = ψ³ ψ² on a gives Adams and Atiyah's equation.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.two_pow_dvd_of_mul_odd
proofs.doc: Euclid's step for powers of 2: an odd factor can be cancelled.
proofs.statement: ∀ (n : Nat) (x y : Int), IsOdd y → (2 : Int) ^ n ∣ x * y → (2 : Int) ^ n ∣ x

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.hopf_invariant_one
proofs.doc: **Part 2.** Commuting Adams operations, the mod-2 rule and an odd Hopf invariant h force n = 1, 2 or 4.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.mpow_formula
proofs.doc: (1 + x)^k − 1 = k x + C(k,2) x², written without division.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.psi_compose
proofs.doc: Mult-add powers compose: ψ^j ψ^k = ψ^(jk), for every j, k.

proofs.name: MultAdd.HopfOne.cp2_case
proofs.doc: CP² meets every hypothesis of Part 2 with n = 1, h = 1: μ₂ = C(2,2) = 1, μ₃ = C(3,2) = 3, and ψ² ψ³ = ψ³ ψ².

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.dsum_eq
proofs.statement: dsum p x = x % p + dsum p (x / p)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.val_of_mod_eq
proofs.statement: val p x = 1 + val p (x / p)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.carries_eq
proofs.statement: carries p a b c = (a % p + b % p + c) / p + carries p (a / p) (b / p) ((a % p + b % p + c) / p)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.carries_dsum
proofs.doc: Adding digit by digit: each carry turns p units of digit sum into 1.
proofs.statement: ∀ s a b c, a + b = s → c ≤ 1 → (p - 1) * carries p a b c + dsum p (a + b + c) = dsum p a + dsum p b + c

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.dsum_succ
proofs.doc: Adding 1: the digit sum goes up by 1, minus p−1 for each trailing digit p−1.
proofs.statement: ∀ x, dsum p (x + 1) + (p - 1) * val p (x + 1) = dsum p x + 1

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.val_spec
proofs.statement: ∀ x, 0 < x → Val p x (val p x)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.euclid
ambiguous: it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.layer_pos
proofs.statement: ∀ n k, k ≤ n → 0 < layer n k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.layer_val_dsum
proofs.doc: The cube count and the digit sums: (p−1)·v_p(C(j+k,k)) = s(j) + s(k) − s(j+k).
proofs.statement: ∀ k j, (p - 1) * val p (layer (j + k) k) + dsum p (j + k) = dsum p j + dsum p k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.kummer
proofs.doc: **Kummer's theorem (1852).** The exact power of p that divides C(j+k, k), the number of corners of the (j+k)-cube with k switches on, is the number of carries when you add j and k in base p.
proofs.statement: p ^ carries p j k 0 ∣ layer (j + k) k ∧ ¬ p ^ (carries p j k 0 + 1) ∣ layer (j + k) k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_add
proofs.statement: S n (fun k => f k + g k) = S n f + S n g

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_mul
proofs.statement: S n (fun k => c * f k) = c * S n f

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_sub
proofs.statement: S n (fun k => f k - g k) = S n f - S n g

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_bsum
proofs.statement: ∀ m, S n (fun k => bsum (fun i => g i k) m) = bsum (fun i => S n (g i)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_succ
proofs.doc: Pascal's rule for the signed sum: adding an axis takes a difference.
proofs.statement: S (n + 1) f = S n f - S n (fun k => f (k + 1))

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.S_pow
proofs.doc: **Inclusion–exclusion on the cube.** Σₖ (−1)ᵏ C(n,k) (c − k)ᵐ is n! when m = n and 0 when m < n. With c = n it counts the orderings of n things: corner K of the n-cube is the set of values a map is made to miss, and the signed count of maps that miss them leaves exactly the maps that miss nothing.
proofs.statement: ∀ n m, m ≤ n → ∀ c : Int, S n (fun k => (c - k) ^ m) = if m = n then (fact n : Int) else 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.bsum_meq
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → MEq p (f k) (g k)) → MEq p (bsum f m) (bsum g m)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.alt_layer
proofs.doc: Along the (p−1)-cube, the layer counts alternate ±1 mod p.
proofs.statement: ∀ k, k ≤ p - 1 → MEq p ((-1 : Int) ^ k * (layer (p - 1) k : Int)) 1

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.fermat_unit
proofs.doc: Fermat for a unit: if p does not divide a, then a^(p−1) ≡ 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.wilson
proofs.doc: **Wilson's theorem (Lagrange 1771).** (p − 1)! ≡ −1 (mod p) for every prime p. Lean's route: inclusion–exclusion on the (p−1)-cube counts the (p−1)! orderings; mod p every layer but the last adds exactly 1, so the count is p − 1 ≡ −1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.dvd_fact
proofs.doc: n! divides into every number from 1 to n.
proofs.statement: ∀ n d, 1 ≤ d → d ≤ n → d ∣ fact n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Cube.wilson_iff
proofs.doc: **Wilson's test.** For n ≥ 2, (n − 1)! ≡ −1 (mod n) exactly when n is prime.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.chart_injective
proofs.doc: Each chart is injective.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.chart_cover
proofs.doc: The three charts cover P².
proofs.statement: ∃ c v, chart c v = p

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.chart_trans
proofs.statement: chart d (trans c d v) = chart c v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.inChart_iff
proofs.doc: A point of chart c lies in chart d exactly on the transition's domain.
proofs.statement: InChart d (chart c v) ↔ Dom c d v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.trans_cocycle
proofs.doc: The cocycle condition, from injectivity: c → d → e equals c → e on the triple overlap.
proofs.statement: trans d e (trans c d v) = trans c e v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.origin_in_one_chart
proofs.doc: Each chart's origin is one of the three fixed points [0:0:1], [1:0:0], [0:1:0], and it lies in that chart only.
proofs.statement: InChart d (chart c ((0 : K), (0 : K))) ↔ d = c

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.torus_in_all
proofs.doc: Points of the torus (both coordinates nonzero) lie in all three charts.
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.trans01_multAdd
proofs.doc: In mult-add coordinates, the chart change c0 → c1, (a, b) ↦ (1/a, b/a), is (u, w) ↦ (u⁻, w ⊞ u⁻): the mult-add inverse, then a mult-add.
proofs.statement: trans c0 c1 (1 + u, 1 + w) = (1 + multAddInv u, 1 + multAdd w (multAddInv u))

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.trans02_multAdd
proofs.statement: trans c0 c2 (1 + u, 1 + w) = (1 + multAddInv w, 1 + multAdd u (multAddInv w))

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.trans_wind
proofs.doc: Windings commute with every chart change: monomial maps commute with x ↦ xⁿ.
proofs.statement: trans c d (pw n v) = pw n (trans c d v)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.P2.chart_wind
proofs.doc: So the winding is one well-defined map of P², read the same way in every chart.
proofs.statement: chart c (pw (n + 1) v) = wind (n + 1) (chart c v)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.corner_all_on
proofs.doc: The top corner (all switches on) is the torus.
proofs.statement: (∀ i, corner v i = true) ↔ ∀ i, v i ≠ 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.corner_scale
proofs.doc: Scaling by the torus (nonzero factors) never moves a point to another corner, so the corners label the torus orbits.
proofs.statement: corner (fun i => t i * v i) = corner v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.chart1_cover
proofs.doc: The two charts cover P¹.
proofs.statement: ∃ b x, chart1 b x = p

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.torus_in_both
proofs.doc: Points of the circle (nonzero, finite) lie in both charts.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.origin_in_one_chart
proofs.doc: The origin of chart c lies in chart c and in no other chart.
proofs.statement: InChart1 d (chart1 c (0 : K)) ↔ d = c

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.chart1_trans
proofs.statement: chart1 d (trans1 c d x) = chart1 c x

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.chart2_injective
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.chart2_cover
proofs.doc: The four charts cover P¹ × P¹.
proofs.statement: ∃ c v, chart2 c v = p
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.inChart2_iff
proofs.statement: InChart2 c p ↔ InChart1 c.1 p.1 ∧ InChart1 c.2 p.2

proofs.doc: Points of the torus lie in all four charts.

it is about chart or divisibility logic more than about a mult-add picture

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.fixed_point_in_one_chart
proofs.doc: Each chart's origin is one of the four fixed points, and it lies in that chart only.
proofs.statement: InChart2 d (chart2 c ((0 : K), (0 : K))) ↔ d = c

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.chart2_trans
proofs.doc: Where two charts overlap, the transition carries one chart's coordinates to the other's.
proofs.statement: chart2 d (trans2 c d v) = chart2 c v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.trans1_cocycle
proofs.doc: The cocycle condition: c → d → e equals c → e, so the gluing is consistent on every triple overlap.
proofs.statement: trans1 d e (trans1 c d x) = trans1 c e x

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.trans2_cocycle
proofs.statement: trans2 d e (trans2 c d v) = trans2 c e v

proofs.name: MultAdd.Toric.fan_count
proofs.doc: With a = q - 1 points on the circle: one torus (a²), four circles (a each), four fixed points. In ordinary coordinates it is (q + 1)².

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.star_def
proofs.statement: a ✳ b = a + b + a * b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.corner_split
proofs.doc: **The corner splits**: ū·v = (u·v) + i(u × v).
proofs.statement: C.mul (C.conj u) v = ⟨dot u v, cross u v⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.corner_swap
proofs.doc: The other order is the conjugate: v̄·u = conj(ū·v).
proofs.statement: C.mul (C.conj v) u = C.conj (C.mul (C.conj u) v)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.cross_anti
proofs.statement: cross v u = - cross u v

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.dot_symm
proofs.statement: dot v u = dot u v

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.cross_is_area
proofs.statement: cross u v = area2 ⟨0, 0⟩ u v

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.cross_collinear
proofs.doc: Collinear speeds (both on the real axis) have no cross part.

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.boost_real
proofs.doc: At q = −1 on the real axis it is the relativity page's [[1, u], [u, 1]].

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.boost_mul
proofs.doc: **Two boosts**: B(u)·B(v) = [[X + iY, u + v], [−q·(ū + v̄), X − iY]].
proofs.statement: M.mul (boost q u) (boost q v) = ⟨⟨tX q u v, tY q u v⟩, C.add u v, C.smul (-q) (C.conj (C.add u v)), ⟨tX q u v, - tY q u v⟩⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.entry_tl
proofs.doc: The top-left entry is 1 − q·u·v̄ and the bottom-right is 1 − q·ū·v.
proofs.statement: C.add C.one (C.smul (-q) (C.mul u (C.conj v))) = ⟨tX q u v, tY q u v⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.entry_br
proofs.statement: C.add C.one (C.smul (-q) (C.mul (C.conj u) v)) = ⟨tX q u v, - tY q u v⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.diag_conj
proofs.doc: The diagonal entries are conjugates.
proofs.statement: (M.mul (boost q u) (boost q v)).a = C.conj (M.mul (boost q u) (boost q v)).d
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.boost_mul_real
proofs.doc: In one dimension at q = −1 this is the relativity page's (1 + uv)·B(u ⊕ v).

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_trivial_iff
proofs.doc: **No twist exactly when the cross part is switched off**: X + iY = X − iY ⇔ q·(u × v) = 0.
proofs.statement: (⟨tX q u v, tY q u v⟩ : C) = ⟨tX q u v, - tY q u v⟩ ↔ q * cross u v = 0

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.collinear_no_twist
proofs.doc: Collinear boosts never twist.

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.galilean_no_twist
proofs.doc: The Galilean dial q = 0 never twists, in any directions.
proofs.statement: tY 0 u v = 0 ∧ tX 0 u v = 1

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_on_circle
proofs.doc: It lies on the unit circle.
proofs.statement: cosT q u v * cosT q u v + sinT q u v * sinT q u v = 1

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_turns
proofs.doc: The twist turns X − iY into X + iY: e^{iω}·(X − iY) = X + iY.
proofs.statement: C.mul ⟨cosT q u v, sinT q u v⟩ ⟨tX q u v, - tY q u v⟩ = ⟨tX q u v, tY q u v⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_half_angle
proofs.doc: **The half-angle of the twist**: tan(ω/2) = sin ω/(1 + cos ω) = Y/X = q(u × v)/(1 − q(u·v)).
proofs.statement: sinT q u v / (1 + cosT q u v) = tY q u v / tX q u v

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.den_swap
proofs.statement: den q v u = C.conj (den q u v)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_eq
proofs.doc: The twist is exactly the unit-circle point (cos ω, sin ω) of section 3.
proofs.statement: twist q u v = ⟨cosT q u v, sinT q u v⟩

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.order_swap
proofs.doc: **Order swap**: u ⊕ v = twist(u, v) · (v ⊕ u).
proofs.statement: oplus q u v = C.mul (twist q u v) (oplus q v u)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.boost_shape
proofs.doc: Boosts have the shape.
proofs.statement: boost q u = shape q C.one u
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.shape_mul
proofs.doc: **The shape is closed under products**: one group for each q (q = −1 the Lorentz spin group SU(1,1), q = 0 the Galilean one, q = +1 SU(2)).
proofs.statement: M.mul (shape q α β) (shape q γ δ) = shape q (C.add (C.mul α γ) (C.smul (-q) (C.mul β (C.conj δ)))) (C.add (C.mul α δ) (C.mul β (C.conj γ)))

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.sdet_mul
proofs.doc: **The determinant multiplies** (a two-square identity for each q).
proofs.statement: sdet q (C.add (C.mul α γ) (C.smul (-q) (C.mul β (C.conj δ)))) (C.add (C.mul α δ) (C.mul β (C.conj γ))) = sdet q α β * sdet q γ δ

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.boost_det
proofs.doc: For two boosts: |1 − q·ū·v|² + q·|u + v|² = (1 + q|u|²)(1 + q|v|²).
proofs.statement: C.nsq (den q u v) + q * C.nsq (C.add u v) = (1 + q * C.nsq u) * (1 + q * C.nsq v)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.light_wall_2d
proofs.doc: **The light wall in two dimensions** (q = −1): |1 + ū·v|² − |u + v|² = (1 − |u|²)(1 − |v|²).
proofs.statement: C.nsq (den (-1) u v) - C.nsq (C.add u v) = (1 - C.nsq u) * (1 - C.nsq v)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.under_light_2d
proofs.doc: **Below light stays below light, in any directions**: |u|, |v| < 1 ⇒ |u + v| < |1 + ū·v|, so |u ⊕ v| < 1.
proofs.statement: C.nsq (C.add u v) < C.nsq (den (-1) u v)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.sphere_no_wall
proofs.doc: At the sphere end q = +1 there is no wall: the determinant of a boost is ≥ 1.

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.half_kick
proofs.doc: The half-velocity t composed with itself gives the velocity: t ⊕ t = 2t/(1 + t²).
proofs.statement: vel t t = 2 * t / (1 + t * t)

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.half_kick_ruler
proofs.doc: On the mult-add ruler, the velocity is the half-velocity mult-added to itself: d(t ⊕ t) = d(t) ✳ d(t). The half-velocity is half a kick.
proofs.statement: dop (vel t t) = dop t ✳ dop t
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: TwistedBoosts.twist_from_corner
proofs.doc: The twist's tangent, written with the mult-add corner: Y/X = q(u × v)/(1 − q(u·v)), and both parts come from the one corner ū·v.
proofs.statement: tX q u v = 1 - q * (C.mul (C.conj u) v).re ∧ tY q u v = q * (C.mul (C.conj u) v).im
